# The Agent's Data Tools, the Screen's Safety, the Orchestrator, the App and the Fixtures (Plan 5B) Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Build the Android half of Kestrel's agent (sub-project 5) that plan 5A's plain core needs: the module `:core:datatools` with the data tools and the notification listener, the screen's safety changes in `:core:screen` (Kestrel's own actions and the owner's finger, the press policy, the checked typing, the links and intents, the confirmation card's arming delay and refusal of actions, the tooltip and scroll-axis reads, Firefox), the activity log for prompts, the Orchestrator's task phases, questions, pause and "Kestrel, continue", `:app`'s `AgentRunner` and the ports, the permission flow, the Safety and Memory pages, `:testapp`'s fixtures, the debug hooks, the device tests and `scripts\task-check.ps1`, all checked on kestrel-api37 with the scripted model.

**Architecture:** `:core:datatools` implements plan 5A's `DataPort` (`AndroidDataPort`) with Android's providers and intents, and holds the contacts that `:app`'s instant commands also read (design D1, D9, D12). `:core:screen` gets the rules that keep the agent's actions safe on a real screen (D19, D32 items 12, 20 to 29). `:app` connects plan 5A's `Agent` to the Orchestrator, the screen, the owner, the models, the memory and the log through its ports (D2, D14, D15, D24 to D26), and its debug build gets the hooks through which scripts give tasks as text and check their results on the device (D27 to D29). Plan 5C adds looking closer and the sittings below its own anchors.

**Tech Stack:** Kotlin 2.4.21, kotlinx.coroutines 1.11.0, kotlinx.serialization 1.13.0, Android SDK 37 (`minSdk 33`), Jetpack Compose for the settings pages, JUnit 4, AndroidX Test (runner 1.7.0, ext-junit 1.3.0), PowerShell 7.3 and Pester 6.2.0 for the scripts.

## Global Constraints

- Package and application ID `dev.kestrel`; licence GPL-3.0-or-later. One new dependency ships in the release app: `com.microsoft.onnxruntime:onnxruntime-android:1.28.0` (MIT) as an `implementation` of `:core:perception`, pinned by the audit and by Gradle's verification metadata (plan 5C). Nothing else new ships; `java-test-fixtures` adds no dependency, and the test fixtures use only Kotlin, coroutines and kotlinx.serialization, because the audit checks the debug runtime classpath (review C M13). No Python, Pillow, piexif or exiftool in any script.
- `minSdk 33`, `targetSdk 37`, `compileSdk 37`. Every call that the A71 (API 33) lacks (`takeScreenshotOfWindow`, `READ_MEDIA_VISUAL_USER_SELECTED`, `getTooltipText` is API 28 and fine) has a check of the API level.
- No dependency-injection framework; `AppGraph` wires by hand. `:core:agent` and `:core:safety` stay plain Kotlin. Every new coroutine scope (the task runner, the agent's loop, the memory and routine stores, the notification listener, the OCR engine) reports its failures through `graph.errors`, by class only (D32 item 48).
- All network traffic goes through `NetworkGateway`; no new module names a type or calls a method that the audit flags, `audit/rules.txt` gets no new network exception, and `Geocoder`, the network and fused location providers and Google's location client are never used.
- No request to any provider's API outside the owner's second sitting (D30): not in a plan's step, a test or a script; every agent test uses the scripted model, and a task given through H1 refuses to run without it unless a live sitting is open (D28).
- Every device check is automated (the owner's rule of 2026-11-20): a script gives each task or command as text through a debug hook and checks the result on the device; speech is checked with generated clips through the PC's speakers; the owner is asked only for sign-ins and links, one real touch and answers only he can give, in one short step at the start of a sitting (D30); the scripts unlock the A71 with the test PIN through plan 4D's unlock function (Q6; review C3 nit 1). Checks match a result to the task number of the text that they sent, never to the newest task. The OCR files and the Python reference are fetched once by plan 5C's writer from ModelScope, Hugging Face and GitHub, which are not providers' APIs.
- Never log, print or put into a test's output the owner's words, screen text, a notification, an SMS, an e-mail, a contact, a prompt, a reply, a tool's arguments, a screenshot, a vault value, the A71's PIN, a token or a key; `toString` of anything that carries them prints only kinds, counts or lengths (D25). Failures are logged by their classes and stack frames only. Screenshots stay in memory.
- Device tests never touch the owner's contacts, calendar, messages, photos, profiles or spending; they use test-only data and remove it, also after a failure.
- Test only on kestrel-api37 (check `adb -s <serial> emu avd name` in the same command as each device command); never on the S23+ or the AVD `zoran`; the A71 only in the two sittings (D30). The main session owns `.superpowers/sdd/emulator.lock` (process rule 9); subagents never create, wait for or delete it. Only one Gradle build at a time. Gradle only through `scripts\gradle.ps1`, stopped with `--stop` at the end of each task; device tests only through `scripts\connected-test.ps1` (with `-Pandroid.injected.androidTest.leaveApksInstalledAfterRun=true`) or the scripts that a plan names; installs only through `scripts\install.ps1`.
- No device test, script or session step ever places a call to an emergency number or answers "yes, call" (process rule 10); test mode blocks every agent call, and the agent hands every call over in every mode (D13). The fixtures use only fictional addresses and the fictional number of D28.
- Scripts run on Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7, or declare `#Requires -Version 7.3` as `hook.ps1` does; `scripts\test-scripts.ps1` passes after every script change.
- The repository uses LF line endings.
- The plan files are named with the day they are written: this plan is `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-22-agent-5b-datatools-app.md`; plan 5C is `2026-11-22-agent-5c-perception-session.md`. A plan is frozen once committed; a later difference goes into `.superpowers/sdd/progress.md`.

D-numbers refer to the design `.superpowers/sdd/plan-5-design.md`. Code comments call it "design D… of sub-project 5", as plan 5A's code does. The interfaces between this plan's tasks, and the names of this plan that plan 5C uses, are in `.superpowers/sdd/plan-5b-interfaces.md`.

## Before you start

- The code is `origin/main` after plan 5A and its final fix round (the starting commit is in each task's brief). The counts at the start of this plan: `:app` JVM tests A₀ = 488 (with the debug-only JVM tests of `app/src/testDebug`, which `:app:testDebugUnitTest` runs too), `:core:commands` 157, `:core:providers` 456, `:core:safety` F₀, `:core:screen` 70, `:core:screen-model` 22, `:core:agent` G₀ (plan 5A's final fix round sets F₀ and G₀; the controller gives them), `:core:datatools` 0, Pester 282 in each shell; `:app`'s device tests by package: voice 96, commands 108, screen 64, settings 50, debug 14, providers 20, the root package 15. Each task gives its counts as "N + k", where N is the count before the task; before each task, compare the counts with the ones that the earlier tasks left. If a count differs, stop and ask the controller.
- Before each task, check that every text that the task replaces exists, and exists once, in its file. If a text is missing, stop and ask the controller.
- Before each task, run `git status --short`. If a file that the task changes (its **Files** list) already shows changes that are not the task's own, stop and ask the controller, because the task's `git add` would commit them too.
- Run Gradle only through `scripts\gradle.ps1`, and stop it with `scripts\gradle.ps1 --stop` at the end of each task. Only one Gradle build may run on this computer at a time (process rule 8b); if another agent's build runs, wait for it to end.
- The device steps use kestrel-api37. The controller holds the emulator's lock for each task that uses it (process rule 9) and says so in the task's brief; never create, wait for or delete `.superpowers\sdd\emulator.lock` yourself. If the brief does not say that the controller holds the lock, ask the controller before the device steps. Every device command starts with a check of the emulator, in the same command: `. scripts\lib\Kestrel.ps1; Use-KestrelToolchain; if ("$(& (Get-Adb) -s emulator-5554 emu avd name)" -notmatch '^kestrel-api37\b') { throw 'emulator-5554 is not kestrel-api37' };` and then the command itself. If the check throws, or no emulator runs, start the emulator with `scripts\start-emulator.ps1`, check that the serial that it prints belongs to `kestrel-api37`, and use that serial in place of `emulator-5554`. Never send a command to a connected phone. No task of this plan uses the A71.
- No step of this plan calls a provider's API: every agent test and every dry run uses the scripted model.
- Every commit message ends with the line `Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>`.

## Changes to the design that this plan makes

- The design's `web.BrowserIntents` and `settings.SettingsPages` are not created: plan 5A built the browsers and the settings pages as `tools.Browser` and `tools.SettingsPage` in `:core:agent`, and its `ScreenSteps` sends them as `IntentSpec`s through `ScreenPort`; `:core:datatools`' `IntentSpecs` turns an `IntentSpec` into an Android `Intent` and resolves it, for `AppScreenPort` (Task 4).
- `AndroidDataPort` is created in Task 5, once every tool exists; Tasks 1 to 4 build the tools as classes of their own (`contacts.FindContact`, `media.MediaTool`, `calendar.CalendarTool`, `clock.ClockIntents`, `sms.SmsTool`, `calls.CallLogTool`, `media.MediaKeys`, `location.GpsLocation`, `navigation.NavigationIntents`), each tested on its own.
- `DataToolsTest` also checks the intents that the tools build (share, alarm, timer, SMS, calendar insert, `IntentSpecs`) without starting them, because a JVM test cannot build a real `Intent`.
- D19's probe is `OwnActionsTest.probeRecordsWhatKestrelsActionsLookLikeToTheWatcher` in `app/src/androidTest`. Its record goes to logcat with the tag `KestrelProbe` (numbers only), and on API 34 and later it fails when a kind of node action other than a click or long click, or a refused click, reaches the watcher, or when an echo comes later than half of a credit's life (400 ms); the credits are created only for clicks and long clicks (`OwnActions.ECHOING`), the kinds that the probe expects to echo on Android 17 (plan 3C's evidence: a click arrives at once as a touch from device 0). The fixture with a list that scrolls by itself is not built: `OwnerSignalTest` checks on the JVM that `TYPE_VIEW_SCROLLED` never counts.
- `ActionResult.CARD_OPEN` is the result of every gesture and node action while the confirmation card shows (D32 item 20); global actions, magnification and intents are not refused, because the agent's loop is sequential and D2 lets no instant command run during a confirmation.
- `ScreenSession.touches` reports every touch that the watcher classified, with its device, source, tool type, flags and the time since Kestrel's last node action, for the probe and for the activity log's "possible late echo" (D19).
- `BoostWordSource` gets the owner's names (D32 item 44) through a `PeopleNames` reader, `OwnerNames`, which Task 1 builds with the starred contacts and Task 14 completes with memory's aliases and the contacts that tasks found.

## Threads

| Call | Thread | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `AndroidDataPort`'s tools | the agent's coroutine | each provider query switches to `Dispatchers.IO`; the intents go through `ScreenActions.openIntent` |
| `KestrelNotificationListener` | Android's main thread for its callbacks; `getActiveNotifications` from `Dispatchers.IO` | no coroutine scope of its own |
| `OwnActions` | any thread | every method locks; `ScreenActions` calls it on `Dispatchers.IO`, the touch watcher on the main thread |
| `ScreenActions` | `Dispatchers.IO` (the callers' rule, as today) | the card check reads a volatile flag |
| `ConfirmationCard`, `TouchWatcher` | the main thread | as today |

Design D1, D12; deferred items 43 and 44 (D32). `ContactsReader`, `ContactsAccess` and the query move unchanged in behaviour from `:app` into `:core:datatools`' package `dev.kestrel.datatools.contacts` and become public, so that the instant commands and the agent's `find_contact` read the contacts through one module (spec 7.4). `find_contact` reads Android's `ContactsContract.Data` by mimetype in one query, never with SQL `LIKE` (r53): names, nicknames, phones, e-mail addresses and the messaging apps' rows (Telegram, WhatsApp, Viber, Signal; Viber Out's rows do not count). A Telegram row on a contact of its own (Telegram writes it on its own raw contact, which Android joins by name, and may fail to join for a Serbian name) joins the contact that `ContactMatcher` finds by its name. The result names up to four contacts with their apps, or says "no app link found; the contact may still use an app", because a missing row proves nothing. `:core:commands`' `Contact` stays as it is; the extra data lives in `ContactDetails`. Create `core/datatools/src/main/kotlin/dev/kestrel/datatools/contacts/ContactsAccess.kt`:

```kotlin
package dev.kestrel.datatools.contacts

import android.Manifest
import android.content.Context
import android.content.pm.PackageManager

/**
 * Whether Kestrel may read the contacts (`READ_CONTACTS`, design spec, section 13.6). An interface, so that the JVM tests
 * can check the first use without the permission.
 */
fun interface ContactsAccess {
    fun allowed(): Boolean
}

/** Kestrel's own permission to read the contacts, which the owner gives at the first "call [name]" or `find_contact`. */
fun contactsAccess(context: Context) = ContactsAccess {
    context.checkSelfPermission(Manifest.permission.READ_CONTACTS) == PackageManager.PERMISSION_GRANTED
}
```

Create `core/datatools/src/main/kotlin/dev/kestrel/datatools/contacts/ContactsReader.kt`:

```kotlin
package dev.kestrel.datatools.contacts

import android.content.ContentResolver
import android.database.ContentObserver
import android.os.Handler
import android.os.Looper
import android.provider.ContactsContract
import android.provider.ContactsContract.CommonDataKinds.Email
import android.provider.ContactsContract.CommonDataKinds.Nickname
import android.provider.ContactsContract.CommonDataKinds.Phone
import android.provider.ContactsContract.CommonDataKinds.StructuredName
import android.provider.ContactsContract.Data
import dev.kestrel.commands.phone.Contact

/** Where the contacts come from: Android's contacts provider, or a fake in the JVM tests. */
interface ContactsSource {
    /** Every contact with its names and numbers. Throws [SecurityException] without `READ_CONTACTS`. */
    fun read(): List<Contact>

    /** Calls [changed] after each change of the contacts until the returned handle closes. Throws without the permission. */
    fun watch(changed: () -> Unit): AutoCloseable
}

/**
 * The owner's contacts for "call [name]" (design spec, section 13.6; research r20), kept in memory. Nothing touches the
 * provider until the first read that finds `READ_CONTACTS` granted; that read registers the watch for changes only after
 * it has read, because Android refuses the registration without the permission. After a change, the next read reads
 * again. When the permission is missing at a read, the reader drops what it kept and its watch, so that a later grant
 * starts afresh. It never logs a name or a number; a failure is reported by its classes only.
 */
class ContactsReader(
    private val access: ContactsAccess,
    private val source: ContactsSource,
    private val report: (String, Throwable) -> Unit,
) {
    private var kept: List<Contact>? = null
    private var watch: AutoCloseable? = null

    @Volatile
    private var changed = false

    /** The contacts, or null without the permission. */
    @Synchronized
    fun contacts(): List<Contact>? {
        if (!access.allowed()) {
            drop()
            return null
        }
        // Kept only while a watch tells of changes; after a refused watch, every read reads again.
        kept?.let { if (!changed && watch != null) return it }
        // Cleared before the read, so that a change during the read leads to another read next time.
        changed = false
        val contacts = try {
            source.read()
        } catch (e: SecurityException) {
            drop()
            return null
        }
        kept = contacts
        if (watch == null) {
            watch = try {
                source.watch { changed = true }
            } catch (e: SecurityException) {
                report("Watching the contacts", e)
                null
            }
        }
        return contacts
    }

    private fun drop() {
        kept = null
        changed = false
        watch?.close()
        watch = null
    }
}

/**
 * The contacts of Android's provider, read by mimetype in one query, never with SQL `LIKE` (research r53): for the instant
 * commands names, nicknames and phone numbers; for the agent's `find_contact` also the e-mail addresses and the messaging
 * apps' rows (design D12 of sub-project 5). Call it off the main thread.
 */
class AndroidContacts(private val resolver: ContentResolver) : ContactsSource {
    override fun read(): List<Contact> = ContactRows.fold(rows(BASIC)).map { it.contact }

    /** Every contact with its e-mail addresses and the messaging apps whose rows it has. Throws without `READ_CONTACTS`. */
    fun details(): List<ContactDetails> = ContactRows.fold(rows(BASIC + Email.CONTENT_ITEM_TYPE + MessagingApps.MIMETYPES.keys))

    override fun watch(changed: () -> Unit): AutoCloseable {
        val observer = object : ContentObserver(Handler(Looper.getMainLooper())) {
            override fun onChange(selfChange: Boolean) = changed()
        }
        resolver.registerContentObserver(ContactsContract.Contacts.CONTENT_URI, true, observer)
        return AutoCloseable { resolver.unregisterContentObserver(observer) }
    }

    private fun rows(kinds: List<String>): List<ContactRow> {
        val rows = mutableListOf<ContactRow>()
        val selection = "${Data.MIMETYPE} IN (${kinds.joinToString(", ") { "?" }})"
        resolver.query(Data.CONTENT_URI, COLUMNS, selection, kinds.toTypedArray(), Data._ID)?.use { cursor ->
            while (cursor.moveToNext()) {
                val mimetype = cursor.getString(2)
                rows += ContactRow(
                    contactId = cursor.getLong(0),
                    displayName = cursor.getString(1),
                    mimetype = mimetype,
                    value = cursor.getString(3),
                    // Only a phone row keeps a number in DATA2; the apps' rows keep text there.
                    type = if (mimetype == Phone.CONTENT_ITEM_TYPE) cursor.getInt(4) else 0,
                    label = if (mimetype == Phone.CONTENT_ITEM_TYPE) cursor.getString(5) else null,
                    starred = cursor.getInt(6) != 0,
                    superPrimary = cursor.getInt(7) != 0,
                )
            }
        }
        return rows
    }

    private companion object {
        val BASIC = listOf(StructuredName.CONTENT_ITEM_TYPE, Nickname.CONTENT_ITEM_TYPE, Phone.CONTENT_ITEM_TYPE)

        // The display name of the contact, the row's kind and value, a phone number's type and label, the star and
        // whether the number is the contact's default.
        val COLUMNS = arrayOf(
            Data.CONTACT_ID, Data.DISPLAY_NAME, Data.MIMETYPE, Data.DATA1, Data.DATA2, Data.DATA3, Data.STARRED, Data.IS_SUPER_PRIMARY,
        )
    }
}
```

```kotlin
package dev.kestrel.datatools.contacts

import dev.kestrel.commands.phone.Contact
import dev.kestrel.commands.phone.PhoneEntry
import org.junit.Assert.assertEquals
import org.junit.Assert.assertNull
import org.junit.Test

class ContactsReaderTest {
    private val ana = Contact(1, listOf("Ana Petrović"), listOf(PhoneEntry("064 123 4567", "mobile", superPrimary = false)), starred = false)

    /** The provider as the tests see it: what it was asked, in order. */
    private class Provider(var contacts: List<Contact>) : ContactsSource {
        val calls = mutableListOf<String>()
        var refuseWatch = false
        var changed: (() -> Unit)? = null

        override fun read(): List<Contact> {
            calls += "read"
            return contacts
        }

        override fun watch(changed: () -> Unit): AutoCloseable {
            calls += "watch"
            if (refuseWatch) throw SecurityException("Permission Denial: Ana Petrović")
            this.changed = changed
            return AutoCloseable { calls += "unwatch" }
        }
    }

    private var allowed = true
    private val reports = mutableListOf<String>()
    private val provider = Provider(listOf(ana))
    private val reader = ContactsReader({ allowed }, provider) { what, error -> reports += "$what: ${error.javaClass.simpleName}" }

    @Test
    fun nothingIsReadOrWatchedBeforeTheFirstReadWithThePermission() {
        allowed = false

        assertNull(reader.contacts())
        assertEquals(emptyList<String>(), provider.calls)

        allowed = true
        assertEquals(listOf(ana), reader.contacts())
        // The watch comes after the read, because Android refuses it without the permission.
        assertEquals(listOf("read", "watch"), provider.calls)
    }

    @Test
    fun theContactsAreKeptUntilTheyChange() {
        reader.contacts()
        reader.contacts()
        assertEquals(listOf("read", "watch"), provider.calls)

        val marko = ana.copy(id = 2, names = listOf("Marko"))
        provider.contacts = listOf(ana, marko)
        checkNotNull(provider.changed).invoke()

        assertEquals(listOf(ana, marko), reader.contacts())
        assertEquals(listOf("read", "watch", "read"), provider.calls)
    }

    @Test
    fun aLostPermissionDropsTheContactsAndTheWatchAndAGrantStartsAfresh() {
        reader.contacts()
        allowed = false

        assertNull(reader.contacts())
        assertEquals(listOf("read", "watch", "unwatch"), provider.calls)

        allowed = true
        reader.contacts()
        assertEquals(listOf("read", "watch", "unwatch", "read", "watch"), provider.calls)
    }

    @Test
    fun aRefusedWatchIsReportedByItsClassAndTheContactsStillCome() {
        provider.refuseWatch = true

        assertEquals(listOf(ana), reader.contacts())
        assertEquals(listOf("Watching the contacts: SecurityException"), reports)
        // Without a watch, nothing tells the reader of a change, so it reads again and tries the watch again.
        assertEquals(listOf(ana), reader.contacts())
        assertEquals(listOf("read", "watch", "read", "watch"), provider.calls)
    }
}
```

```kotlin
package dev.kestrel.datatools

import android.Manifest
import android.content.ContentProviderOperation
import android.content.ContentResolver
import android.content.Context
import android.os.SystemClock
import android.provider.ContactsContract
import android.provider.ContactsContract.CommonDataKinds.Email
import android.provider.ContactsContract.CommonDataKinds.Phone
import android.provider.ContactsContract.CommonDataKinds.StructuredName
import android.provider.ContactsContract.Data
import android.provider.ContactsContract.RawContacts
import androidx.test.ext.junit.runners.AndroidJUnit4
import androidx.test.platform.app.InstrumentationRegistry
import dev.kestrel.agent.port.DataResult
import dev.kestrel.datatools.contacts.AndroidContacts
import dev.kestrel.datatools.contacts.FindContact
import org.junit.After
import org.junit.Assert.assertEquals
import org.junit.Before
import org.junit.Test
import org.junit.runner.RunWith

/**
 * The data tools against Android's own providers on kestrel-api37 (design D12 and D27 of sub-project 5): each case adds
 * its own test data under this test package and removes it again, also after a failure, and never reads anything else.
 * The intents are built and checked, never started.
 */
@RunWith(AndroidJUnit4::class)
class DataToolsTest {
    private val instrumentation = InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation()

    // A library's device tests run in their own test package, which is also the target here.
    private val context: Context = instrumentation.targetContext
    private val resolver: ContentResolver = context.contentResolver

    @Before
    fun grant() {
        for (permission in PERMISSIONS) instrumentation.uiAutomation.grantRuntimePermission(context.packageName, permission)
        removeTestData()
    }

    @After
    fun cleanUp() = removeTestData()

    @Test
    fun findContactGivesTheTestContactsNumberAddressAndMessagingApps() {
        addTestContact("Zora Testić", phone = NUMBER, email = "zora@example.com", appMimetype = TELEGRAM)

        val line = waitFor { (FindContact.result("Zora Testić", AndroidContacts(resolver).details()) as DataResult.Ok).lines.singleOrNull() }

        assertEquals("contact 1 (apps: Telegram)", line.fixed)
        assertEquals(listOf("name", "phone", "e-mail"), line.fields.map { it.name })
        assertEquals("$NUMBER (mobile)", line.fields[1].value)
    }

    /** Adds a contact of the test account with a name and, when given, a mobile number, an address and an app's row. */
    private fun addTestContact(name: String, phone: String? = null, email: String? = null, appMimetype: String? = null) {
        val operations = arrayListOf(
            ContentProviderOperation.newInsert(RawContacts.CONTENT_URI)
                .withValue(RawContacts.ACCOUNT_TYPE, TEST_ACCOUNT_TYPE)
                .withValue(RawContacts.ACCOUNT_NAME, TEST_ACCOUNT)
                .build(),
            data(StructuredName.CONTENT_ITEM_TYPE, StructuredName.DISPLAY_NAME, name),
        )
        phone?.let { operations += data(Phone.CONTENT_ITEM_TYPE, Phone.NUMBER, it, Phone.TYPE to Phone.TYPE_MOBILE) }
        email?.let { operations += data(Email.CONTENT_ITEM_TYPE, Email.ADDRESS, it) }
        appMimetype?.let { operations += data(it, Data.DATA1, "1000001") }
        resolver.applyBatch(ContactsContract.AUTHORITY, operations)
    }

    private fun data(mimetype: String, column: String, value: String, type: Pair<String, Int>? = null): ContentProviderOperation =
        ContentProviderOperation.newInsert(Data.CONTENT_URI)
            .withValueBackReference(Data.RAW_CONTACT_ID, 0)
            .withValue(Data.MIMETYPE, mimetype)
            .withValue(column, value)
            .apply { type?.let { withValue(it.first, it.second) } }
            .build()

    /** Removes everything that the cases add: the contacts of the test account. */
    private fun removeTestData() {
        val rawContacts = RawContacts.CONTENT_URI.buildUpon().appendQueryParameter(ContactsContract.CALLER_IS_SYNCADAPTER, "true").build()
        resolver.delete(rawContacts, "${RawContacts.ACCOUNT_NAME} = ? AND ${RawContacts.ACCOUNT_TYPE} = ?", arrayOf(TEST_ACCOUNT, TEST_ACCOUNT_TYPE))
    }

    /** The provider joins a new raw contact into a contact shortly after the insert, so the cases wait up to 5 s for it. */
    private fun <T : Any> waitFor(read: () -> T?): T {
        val deadline = SystemClock.uptimeMillis() + 5_000
        while (true) {
            read()?.let { return it }
            check(SystemClock.uptimeMillis() < deadline) { "The test data did not appear within 5 s" }
            Thread.sleep(100)
        }
    }

    private companion object {
        val PERMISSIONS = listOf(Manifest.permission.READ_CONTACTS, Manifest.permission.WRITE_CONTACTS)

        // The account of the instant commands' test contacts (PhoneTests), which command-test.ps1 also deletes.
        const val TEST_ACCOUNT = "kestrel-test"
        const val TEST_ACCOUNT_TYPE = "dev.kestrel.test"

        // The fictional number of design D28.
        const val NUMBER = "+1 202 555 0143"
        const val TELEGRAM = "vnd.android.cursor.item/vnd.org.telegram.messenger.android.profile"
    }
}
```

Create `core/datatools/src/main/kotlin/dev/kestrel/datatools/contacts/ContactDetails.kt`:

```kotlin
package dev.kestrel.datatools.contacts

import android.provider.ContactsContract.CommonDataKinds.Email
import android.provider.ContactsContract.CommonDataKinds.Nickname
import android.provider.ContactsContract.CommonDataKinds.Phone
import dev.kestrel.commands.phone.Contact
import dev.kestrel.commands.phone.ContactMatch
import dev.kestrel.commands.phone.ContactMatcher
import dev.kestrel.commands.phone.PhoneEntry

/**
 * A contact as the agent's `find_contact` sees it (design D12 of sub-project 5): the instant commands' [contact] with its
 * names and numbers, its e-mail addresses, and the messaging [apps] (names of [MessagingApps]) whose rows it has. Its text
 * form shows only counts (spec 13.5).
 */
data class ContactDetails(val contact: Contact, val emails: List<String>, val apps: Set<String>) {
    override fun toString() = "ContactDetails(${contact.names.size} names, ${contact.numbers.size} numbers, ${emails.size} addresses, ${apps.size} apps)"
}

/**
 * The rows by which messaging apps mark a contact that uses them in Android's contacts (research r53): Telegram's and
 * Signal's from their source code, WhatsApp's and Viber's from other apps' parsers. Viber Out's rows are paid calls to
 * ordinary numbers and prove nothing, so they are not here. A missing row proves nothing either.
 */
object MessagingApps {
    const val TELEGRAM = "Telegram"
    const val WHATSAPP = "WhatsApp"
    const val VIBER = "Viber"
    const val SIGNAL = "Signal"

    /** Each app's row by its mimetype, in the order in which a result names the apps. */
    val MIMETYPES: Map<String, String> = linkedMapOf(
        "vnd.android.cursor.item/vnd.org.telegram.messenger.android.profile" to TELEGRAM,
        "vnd.android.cursor.item/vnd.com.whatsapp.profile" to WHATSAPP,
        "vnd.android.cursor.item/vnd.com.viber.voip.viber_number_message" to VIBER,
        "vnd.android.cursor.item/vnd.org.thoughtcrime.securesms.contact" to SIGNAL,
    )

    fun appOf(mimetype: String?): String? = MIMETYPES[mimetype]

    /** [apps] in the order of [MIMETYPES]. */
    fun ordered(apps: Set<String>): List<String> = MIMETYPES.values.filter { it in apps }
}

/** One row of Android's `ContactsContract.Data` as [AndroidContacts] reads it. It is never logged. */
internal class ContactRow(
    val contactId: Long,
    val displayName: String?,
    val mimetype: String?,
    val value: String?,
    val type: Int,
    val label: String?,
    val starred: Boolean,
    val superPrimary: Boolean,
)

/** Turns the provider's rows into contacts (design D12 of sub-project 5). Pure, for the JVM tests. */
internal object ContactRows {
    private class Building {
        val names = mutableListOf<String>()
        val numbers = mutableListOf<PhoneEntry>()
        val emails = mutableListOf<String>()
        val apps = mutableSetOf<String>()
        var starred = false
    }

    /**
     * One contact per contact ID, in the order of the rows: the display name first, then the nicknames, the phone numbers
     * with their kinds, the e-mail addresses and the apps whose rows it has. A contact without a name is left out.
     */
    fun fold(rows: List<ContactRow>): List<ContactDetails> {
        val built = LinkedHashMap<Long, Building>()
        for (row in rows) {
            val contact = built.getOrPut(row.contactId) { Building() }
            row.displayName?.let { if (it !in contact.names) contact.names.add(0, it) }
            contact.starred = row.starred
            MessagingApps.appOf(row.mimetype)?.let { contact.apps += it }
            val value = row.value ?: continue
            when (row.mimetype) {
                Nickname.CONTENT_ITEM_TYPE -> if (value !in contact.names) contact.names += value
                Phone.CONTENT_ITEM_TYPE -> contact.numbers += PhoneEntry(value, kind(row.type, row.label), row.superPrimary)
                Email.CONTENT_ITEM_TYPE -> if (value !in contact.emails) contact.emails += value
            }
        }
        return built.filterValues { it.names.isNotEmpty() }.map { (id, contact) ->
            ContactDetails(Contact(id, contact.names.toList(), contact.numbers.toList(), contact.starred), contact.emails.toList(), contact.apps.toSet())
        }
    }

    /**
     * Telegram writes its row on a raw contact of its own, without a number, which Android joins to the owner's contact by
     * name and may fail to join, for example for a Serbian name (research r53). So a contact that has only apps' rows joins
     * the contact with a number or an address that `ContactMatcher` finds as the only one for its name, and its apps go
     * with it; when its name finds none or several, it stays as it is.
     */
    fun joinAppOnly(contacts: List<ContactDetails>): List<ContactDetails> {
        val (appOnly, full) = contacts.partition { it.contact.numbers.isEmpty() && it.emails.isEmpty() && it.apps.isNotEmpty() }
        val merged = LinkedHashMap(full.associateBy { it.contact.id })
        val kept = mutableListOf<ContactDetails>()
        for (only in appOnly) {
            val match = ContactMatcher.find(only.contact.names.first(), full.map { it.contact })
            val target = (match as? ContactMatch.One)?.let { merged[it.contact.id] }
            if (target == null) kept += only else merged[target.contact.id] = target.copy(apps = target.apps + only.apps)
        }
        return contacts.mapNotNull { contact -> merged[contact.contact.id] ?: contact.takeIf { it in kept } }
    }

    private fun kind(type: Int, label: String?): String = when (type) {
        Phone.TYPE_MOBILE -> "mobile"
        Phone.TYPE_WORK -> "work"
        Phone.TYPE_HOME -> "home"
        Phone.TYPE_MAIN -> "main"
        Phone.TYPE_WORK_MOBILE -> "work mobile"
        Phone.TYPE_CUSTOM -> label?.takeIf { it.isNotBlank() } ?: "other"
        else -> "other"
    }
}
```

Create `core/datatools/src/main/kotlin/dev/kestrel/datatools/contacts/FindContact.kt`:

```kotlin
package dev.kestrel.datatools.contacts

import dev.kestrel.agent.port.DataField
import dev.kestrel.agent.port.DataLine
import dev.kestrel.agent.port.DataResult
import dev.kestrel.commands.phone.ContactMatch
import dev.kestrel.commands.phone.ContactMatcher

/**
 * The agent's `find_contact` (design D12 of sub-project 5; research r53): the contacts that `ContactMatcher` finds for
 * [name] (folded Serbian names, Ana and Anna, Latin and Cyrillic), at most [ContactMatcher.MAX_CHOICES], each with its
 * names, numbers, e-mail addresses and messaging apps. Memory's aliases are resolved before (plan 5A's `DataSteps`). The
 * fields are untrusted and unquoted; `:core:agent` redacts and quotes them. The field `name` is the contact's display
 * name, which `DataSteps` remembers as a found contact (D32 item 44).
 */
object FindContact {
    const val NO_APP = "no app link found; the contact may still use an app"

    fun result(name: String, contacts: List<ContactDetails>): DataResult {
        val joined = ContactRows.joinAppOnly(contacts)
        val byId = joined.associateBy { it.contact.id }
        val found = when (val match = ContactMatcher.find(name, joined.map { it.contact })) {
            is ContactMatch.One -> listOf(match.contact)
            is ContactMatch.Several -> match.contacts
            is ContactMatch.TooMany -> return DataResult.Ok(emptyList(), note = "${match.count} contacts match; ask for a fuller name.")
            ContactMatch.None -> emptyList()
        }
        return DataResult.Ok(found.mapNotNull { byId[it.id] }.mapIndexed(::line))
    }

    private fun line(index: Int, details: ContactDetails): DataLine {
        val apps = MessagingApps.ordered(details.apps)
        val fixed = "contact ${index + 1} (${if (apps.isEmpty()) NO_APP else "apps: ${apps.joinToString(", ")}"})"
        val names = details.contact.names
        val fields = listOf(DataField("name", names.first())) +
            names.drop(1).map { DataField("other name", it) } +
            details.contact.numbers.map { DataField("phone", "${it.number} (${it.kind})") } +
            details.emails.map { DataField("e-mail", it) }
        return DataLine(fixed, fields)
    }
}
```

```kotlin
/**
 * The boost words of a voice session (design spec, section 8.3): "Kestrel" first, then the names of the apps that the
 * owner installed, and then those of the system apps, each group in the order in which [labels] reads them. sherpa-onnx
 * gets at most 100 phrases, so the cap drops system apps first: their common names, such as "Phone" or "Camera", need
 * no boost, while the owner's apps have the rare names that the recogniser misses, such as "Revolut". Sub-project 3
 * adds the labels on the screen and the command vocabulary, and sub-project 5 the owner's aliases and contact names. A
 * name with fewer than [SHORTEST] letters or digits, such as "X", is left out, because so short a boost would pull many
 * words towards it, and a repeated name counts once, ignoring case. When the names cannot be read, [report] gets the
 * error, which it must log by its classes only (section 13.5), and the words are "Kestrel" alone. Never log a boost
 * word or an app's name.
 */
internal class BoostWordSource(private val labels: AppLabels, private val report: (String, Throwable) -> Unit) {
    /** Reads the names of the apps on [Dispatchers.IO]. A voice session asks once, when it opens. */
    suspend fun words(): List<String> {
        val apps = try {
            withContext(Dispatchers.IO) { labels.read() }
        } catch (e: CancellationException) {
            throw e
        } catch (e: Exception) {
            report("Reading the names of the apps", e)
            emptyList()
        }
        // The owner's apps first; filter and filterNot keep the package manager's order within each group.
        val names = (apps.filterNot { it.system } + apps.filter { it.system })
            .map { it.label.trim() }
            .filter { name -> name.count { it.isLetterOrDigit() } >= SHORTEST }
        return (listOf(NAME) + names).distinctBy { it.lowercase() }
    }

    companion object {
        const val NAME = "Kestrel"
        const val SHORTEST = 3
    }
}
```

```kotlin
/** Reads the owner's own names for the boost words: aliases and contact names (D32 item 44 of sub-project 5). */
internal fun interface PeopleNames {
    suspend fun read(): List<String>
}

/**
 * The owner's names (D32 item 44 of sub-project 5): memory's [aliases] always, and, only while Kestrel may read the
 * contacts, the starred contacts and the contacts that recent tasks [found]. Android stopped reporting "recently
 * contacted" in API 29, so the recent contacts are those that Kestrel's own tasks found. It reads the contacts through
 * [contacts], so call it off the main thread.
 */
internal class OwnerNames(
    private val contacts: ContactsReader,
    private val aliases: suspend () -> List<String> = { emptyList() },
    private val found: suspend () -> List<String> = { emptyList() },
) : PeopleNames {
    override suspend fun read(): List<String> {
        val all = contacts.contacts() ?: return aliases()
        return aliases() + all.filter { it.starred }.mapNotNull { it.names.firstOrNull() } + found()
    }
}

/**
 * The boost words of a voice session (design spec, section 8.3): "Kestrel" first, then at most [MAX_PEOPLE] of the
 * owner's own names that [people] reads (D32 item 44 of sub-project 5), then the names of the apps that the owner
 * installed, and then those of the system apps, each group in the order in which it is read. sherpa-onnx gets at most
 * 100 phrases, so the cap drops system apps first: their common names, such as "Phone" or "Camera", need no boost, while
 * the owner's apps and people have the rare names that the recogniser misses, such as "Revolut". Sub-project 3 adds the
 * labels on the screen and the command vocabulary. A name with fewer than [SHORTEST] letters or digits, such as "X", is
 * left out, because so short a boost would pull many words towards it, and a repeated name counts once, ignoring case. A
 * capital "Đ" becomes "Dj" ([spellable]), because the speech model has no piece for it and its guard would drop the whole
 * name. When the names cannot be read, [report] gets the error, which it must log by its classes only (section 13.5),
 * and the words go on without them. Never log a boost word, an app's name or a person's name.
 */
internal class BoostWordSource(
    private val labels: AppLabels,
    private val people: PeopleNames = PeopleNames { emptyList() },
    private val report: (String, Throwable) -> Unit,
) {
    /** Reads the names of the people and the apps on [Dispatchers.IO]. A voice session asks once, when it opens. */
    suspend fun words(): List<String> {
        val owners = read("Reading the owner's names") { people.read() }.map { it.trim() }.filter(::fits).take(MAX_PEOPLE)
        val apps = read("Reading the names of the apps") { labels.read() }
        // The owner's apps first; filter and filterNot keep the package manager's order within each group.
        val names = (apps.filterNot { it.system } + apps.filter { it.system })
            .map { it.label.trim() }
            .filter(::fits)
        return (listOf(NAME) + owners + names).map(::spellable).distinctBy { it.lowercase() }
    }

    private suspend fun <T> read(what: String, block: suspend () -> List<T>): List<T> = try {
        withContext(Dispatchers.IO) { block() }
    } catch (e: CancellationException) {
        throw e
    } catch (e: Exception) {
        report(what, e)
        emptyList()
    }

    private fun fits(name: String): Boolean = name.count { it.isLetterOrDigit() } >= SHORTEST

    companion object {
        const val NAME = "Kestrel"
        const val SHORTEST = 3

        /** The owner's names take at most this many of sherpa-onnx's 100 phrases, so that his apps keep their place. */
        const val MAX_PEOPLE = 20

        /** [name] with a capital "Đ" as "Dj", which the speech model can spell; a small "đ" stays, because the model has it. */
        fun spellable(name: String): String = name.replace("Đ", "Dj")
    }
}
```

**Files:**
- Create: `core/datatools/src/main/kotlin/dev/kestrel/datatools/media/MediaQuery.kt`, `core/datatools/src/main/kotlin/dev/kestrel/datatools/media/ShareIntent.kt`, `core/datatools/src/main/kotlin/dev/kestrel/datatools/media/MediaTool.kt`
- Modify: `app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml` (below `<!-- sub-project 5B: permissions -->`)
- Test: `core/datatools/src/test/kotlin/dev/kestrel/datatools/media/MediaQueryTest.kt`, `core/datatools/src/androidTest/AndroidManifest.xml`, `core/datatools/src/androidTest/kotlin/dev/kestrel/datatools/DataToolsTest.kt`
- Modify: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-12-kestrel-design.md` (11.5's `find_media` and `share_media` rows, 13.6's table, Appendix B's B57 and B58)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: plan 5A's `MediaKinds`, `DataResult`, `DataLine`; Task 1's `DataToolsTest`.
- Produces (package `dev.kestrel.datatools.media`): `object MediaQuery { const val MAX_ITEMS = 30; const val PARTIAL: String; enum class Access { FULL, SELECTED, NONE }; fun permissions(kinds: MediaKinds, sdk: Int): List<String>; fun access(kinds: MediaKinds, sdk: Int, granted: (String) -> Boolean): Access; fun bounds(from: LocalDate, until: LocalDate, zone: ZoneId): Pair<Long, Long>; fun taken(dateTaken: Long?, dateAddedSeconds: Long): Long; fun line(id: String, video: Boolean, takenMillis: Long, sizeBytes: Long, zone: ZoneId): String; fun size(bytes: Long): String }`, `object ShareIntent { fun mimeType(photos: Int, videos: Int): String; fun build(packageName: String, uris: List<Uri>, mimeType: String): Intent }`, `class MediaTool(resolver: ContentResolver, granted: (String) -> Boolean, sdk: Int = Build.VERSION.SDK_INT) { suspend fun find(from: LocalDate, until: LocalDate, kinds: MediaKinds, zone: ZoneId): DataResult; fun unknown(ids: List<String>): List<String>; fun shareIntent(packageName: String, ids: List<String>): Intent; fun forget() }`.

Design D12 (research r55, r65). `find_media` reads MediaStore by `DATE_TAKEN` between the local day's bounds in the device's time zone, and falls back to `DATE_ADDED` (in seconds) when `DATE_TAKEN` is null or 0, because Android fills `DATE_TAKEN` only from EXIF's `DateTimeOriginal` with `OffsetTimeOriginal`. It returns at most 30 items, each with an item number that Kestrel assigns for the task (`m1`, `m2`, …), its kind, time and size, never the image, the file's name or its path; plan 5A's `DataSteps` reads the number before the first space and the word `video`. The media permissions are asked together, with `READ_MEDIA_VISUAL_USER_SELECTED` on API 34 and later; with only selected photos, the result says "Android gave Kestrel only the photos that you selected." `share_media` builds the `content://media/…` URIs from the task's item table (the model never sees them): `ACTION_SEND` for one item or `ACTION_SEND_MULTIPLE` for several, `setPackage`, `ClipData` with every URI and `FLAG_GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION`, and the type `image/*` for photos only, `video/*` for one video, `*/*` otherwise (Telegram's manifest); never an unofficial extra such as WhatsApp's `jid`. Task 5's `AndroidDataPort` sends the intent through `ScreenActions.openIntent`.

Counts: `:core:datatools` JVM N + 5 (`MediaQueryTest`); `:core:datatools` device N + 1 (`DataToolsTest`); the rest unchanged.

```kotlin
    fun theBoundsAreTheLocalDaysInTheDevicesZone() {
        val day = LocalDate.of(2026, 11, 19)

        assertEquals(millis("2026-11-19T00:00") to millis("2026-11-20T00:00"), MediaQuery.bounds(day, day, belgrade))
        // The day on which the clocks go forward has 23 hours, and a range ends at the start of the day after it.

        val (start, end) = MediaQuery.bounds(spring, spring, belgrade)

        assertEquals(1_795_100_000_000L, MediaQuery.taken(null, 1_795_100_000L))
        assertEquals(1_795_100_000_000L, MediaQuery.taken(0L, 1_795_100_000L))
    }

        assertEquals("m2 · photo · 2026-11-19 12:05 · 2.2 MB", line)
        assertEquals("m3 · video · 2026-11-19 12:00 · 640 KB", MediaQuery.line("m3", true, millis("2026-11-19T12:00"), 640_000, belgrade))
        assertEquals("900 B", MediaQuery.size(900))

        assertEquals("video/*", ShareIntent.mimeType(photos = 0, videos = 1))
        assertEquals("*/*", ShareIntent.mimeType(photos = 0, videos = 2))
        assertEquals("*/*", ShareIntent.mimeType(photos = 2, videos = 1))
    }

    @Test

        val video = Manifest.permission.READ_MEDIA_VIDEO
        val selected = Manifest.permission.READ_MEDIA_VISUAL_USER_SELECTED

        assertEquals(listOf(images, video, selected), MediaQuery.permissions(MediaKinds.BOTH, sdk = 34))
```

```kotlin
    private fun addTestPhoto(number: Int, taken: LocalDateTime) {
        val name = "kestrel_test_$number.jpg"
        val file = File(context.cacheDir, name)
        val card = Bitmap.createBitmap(64, 64, Bitmap.Config.ARGB_8888).apply { eraseColor(Color.BLUE) }
        file.outputStream().use { card.compress(Bitmap.CompressFormat.JPEG, 90, it) }
        val offset = ZoneId.systemDefault().rules.getOffset(taken).totalSeconds
        ExifInterface(file.path).apply {
            setAttribute(ExifInterface.TAG_DATETIME_ORIGINAL, taken.format(DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("yyyy:MM:dd HH:mm:ss")))
            setAttribute(ExifInterface.TAG_OFFSET_TIME_ORIGINAL, "%s%02d:%02d".format(if (offset < 0) "-" else "+", abs(offset) / 3600, abs(offset) % 3600 / 60))
            saveAttributes()
        }
        val values = ContentValues().apply {
            put(MediaStore.MediaColumns.DISPLAY_NAME, name)
            put(MediaStore.MediaColumns.MIME_TYPE, "image/jpeg")
            put(MediaStore.MediaColumns.RELATIVE_PATH, PHOTOS_FOLDER)
            put(MediaStore.MediaColumns.IS_PENDING, 1)
        }
        val uri = checkNotNull(resolver.insert(MediaStore.Images.Media.getContentUri(MediaStore.VOLUME_EXTERNAL_PRIMARY), values))
        checkNotNull(resolver.openOutputStream(uri)).use { output -> file.inputStream().use { it.copyTo(output) } }
        resolver.update(uri, ContentValues().apply { put(MediaStore.MediaColumns.IS_PENDING, 0) }, null, null)
        file.delete()
    }

    /** Adds a contact of the test account with a name and, when given, a mobile number, an address and an app's row. */
```

```kotlin
package dev.kestrel.datatools.media

import android.Manifest
import dev.kestrel.agent.port.MediaKinds
import java.time.Instant
import java.time.LocalDate
import java.time.ZoneId
import java.time.format.DateTimeFormatter
import java.util.Locale

/**
 * The plain rules of `find_media` (design D12 of sub-project 5; research r55, r65): which permissions it needs, which
 * days it reads, when an item was taken, and the line that names an item without its image, file name or path.
 */
object MediaQuery {
    /** `find_media` lists at most this many items. */
    const val MAX_ITEMS = 30

    const val PARTIAL = "Android gave Kestrel only the photos that you selected."

    /** How much of the owner's media Kestrel may read: all of the kinds asked for, only what he selected, or nothing. */
    enum class Access { FULL, SELECTED, NONE }

    // Manifest.permission.READ_MEDIA_VISUAL_USER_SELECTED, which Android 14 (API 34) added.
    private const val USER_SELECTED = "android.permission.READ_MEDIA_VISUAL_USER_SELECTED"

    private val TIME: DateTimeFormatter = DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm", Locale.ROOT)

    /**
     * The permissions that `find_media` asks for together: photos and videos, and on Android 14 and later the partial
     * access, which Android's dialog offers as "Select photos and videos".
     */
    fun permissions(kinds: MediaKinds, sdk: Int): List<String> =
        listOf(Manifest.permission.READ_MEDIA_IMAGES, Manifest.permission.READ_MEDIA_VIDEO) +
            if (sdk >= 34) listOf(USER_SELECTED) else emptyList()

    fun access(kinds: MediaKinds, sdk: Int, granted: (String) -> Boolean): Access {
        val needed = when (kinds) {
            MediaKinds.PHOTOS -> listOf(Manifest.permission.READ_MEDIA_IMAGES)
            MediaKinds.VIDEOS -> listOf(Manifest.permission.READ_MEDIA_VIDEO)
            MediaKinds.BOTH -> listOf(Manifest.permission.READ_MEDIA_IMAGES, Manifest.permission.READ_MEDIA_VIDEO)
        }
        return when {
            needed.all(granted) -> Access.FULL
            sdk >= 34 && granted(USER_SELECTED) -> Access.SELECTED
            else -> Access.NONE
        }
    }

    /** The start of [from] and the start of the day after [until] in [zone], in milliseconds since the epoch. */
    fun bounds(from: LocalDate, until: LocalDate, zone: ZoneId): Pair<Long, Long> =
        from.atStartOfDay(zone).toInstant().toEpochMilli() to until.plusDays(1).atStartOfDay(zone).toInstant().toEpochMilli()

    /** When an item was taken: `DATE_TAKEN`, or `DATE_ADDED` (in seconds) when Android has no `DATE_TAKEN` (r65). */
    fun taken(dateTaken: Long?, dateAddedSeconds: Long): Long = if (dateTaken == null || dateTaken == 0L) dateAddedSeconds * 1000 else dateTaken

    /** "m2 · photo · 2026-11-19 12:05 · 2.2 MB": Kestrel's own words, so the line has no untrusted field. */
    fun line(id: String, video: Boolean, takenMillis: Long, sizeBytes: Long, zone: ZoneId): String =
        "$id · ${if (video) "video" else "photo"} · ${TIME.format(Instant.ofEpochMilli(takenMillis).atZone(zone))} · ${size(sizeBytes)}"

    fun size(bytes: Long): String = when {
        bytes >= 1_000_000 -> String.format(Locale.ROOT, "%.1f MB", bytes / 1_000_000.0)
        bytes >= 1_000 -> "${bytes / 1_000} KB"
        else -> "$bytes B"
    }
}
```

Create `core/datatools/src/main/kotlin/dev/kestrel/datatools/media/ShareIntent.kt`:

```kotlin
package dev.kestrel.datatools.media

import android.content.ClipData
import android.content.Intent
import android.net.Uri

/**
 * The intent of `share_media` (design D12 of sub-project 5; research r55): `ACTION_SEND` for one item, or
 * `ACTION_SEND_MULTIPLE` for several, to one app, with every item in the `ClipData` and the read grant, so that the app
 * may open them. It never carries an app's unofficial extras, such as WhatsApp's `jid`, so the app shows its own chat
 * picker and the agent picks the chat on the screen.
 */
object ShareIntent {
    /** Any image for photos only, any video for one video alone, and anything otherwise (Telegram's manifest; r55). */
    fun mimeType(photos: Int, videos: Int): String = when {
        videos == 0 -> "image/*"
        photos == 0 && videos == 1 -> "video/*"
        else -> "*/*"
    }

    fun build(packageName: String, uris: List<Uri>, mimeType: String): Intent {
        require(uris.isNotEmpty()) { "A share needs at least one item" }
        val intent = if (uris.size == 1) {
            Intent(Intent.ACTION_SEND).putExtra(Intent.EXTRA_STREAM, uris[0])
        } else {
            Intent(Intent.ACTION_SEND_MULTIPLE).putParcelableArrayListExtra(Intent.EXTRA_STREAM, ArrayList(uris))
        }
        val clip = ClipData.newRawUri("", uris[0]).apply { uris.drop(1).forEach { addItem(ClipData.Item(it)) } }
        return intent.setPackage(packageName).setType(mimeType).apply { clipData = clip }
            .addFlags(Intent.FLAG_GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION or Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK)
    }
}
```

Create `core/datatools/src/main/kotlin/dev/kestrel/datatools/media/MediaTool.kt`:

```kotlin
package dev.kestrel.datatools.media

import android.content.ContentResolver
import android.content.ContentUris
import android.content.Intent
import android.net.Uri
import android.os.Build
import android.provider.MediaStore
import dev.kestrel.agent.port.DataLine
import dev.kestrel.agent.port.DataResult
import dev.kestrel.agent.port.MediaKinds
import kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers
import kotlinx.coroutines.withContext
import java.time.LocalDate
import java.time.ZoneId

/**
 * `find_media` and `share_media` (design D12 of sub-project 5): finds the owner's photos and videos of the days asked for
 * in MediaStore, and keeps for the task a table of item numbers (`m1`, `m2`, …) and their URIs, which the model never
 * sees; `share_media` builds its intent from that table. [granted] tells whether Kestrel holds a permission. One per
 * task's data port; [forget] drops the table when the task ends.
 */
class MediaTool(
    private val resolver: ContentResolver,
    private val granted: (String) -> Boolean,
    private val sdk: Int = Build.VERSION.SDK_INT,
) {
    private class Item(val id: String, val uri: Uri, val video: Boolean)

    private class Found(val uri: Uri, val video: Boolean, val taken: Long, val size: Long)

    private val items = LinkedHashMap<Uri, Item>()

    suspend fun find(from: LocalDate, until: LocalDate, kinds: MediaKinds, zone: ZoneId): DataResult {
        val access = MediaQuery.access(kinds, sdk, granted)
        if (access == MediaQuery.Access.NONE) return DataResult.NeedsPermission(MediaQuery.permissions(kinds, sdk))
        val (start, end) = MediaQuery.bounds(from, until, zone)
        val found = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
            val photos = if (kinds != MediaKinds.VIDEOS) query(MediaStore.Images.Media.getContentUri(MediaStore.VOLUME_EXTERNAL), false, start, end) else emptyList()
            val videos = if (kinds != MediaKinds.PHOTOS) query(MediaStore.Video.Media.getContentUri(MediaStore.VOLUME_EXTERNAL), true, start, end) else emptyList()
            (photos + videos).sortedBy { it.taken }
        }
        val lines = found.take(MediaQuery.MAX_ITEMS).map { item ->
            val known = items.getOrPut(item.uri) { Item("m${items.size + 1}", item.uri, item.video) }
            DataLine(MediaQuery.line(known.id, item.video, item.taken, item.size, zone), emptyList())
        }
        val notes = listOfNotNull(
            MediaQuery.PARTIAL.takeIf { access == MediaQuery.Access.SELECTED },
            "Kestrel lists the first ${MediaQuery.MAX_ITEMS} of ${found.size} items.".takeIf { found.size > MediaQuery.MAX_ITEMS },
        )
        return DataResult.Ok(lines, note = notes.joinToString(" ").ifEmpty { null })
    }

    /** The item numbers of [ids] that this task's `find_media` never gave. */
    fun unknown(ids: List<String>): List<String> {
        val known = items.values.map { it.id }.toSet()
        return ids.filter { it !in known }
    }

    /** The share intent of the task's items [ids] to [packageName]; every one of them must be known ([unknown]). */
    fun shareIntent(packageName: String, ids: List<String>): Intent {
        val byId = items.values.associateBy { it.id }
        val chosen = ids.distinct().map { byId.getValue(it) }
        val videos = chosen.count { it.video }
        return ShareIntent.build(packageName, chosen.map { it.uri }, ShareIntent.mimeType(chosen.size - videos, videos))
    }

    fun forget() = items.clear()

    private fun query(base: Uri, video: Boolean, start: Long, end: Long): List<Found> {
        val found = mutableListOf<Found>()
        val selection = "((${MediaStore.MediaColumns.DATE_TAKEN} >= ? AND ${MediaStore.MediaColumns.DATE_TAKEN} < ?) OR " +
            "((${MediaStore.MediaColumns.DATE_TAKEN} IS NULL OR ${MediaStore.MediaColumns.DATE_TAKEN} = 0) AND " +
            "${MediaStore.MediaColumns.DATE_ADDED} >= ? AND ${MediaStore.MediaColumns.DATE_ADDED} < ?))"
        val arguments = arrayOf(start.toString(), end.toString(), (start / 1000).toString(), (end / 1000).toString())
        resolver.query(base, COLUMNS, selection, arguments, null)?.use { rows ->
            while (rows.moveToNext()) {
                val taken = if (rows.isNull(1)) null else rows.getLong(1)
                found += Found(ContentUris.withAppendedId(base, rows.getLong(0)), video, MediaQuery.taken(taken, rows.getLong(2)), rows.getLong(3))
            }
        }
        return found
    }

    override fun toString(): String = "MediaTool(items=${items.size})"

    private companion object {
        val COLUMNS = arrayOf(MediaStore.MediaColumns._ID, MediaStore.MediaColumns.DATE_TAKEN, MediaStore.MediaColumns.DATE_ADDED, MediaStore.MediaColumns.SIZE)
    }
}
```

- Modify: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-12-kestrel-design.md` (11.5's rows of the calendar, the clock, SMS, the call log and the media keys)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: plan 5A's `DataResult`, `DataLine`, `DataField`, `MediaAction`; `:core:commands`' `Contact`, `ContactMatcher`, `ContactMatch`, `Normalizer`; Tasks 1 and 2's `DataToolsTest`.
- Produces: `object DataLines { const val SAME_DIGITS = 8; fun time(millis: Long, zone: ZoneId): String; fun event(title: String?, begin: Long, end: Long, allDay: Boolean, location: String?, calendar: String?, zone: ZoneId): DataLine; fun sms(received: Boolean, address: String?, name: String?, body: String?, date: Long, zone: ZoneId): DataLine; fun call(type: Int, name: String?, number: String?, date: Long, durationSeconds: Long, zone: ZoneId): DataLine; fun callKind(type: Int): String; fun duration(seconds: Long): String; fun sameNumber(a: String?, b: String?): Boolean }` (package `dev.kestrel.datatools`); `class CalendarTool(resolver: ContentResolver, granted: (String) -> Boolean) { suspend fun list(from: LocalDate, to: LocalDate, zone: ZoneId): DataResult; companion object { const val MAX = 20; fun insertIntent(title: String, start: LocalDateTime, end: LocalDateTime?, location: String?, zone: ZoneId): Intent } }`; `object ClockIntents { fun alarm(hour: Int, minute: Int, label: String?, days: List<DayOfWeek>): Intent; fun timer(seconds: Int, label: String?): Intent; fun calendarDays(days: List<DayOfWeek>): ArrayList<Int> }`; `class SmsTool(resolver: ContentResolver, granted: (String) -> Boolean, contacts: () -> List<Contact>?) { suspend fun list(from: String?, limit: Int, zone: ZoneId): DataResult; companion object { const val MAX = 20; fun composeIntent(number: String, text: String): Intent; fun numbersOf(wanted: String, contacts: List<Contact>?): List<String>?; fun matches(wanted: String, numbers: List<String>?, address: String?): Boolean; fun nameOf(address: String?, contacts: List<Contact>): String? } }`; `class CallLogTool(resolver: ContentResolver, granted: (String) -> Boolean) { suspend fun list(limit: Int, zone: ZoneId): DataResult; companion object { const val MAX = 20 } }`; `class MediaKeys(audio: AudioManager) { fun press(action: MediaAction): DataResult }`.

Design D12. `list_events` reads `CalendarContract.Instances` between two local days, at most 20, with the title, the location and the calendar's name as untrusted fields and the times in Kestrel's own words; `create_event` builds `ACTION_INSERT` on `CalendarContract.Events` with its extras, so that the calendar app's own screen shows the event and the agent taps Save (an `ordinary_settings` action). `set_alarm` and `set_timer` build `AlarmClock`'s intents with `EXTRA_SKIP_UI`, which need the normal permission `SET_ALARM`. `list_sms` reads `Telephony.Sms` (received and sent), newest first, at most 20, optionally from one number or one contact, with the contact's name when Kestrel may read the contacts; `compose_sms` builds `ACTION_SENDTO` with `smsto:` and `sms_body`, so that the send happens on screen as a `sending` action; Kestrel never asks for `SEND_SMS`. `list_calls` reads `CallLog.Calls` with the name, number, kind, time and duration. `media_control` presses the media keys through `AudioManager`, as the instant commands' "play" and "pause" do. Task 5's `AndroidDataPort` starts the intents through `ScreenActions.openIntent`.

```kotlin
class DataLinesTest {

    @Test

        assertEquals("event · 2026-11-20 12:00 to 13:30", line.fixed)
        assertEquals(listOf("title" to "Lunch", "location" to "Main Street 1", "calendar" to "Personal"), line.fields.map { it.name to it.value })
        // An all-day event is stored at midnight UTC, so its day is read in UTC; an empty location gives no field.
        val allDay = DataLines.event("Holiday", 1_795_046_400_000L, 1_795_132_800_000L, true, "", "Personal", belgrade)
        assertEquals("event · 2026-11-19 · all day", allDay.fixed)
        assertEquals(listOf("title", "calendar"), allDay.fields.map { it.name })

    @Test
    fun anSmsFromAContactIsNamedByTheContactWhoseNumberEndsTheSame() {
        val ana = Contact(1, listOf("Ana Petrović"), listOf(PhoneEntry("064 123 4567", "mobile", superPrimary = false)), starred = false)

        assertEquals("Ana Petrović", SmsTool.nameOf("+381641234567", listOf(ana)))
        assertNull(SmsTool.nameOf("+381641234568", listOf(ana)))
        assertTrue(DataLines.sameNumber("+1 202 555 0143", "2025550143"))
        assertFalse(DataLines.sameNumber("1234", "51234"))
        // By name only with the contacts; without them a name compares with an alphanumeric sender.
        assertEquals(listOf("064 123 4567"), SmsTool.numbersOf("Ana", listOf(ana)))
        assertTrue(SmsTool.matches("Ana", listOf("064 123 4567"), "+381641234567"))
        assertNull(SmsTool.numbersOf("Telenor", null))
        assertTrue(SmsTool.matches("telenor", null, "Telenor"))
        // With the contacts too, a name that is no contact's compares with an alphanumeric sender.
        assertEquals(emptyList<String>(), SmsTool.numbersOf("Telenor", listOf(ana)))
        assertTrue(SmsTool.matches("Telenor", emptyList(), "Telenor"))
        assertTrue(SmsTool.matches("064 123 4567", null, "+381641234567"))

        val line = DataLines.sms(received = true, address = "+381641234567", name = "Ana Petrović", body = "Kasnim 10 minuta", date = millis("2026-11-20T10:20"), zone = belgrade)
        assertEquals("sms · received · 2026-11-20 10:20", line.fixed)
        assertEquals(listOf("from" to "Ana Petrović", "number" to "+381641234567", "text" to "Kasnim 10 minuta"), line.fields.map { it.name to it.value })
    }

    @Test
    fun aCallLineSaysItsKindTimeAndDuration() {
        val line = DataLines.call(CallLog.Calls.MISSED_TYPE, "Ana Petrović", "+381641234567", millis("2026-11-20T10:20"), 0, belgrade)

        assertEquals("call · missed · 2026-11-20 10:20 · 0 s", line.fixed)
        assertEquals("3 min 12 s", DataLines.duration(192))
        assertEquals("outgoing", DataLines.callKind(CallLog.Calls.OUTGOING_TYPE))
        assertEquals(listOf("number"), DataLines.call(CallLog.Calls.INCOMING_TYPE, null, "+381641234567", 0, 5, belgrade).fields.map { it.name })
    }

    @Test
    fun anAlarmsDaysAreTheCalendarsDayNumbers() {
        assertEquals(arrayListOf(Calendar.MONDAY, Calendar.FRIDAY, Calendar.SUNDAY), ClockIntents.calendarDays(listOf(DayOfWeek.MONDAY, DayOfWeek.FRIDAY, DayOfWeek.SUNDAY, DayOfWeek.MONDAY)))
    }
```

```kotlin
package dev.kestrel.datatools

import android.provider.CallLog
import dev.kestrel.agent.port.DataField
import dev.kestrel.agent.port.DataLine
import java.time.Instant
import java.time.ZoneId
import java.time.ZoneOffset
import java.time.format.DateTimeFormatter
import java.util.Locale

/**
 * The result lines of the data tools that read Android's providers (design D12 of sub-project 5): Kestrel's own words,
 * such as kinds and times, in the fixed text; every text that comes from the owner's data (titles, places, names,
 * numbers, bodies) as an unquoted field, which `:core:agent` redacts and quotes. A blank text gives no field. Pure, so
 * that the JVM tests check it.
 */
object DataLines {
    /** Two phone numbers with at least this many digits are the same when their last this many digits are. */
    const val SAME_DIGITS = 8

    private val TIME: DateTimeFormatter = DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm", Locale.ROOT)
    private val CLOCK: DateTimeFormatter = DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("HH:mm", Locale.ROOT)
    private val DAY: DateTimeFormatter = DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("yyyy-MM-dd", Locale.ROOT)

    fun time(millis: Long, zone: ZoneId): String = TIME.format(Instant.ofEpochMilli(millis).atZone(zone))

    /** "event · 2026-11-20 12:00 to 13:30", or "event · 2026-11-19 · all day" for an event that Android stores in UTC. */
    fun event(title: String?, begin: Long, end: Long, allDay: Boolean, location: String?, calendar: String?, zone: ZoneId): DataLine {
        val fixed = if (allDay) {
            "event · ${DAY.format(Instant.ofEpochMilli(begin).atZone(ZoneOffset.UTC))} · all day"
        } else {
            val from = Instant.ofEpochMilli(begin).atZone(zone)
            val to = Instant.ofEpochMilli(end).atZone(zone)
            "event · ${TIME.format(from)} to ${if (to.toLocalDate() == from.toLocalDate()) CLOCK.format(to) else TIME.format(to)}"
        }
        return DataLine(fixed, listOfNotNull(field("title", title), field("location", location), field("calendar", calendar)))
    }

    /** "sms · received · 2026-11-20 10:20", with the other side by the contact's [name] and its number, and the body. */
    fun sms(received: Boolean, address: String?, name: String?, body: String?, date: Long, zone: ZoneId): DataLine {
        val fixed = "sms · ${if (received) "received" else "sent"} · ${time(date, zone)}"
        val side = if (received) "from" else "to"
        return DataLine(fixed, listOfNotNull(field(side, name ?: address), field("number", address.takeIf { name != null }), field("text", body)))
    }

    /** "call · missed · 2026-11-20 10:20 · 0 s", with the name that the call log keeps and the number. */
    fun call(type: Int, name: String?, number: String?, date: Long, durationSeconds: Long, zone: ZoneId): DataLine =
        DataLine("call · ${callKind(type)} · ${time(date, zone)} · ${duration(durationSeconds)}", listOfNotNull(field("name", name), field("number", number)))

    fun callKind(type: Int): String = when (type) {
        CallLog.Calls.INCOMING_TYPE -> "incoming"
        CallLog.Calls.OUTGOING_TYPE -> "outgoing"
        CallLog.Calls.MISSED_TYPE -> "missed"
        CallLog.Calls.VOICEMAIL_TYPE -> "voicemail"
        CallLog.Calls.REJECTED_TYPE -> "rejected"
        CallLog.Calls.BLOCKED_TYPE -> "blocked"
        else -> "other"
    }

    fun duration(seconds: Long): String = if (seconds >= 60) "${seconds / 60} min ${seconds % 60} s" else "$seconds s"

    /**
     * Whether two phone numbers name the same phone: their last [SAME_DIGITS] digits when both have that many, so that a
     * country code or a leading zero does not count, else all their digits.
     */
    fun sameNumber(a: String?, b: String?): Boolean {
        val first = a?.filter(Char::isDigit).orEmpty()
        val second = b?.filter(Char::isDigit).orEmpty()
        if (first.isEmpty() || second.isEmpty()) return false
        return if (first.length >= SAME_DIGITS && second.length >= SAME_DIGITS) first.takeLast(SAME_DIGITS) == second.takeLast(SAME_DIGITS) else first == second
    }

    private fun field(name: String, value: String?): DataField? = value?.takeIf { it.isNotBlank() }?.let { DataField(name, it) }
}
```

```kotlin
package dev.kestrel.datatools.calendar

import android.Manifest
import android.content.ContentResolver
import android.content.ContentUris
import android.content.Intent
import android.provider.CalendarContract
import dev.kestrel.agent.port.DataLine
import dev.kestrel.agent.port.DataResult
import dev.kestrel.datatools.DataLines
import kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers
import kotlinx.coroutines.withContext
import java.time.LocalDate
import java.time.LocalDateTime
import java.time.ZoneId

/**
 * `list_events` and `create_event` (design D12 of sub-project 5): the events of the owner's calendars between two local
 * days, at most [MAX], and the calendar app's own insert screen for a new event, where the agent taps Save. [granted]
 * tells whether Kestrel holds a permission.
 */
class CalendarTool(private val resolver: ContentResolver, private val granted: (String) -> Boolean) {
    suspend fun list(from: LocalDate, to: LocalDate, zone: ZoneId): DataResult {
        if (!granted(Manifest.permission.READ_CALENDAR)) return DataResult.NeedsPermission(listOf(Manifest.permission.READ_CALENDAR))
        val start = from.atStartOfDay(zone).toInstant().toEpochMilli()
        val end = to.plusDays(1).atStartOfDay(zone).toInstant().toEpochMilli()
        val uri = CalendarContract.Instances.CONTENT_URI.buildUpon().also {
            ContentUris.appendId(it, start)
            ContentUris.appendId(it, end)
        }.build()
        val lines = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
            val found = mutableListOf<DataLine>()
            resolver.query(uri, COLUMNS, null, null, "${CalendarContract.Instances.BEGIN} ASC")?.use { rows ->
                while (found.size < MAX && rows.moveToNext()) {
                    found += DataLines.event(rows.getString(0), rows.getLong(1), rows.getLong(2), rows.getInt(3) != 0, rows.getString(4), rows.getString(5), zone)
                }
            }
            found
        }
        return DataResult.Ok(lines)
    }

    companion object {
        const val MAX = 20

        private val COLUMNS = arrayOf(
            CalendarContract.Instances.TITLE,
            CalendarContract.Instances.BEGIN,
            CalendarContract.Instances.END,
            CalendarContract.Instances.ALL_DAY,
            CalendarContract.Instances.EVENT_LOCATION,
            CalendarContract.Instances.CALENDAR_DISPLAY_NAME,
        )

        /** The calendar app's insert screen with the event; without an end, the event lasts an hour. */
        fun insertIntent(title: String, start: LocalDateTime, end: LocalDateTime?, location: String?, zone: ZoneId): Intent {
            val begin = start.atZone(zone).toInstant().toEpochMilli()
            val finish = end?.atZone(zone)?.toInstant()?.toEpochMilli() ?: (begin + 3_600_000)
            return Intent(Intent.ACTION_INSERT, CalendarContract.Events.CONTENT_URI)
                .putExtra(CalendarContract.EXTRA_EVENT_BEGIN_TIME, begin)
                .putExtra(CalendarContract.EXTRA_EVENT_END_TIME, finish)
                .putExtra(CalendarContract.Events.TITLE, title)
                .apply { location?.let { putExtra(CalendarContract.Events.EVENT_LOCATION, it) } }
                .addFlags(Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK)
        }
    }
}
```

```kotlin
package dev.kestrel.datatools.clock

import android.content.Intent
import android.provider.AlarmClock
import java.time.DayOfWeek

/**
 * `set_alarm` and `set_timer` (design D12 of sub-project 5): Android's clock intents with `EXTRA_SKIP_UI`, so that the
 * clock app sets them without showing its screen. They need the normal permission `SET_ALARM`.
 */
object ClockIntents {
    fun alarm(hour: Int, minute: Int, label: String?, days: List<DayOfWeek>): Intent =
        Intent(AlarmClock.ACTION_SET_ALARM)
            .putExtra(AlarmClock.EXTRA_HOUR, hour)
            .putExtra(AlarmClock.EXTRA_MINUTES, minute)
            .putExtra(AlarmClock.EXTRA_SKIP_UI, true)
            .apply {
                label?.let { putExtra(AlarmClock.EXTRA_MESSAGE, it) }
                if (days.isNotEmpty()) putIntegerArrayListExtra(AlarmClock.EXTRA_DAYS, calendarDays(days))
            }
            .addFlags(Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK)

    fun timer(seconds: Int, label: String?): Intent =
        Intent(AlarmClock.ACTION_SET_TIMER)
            .putExtra(AlarmClock.EXTRA_LENGTH, seconds)
            .putExtra(AlarmClock.EXTRA_SKIP_UI, true)
            .apply { label?.let { putExtra(AlarmClock.EXTRA_MESSAGE, it) } }
            .addFlags(Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK)

    /** The days as `java.util.Calendar` numbers them (Sunday 1 to Saturday 7), each once, which `EXTRA_DAYS` expects. */
    fun calendarDays(days: List<DayOfWeek>): ArrayList<Int> = days.distinct().mapTo(ArrayList()) { it.value % 7 + 1 }
}
```

```kotlin
package dev.kestrel.datatools.sms

import android.Manifest
import android.content.ContentResolver
import android.content.Intent
import android.net.Uri
import android.provider.Telephony
import dev.kestrel.agent.port.DataLine
import dev.kestrel.agent.port.DataResult
import dev.kestrel.commands.phone.Contact
import dev.kestrel.commands.phone.ContactMatch
import dev.kestrel.commands.phone.ContactMatcher
import dev.kestrel.commands.text.Normalizer
import dev.kestrel.datatools.DataLines
import kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers
import kotlinx.coroutines.withContext
import java.time.ZoneId

/**
 * `list_sms` and `compose_sms` (design D12 of sub-project 5): the owner's received and sent SMS, newest first, at most
 * [MAX], optionally from one number or one contact, with the contact's name while [contacts] gives the contacts (null
 * without `READ_CONTACTS`); and the SMS app's compose screen with a prefilled text, whose send happens on the screen.
 * Kestrel never asks for `SEND_SMS` (spec 13.6).
 */
class SmsTool(
    private val resolver: ContentResolver,
    private val granted: (String) -> Boolean,
    private val contacts: () -> List<Contact>?,
) {
    suspend fun list(from: String?, limit: Int, zone: ZoneId): DataResult {
        if (!granted(Manifest.permission.READ_SMS)) return DataResult.NeedsPermission(listOf(Manifest.permission.READ_SMS))
        val count = limit.coerceIn(1, MAX)
        val wanted = from?.trim()?.takeIf { it.isNotEmpty() }
        val lines = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
            val known = contacts()
            val numbers = wanted?.let { numbersOf(it, known) }
            val found = mutableListOf<DataLine>()
            val selection = "${Telephony.Sms.TYPE} IN (${Telephony.Sms.MESSAGE_TYPE_INBOX}, ${Telephony.Sms.MESSAGE_TYPE_SENT})"
            resolver.query(Telephony.Sms.CONTENT_URI, COLUMNS, selection, null, "${Telephony.Sms.DATE} DESC")?.use { rows ->
                while (found.size < count && rows.moveToNext()) {
                    val address = rows.getString(0)
                    if (wanted != null && !matches(wanted, numbers, address)) continue
                    val name = known?.let { nameOf(address, it) }
                    found += DataLines.sms(rows.getInt(2) == Telephony.Sms.MESSAGE_TYPE_INBOX, address, name, rows.getString(3), rows.getLong(1), zone)
                }
            }
            found
        }
        return DataResult.Ok(lines)
    }

    companion object {
        const val MAX = 20

        private val COLUMNS = arrayOf(Telephony.Sms.ADDRESS, Telephony.Sms.DATE, Telephony.Sms.TYPE, Telephony.Sms.BODY)

        /** The SMS app's compose screen for [number] with [text], through `smsto:`. */
        fun composeIntent(number: String, text: String): Intent =
            Intent(Intent.ACTION_SENDTO, Uri.fromParts("smsto", number, null))
                .putExtra("sms_body", text)
                .addFlags(Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK)

        /**
         * The numbers of the contacts that [wanted] names, when it is a name and Kestrel has the [contacts]; null when it is
         * a number or there are no contacts to look in.
         */
        fun numbersOf(wanted: String, contacts: List<Contact>?): List<String>? {
            if (wanted.count(Char::isDigit) >= 3 || contacts == null) return null
            val found = when (val match = ContactMatcher.find(wanted, contacts)) {
                is ContactMatch.One -> listOf(match.contact)
                is ContactMatch.Several -> match.contacts
                else -> emptyList()
            }
            return found.flatMap { contact -> contact.numbers.map { it.number } }
        }

        /** Whether an SMS with [address] is from or to [wanted]: its number, its contact's [numbers], or a sender's name. */
        fun matches(wanted: String, numbers: List<String>?, address: String?): Boolean = when {
            wanted.count(Char::isDigit) >= 3 -> DataLines.sameNumber(wanted, address)
            numbers?.any { DataLines.sameNumber(it, address) } == true -> true
            else -> address != null && Normalizer.normalize(address) == Normalizer.normalize(wanted)
        }

        /** The display name of the contact with [address]'s number, if any. */
        fun nameOf(address: String?, contacts: List<Contact>): String? =
            contacts.firstOrNull { contact -> contact.numbers.any { DataLines.sameNumber(it.number, address) } }?.names?.firstOrNull()
    }
}
```

```kotlin
package dev.kestrel.datatools.calls

import android.Manifest
import android.content.ContentResolver
import android.provider.CallLog
import dev.kestrel.agent.port.DataLine
import dev.kestrel.agent.port.DataResult
import dev.kestrel.datatools.DataLines
import kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers
import kotlinx.coroutines.withContext
import java.time.ZoneId

/** `list_calls` (design D12 of sub-project 5): the newest calls of the call history, at most [MAX]. */
class CallLogTool(private val resolver: ContentResolver, private val granted: (String) -> Boolean) {
    suspend fun list(limit: Int, zone: ZoneId): DataResult {
        if (!granted(Manifest.permission.READ_CALL_LOG)) return DataResult.NeedsPermission(listOf(Manifest.permission.READ_CALL_LOG))
        val count = limit.coerceIn(1, MAX)
        val lines = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
            val found = mutableListOf<DataLine>()
            resolver.query(CallLog.Calls.CONTENT_URI, COLUMNS, null, null, "${CallLog.Calls.DATE} DESC")?.use { rows ->
                while (found.size < count && rows.moveToNext()) {
                    found += DataLines.call(rows.getInt(2), rows.getString(0), rows.getString(1), rows.getLong(3), rows.getLong(4), zone)
                }
            }
            found
        }
        return DataResult.Ok(lines)
    }
```
