```kotlin
package dev.kestrel.datatools.media

import android.media.AudioManager
import android.view.KeyEvent
import dev.kestrel.agent.port.DataLine
import dev.kestrel.agent.port.DataResult
import dev.kestrel.agent.port.MediaAction
import java.util.Locale

/** `media_control` (design D12 of sub-project 5): the media keys through Android's audio manager, as the instant commands press them. */
class MediaKeys(private val audio: AudioManager) {
    fun press(action: MediaAction): DataResult {
        val key = when (action) {
            MediaAction.PLAY -> KeyEvent.KEYCODE_MEDIA_PLAY
            MediaAction.PAUSE -> KeyEvent.KEYCODE_MEDIA_PAUSE
            MediaAction.NEXT -> KeyEvent.KEYCODE_MEDIA_NEXT
            MediaAction.PREVIOUS -> KeyEvent.KEYCODE_MEDIA_PREVIOUS
        }
        audio.dispatchMediaKeyEvent(KeyEvent(KeyEvent.ACTION_DOWN, key))
        audio.dispatchMediaKeyEvent(KeyEvent(KeyEvent.ACTION_UP, key))
        return DataResult.Ok(listOf(DataLine("Kestrel pressed the media key ${action.name.lowercase(Locale.ROOT)}.", emptyList())))
    }
}
```

**Files:**

- Modify: `app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml` (the location permissions below Task 3's, and the `<queries>` below `<!-- sub-project 5B: queries -->`), `core/datatools/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml` (replaced whole: the two location permissions, for lint's `MissingPermission`)
- Test: `core/datatools/src/test/kotlin/dev/kestrel/datatools/navigation/NavigationIntentsTest.kt`, `core/datatools/src/test/kotlin/dev/kestrel/datatools/location/GpsLocationTest.kt`, `core/datatools/src/androidTest/kotlin/dev/kestrel/datatools/DataToolsTest.kt`
- Modify: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-12-kestrel-design.md` (11.5's `get_location` and `navigate` rows, 13.6's `<queries>` bullet, Appendix B's B59 and B60)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: plan 5A's `IntentSpec`, `NavigationApp`, `TravelMode`, `DataResult`, `DataLine`; Tasks 1 to 3's `DataToolsTest`.
- Produces: `class GpsLocation(manager: LocationManager, granted: (String) -> Boolean) { suspend fun current(): DataResult; companion object { const val WAIT_MILLIS = 30_000L; const val QUICK_NULL_MILLIS = 2_000L; const val NO_FIX: String; const val LAST_FIX: String; const val BACKGROUND: String; const val LOCATION_OFF: String; fun line(latitude: Double, longitude: Double, accuracyMetres: Float, ageMillis: Long, approximate: Boolean): String; fun age(millis: Long): String; fun refusedInBackground(nullAfterMillis: Long): Boolean } }` (package `dev.kestrel.datatools.location`); `object NavigationIntents { const val WAZE = "com.waze"; const val GOOGLE_MAPS = "com.google.android.apps.maps"; const val WAZE_RESULT: String; const val MAPS_RESULT: String; const val MAPS_NEEDS_ADDRESS: String; fun waze(to: String): IntentSpec; fun googleMaps(to: String, mode: TravelMode?): IntentSpec? }` (package `dev.kestrel.datatools.navigation`); `object IntentSpecs { fun toIntent(spec: IntentSpec): Intent; fun resolve(packageManager: PackageManager, spec: IntentSpec): String?; fun resolve(packageManager: PackageManager, intent: Intent): String? }` (package `dev.kestrel.datatools`).

Design D11, D12 (research r56, r58); deferred item 32 (D32). `get_location` asks only the GPS provider for one fresh fix (`LocationManager.getCurrentLocation(GPS_PROVIDER, …)` with high accuracy and a limit of 30 s), never the network or fused provider and never `Geocoder`, because those can send the location to Google (spec 13.1); without a fix it gives the last GPS fix with its age, or "No satellite fix; try near a window or outdoors". With only coarse access it says `approximate: true`. When Android answers at once with no fix, which is what it does for an app that may not ask for the location in the background, the tool says "no location: Android did not allow it in the background", and the agent tells the owner so; plan 5B's location device test (Task 19) checks it with another app in front (D32 item 45). `navigate` builds Waze's `waze://?favorite=home&navigate=yes` (or `work`, `ll=<lat>,<lon>`, `q=<address>`), which since Waze 5.3 only opens the route preview, so the result says "Waze shows the route; tap Go to start", and Google Maps' `google.navigation:q=…&mode=…` with `setPackage`, which starts turn-by-turn navigation; Google Maps has no home keyword, so "home" and "work" need an address alias there. `IntentSpecs` turns plan 5A's `IntentSpec` (the `open_url`, `open_deep_link` and `open_settings` tools and the navigation links) into Android's `Intent`, and resolves it to the package that would open it, which `AppScreenPort` (Task 13) uses for `ScreenPort.resolve`. The manifest's `<queries>` let Kestrel see the apps and handlers that these tools name (D32 item 32): the share targets, Waze, Google Maps and the browsers by package, `https` links, the deep-link schemes of spec 11.4, the calendar's insert screen, the clock's intents, `smsto:` and the settings pages of `open_settings`.

Counts: `:core:datatools` JVM N + 3 (`NavigationIntentsTest` 2, `GpsLocationTest` 1); `:core:datatools` device N + 1 (`DataToolsTest`); the rest unchanged.

Create `core/datatools/src/main/kotlin/dev/kestrel/datatools/location/GpsLocation.kt`:

```kotlin
package dev.kestrel.datatools.location

import android.Manifest
import android.location.Location
import android.location.LocationManager
import android.location.LocationRequest
import android.os.CancellationSignal
import android.os.SystemClock
import dev.kestrel.agent.port.DataLine
import dev.kestrel.agent.port.DataResult
import kotlinx.coroutines.suspendCancellableCoroutine
import kotlinx.coroutines.withTimeoutOrNull
import java.util.Locale
import java.util.concurrent.Executor
import kotlin.coroutines.resume
import kotlin.coroutines.resumeWithException

/**
 * `get_location` (design D12 of sub-project 5; research r58): one fresh fix from the GPS provider alone, with high
 * accuracy, waiting at most [WAIT_MILLIS]; never the network or fused provider and never `Geocoder`, which can send the
 * location to Google (spec 13.1). Without a fix it gives the phone's last GPS fix with its age. [granted] tells whether
 * Kestrel holds a permission; with only coarse access the location is approximate. The coordinates are Kestrel's own
 * text, so the line has no untrusted field.
 */
class GpsLocation(private val manager: LocationManager, private val granted: (String) -> Boolean) {
    suspend fun current(): DataResult {
        val fine = granted(Manifest.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION)
        if (!fine && !granted(Manifest.permission.ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION)) {
            return DataResult.NeedsPermission(listOf(Manifest.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION, Manifest.permission.ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION))
        }
        if (!manager.isProviderEnabled(LocationManager.GPS_PROVIDER)) return DataResult.Failed(LOCATION_OFF)
        val started = SystemClock.elapsedRealtime()
        val fresh = try {
            fix()
        } catch (e: SecurityException) {
            return DataResult.Failed(BACKGROUND)
        }
        if (fresh != null) return result(fresh, approximate = !fine, note = null)
        if (refusedInBackground(SystemClock.elapsedRealtime() - started)) return DataResult.Failed(BACKGROUND)
        val last = try {
            manager.getLastKnownLocation(LocationManager.GPS_PROVIDER)
        } catch (e: SecurityException) {
            null
        } ?: return DataResult.Failed(NO_FIX)
        return result(last, approximate = !fine, note = LAST_FIX)
    }

    private suspend fun fix(): Location? = withTimeoutOrNull(WAIT_MILLIS) {
        suspendCancellableCoroutine { continuation ->
            val signal = CancellationSignal()
            continuation.invokeOnCancellation { signal.cancel() }
            val request = LocationRequest.Builder(0).setQuality(LocationRequest.QUALITY_HIGH_ACCURACY).setDurationMillis(WAIT_MILLIS).build()
            try {
                manager.getCurrentLocation(LocationManager.GPS_PROVIDER, request, signal, Executor { it.run() }) { continuation.resume(it) }
            } catch (e: SecurityException) {
                continuation.resumeWithException(e)
            }
        }
    }

    private fun result(location: Location, approximate: Boolean, note: String?): DataResult {
        val age = (SystemClock.elapsedRealtimeNanos() - location.elapsedRealtimeNanos) / 1_000_000
        val line = line(location.latitude, location.longitude, location.accuracy, age.coerceAtLeast(0), approximate)
        return DataResult.Ok(listOf(DataLine(line, emptyList())), note = note)
    }

    companion object {
        const val WAIT_MILLIS = 30_000L

        /** A null answer sooner than this is Android's refusal, not a search for satellites that found none. */
        const val QUICK_NULL_MILLIS = 2_000L

        const val NO_FIX = "No satellite fix; try near a window or outdoors."
        const val LAST_FIX = "No satellite fix now; this is the phone's last satellite fix."
        const val BACKGROUND = "no location: Android did not allow it in the background"
        const val LOCATION_OFF = "the phone's location is turned off"

        fun line(latitude: Double, longitude: Double, accuracyMetres: Float, ageMillis: Long, approximate: Boolean): String =
            String.format(Locale.ROOT, "latitude %.5f, longitude %.5f, accuracy %d m, %s old, approximate: %b", latitude, longitude, accuracyMetres.toInt(), age(ageMillis), approximate)

        fun age(millis: Long): String = when {
            millis < 60_000 -> "${millis / 1_000} s"
            millis < 3_600_000 -> "${millis / 60_000} min"
            else -> "${millis / 3_600_000} h"
        }

        fun refusedInBackground(nullAfterMillis: Long): Boolean = nullAfterMillis < QUICK_NULL_MILLIS
    }
}
```

Create `core/datatools/src/main/kotlin/dev/kestrel/datatools/navigation/NavigationIntents.kt`:

```kotlin
package dev.kestrel.datatools.navigation

import dev.kestrel.agent.port.IntentSpec
import dev.kestrel.agent.port.TravelMode
import java.net.URLEncoder

/**
 * `navigate`'s links (design D12 of sub-project 5; research r56). Waze gets `waze://` with `favorite=home` or `work`,
 * `ll=<lat>,<lon>` or `q=<address>`, and `navigate=yes`, which since Waze 5.3 opens only the route preview: the agent then
 * taps Go. Google Maps gets `google.navigation:q=…&mode=…`, which starts turn-by-turn navigation by itself; it has no
 * home keyword, so home and work need an address alias. `geo:` is never used, because it only shows a map.
 */
object NavigationIntents {
    const val WAZE = "com.waze"
    const val GOOGLE_MAPS = "com.google.android.apps.maps"
    const val WAZE_RESULT = "Waze shows the route; tap Go to start."
    const val MAPS_RESULT = "Google Maps starts the navigation."
    const val MAPS_NEEDS_ADDRESS = "Google Maps has no home or work; ask the owner for the address."

    private const val VIEW = "android.intent.action.VIEW"
    private val COORDINATES = Regex("""^\s*(-?\d{1,2}(?:\.\d+)?)\s*,\s*(-?\d{1,3}(?:\.\d+)?)\s*$""")
    private val FAVOURITES = setOf("home", "work")

    fun waze(to: String): IntentSpec {
        val target = to.trim()
        val place = target.lowercase()
        val coordinates = COORDINATES.find(target)
        val query = when {
            place in FAVOURITES -> "favorite=$place"
            coordinates != null -> "ll=${coordinates.groupValues[1]},${coordinates.groupValues[2]}"
            else -> "q=${encode(target)}"
        }
        return IntentSpec(VIEW, "waze://?$query&navigate=yes", WAZE)
    }

    /** Google Maps' navigation to [to], or null for home and work, which Google Maps does not know. */
    fun googleMaps(to: String, mode: TravelMode?): IntentSpec? {
        val target = to.trim()
        if (target.lowercase() in FAVOURITES) return null
        val coordinates = COORDINATES.find(target)
        val place = if (coordinates != null) "${coordinates.groupValues[1]},${coordinates.groupValues[2]}" else encode(target)
        val letter = when (mode) {
            TravelMode.BICYCLE -> "b"
            TravelMode.WALK -> "w"
            TravelMode.TWO_WHEELER -> "l"
            TravelMode.DRIVE, null -> "d"
        }
        return IntentSpec(VIEW, "google.navigation:q=$place&mode=$letter", GOOGLE_MAPS)
    }

    private fun encode(text: String): String = URLEncoder.encode(text, Charsets.UTF_8).replace("+", "%20")
}
```

Create `core/datatools/src/main/kotlin/dev/kestrel/datatools/IntentSpecs.kt`:

```kotlin
package dev.kestrel.datatools

import android.content.Intent
import android.content.pm.PackageManager
import android.net.Uri
import dev.kestrel.agent.port.IntentSpec

/**
 * Turns plan 5A's plain [IntentSpec] (the `open_url`, `open_deep_link` and `open_settings` tools, and `navigate`) into
 * Android's intent, and finds the app that would open it (design D11 and D32 item 12 of sub-project 5), with the
 * `<queries>` of Kestrel's manifest.
 */
object IntentSpecs {
    // Android's own chooser and resolver: a link that several apps take resolves to them, which names no app.
    private val CHOOSERS = setOf("android", "com.android.intentresolver")

    fun toIntent(spec: IntentSpec): Intent = Intent(spec.action).apply {
        spec.data?.let { data = Uri.parse(it) }
        spec.packageName?.let { setPackage(it) }
        if (spec.browsable) addCategory(Intent.CATEGORY_BROWSABLE)
        for ((name, value) in spec.extras) putExtra(name, value)
        addFlags(Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK)
    }

    /** The package of the activity that would open [spec], or null when none would or Android would ask which one. Off the main thread. */
    fun resolve(packageManager: PackageManager, spec: IntentSpec): String? = resolve(packageManager, toIntent(spec))

    /** The package of the activity that would open [intent], or null when none would or Android would ask which one. Off the main thread. */
    fun resolve(packageManager: PackageManager, intent: Intent): String? {
        val flags = PackageManager.ResolveInfoFlags.of(PackageManager.MATCH_DEFAULT_ONLY.toLong())
        return packageManager.resolveActivity(intent, flags)?.activityInfo?.packageName?.takeIf { it !in CHOOSERS }
    }
}
```

### Task 5: `list_notifications`, the data port, and the restricted-settings check

**Files:**
- Create: `core/datatools/src/main/kotlin/dev/kestrel/datatools/notifications/NotificationLines.kt`, `core/datatools/src/main/kotlin/dev/kestrel/datatools/notifications/KestrelNotificationListener.kt`, `core/datatools/src/main/kotlin/dev/kestrel/datatools/AndroidDataPort.kt`
- Modify: `core/datatools/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml` (replaced whole)
- Test: `core/datatools/src/test/kotlin/dev/kestrel/datatools/notifications/NotificationLinesTest.kt`, `core/datatools/src/androidTest/kotlin/dev/kestrel/datatools/DataToolsTest.kt`
- Modify: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-12-kestrel-design.md` (11.5's `list_notifications` row, 13.6's notification-access row and last bullet, B6, and B61)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: plan 5A's `DataPort` and its types; Tasks 1 to 4's tools and `IntentSpecs`.
- Produces: `class AndroidDataPort(context: Context, open: suspend (Intent) -> Boolean, isAgentFree: (String?) -> Boolean, zone: () -> ZoneId = ZoneId::systemDefault) : DataPort` (package `dev.kestrel.datatools`); package `dev.kestrel.datatools.notifications`: `class KestrelNotificationListener : NotificationListenerService` with `companion object { val connected: StateFlow<Boolean>; fun component(context: Context): ComponentName; fun hasAccess(context: Context): Boolean; fun accessSettings(context: Context): Intent }`, `object NotificationLines { const val MAX = 20; const val MESSAGES = 5; const val HIDDEN_TEXT: String; const val HIDDEN_NOTE: String; fun lines(all: List<NotificationFacts>, ownPackage: String, isAgentFree: (String?) -> Boolean, sdk: Int, zone: ZoneId): List<DataLine> }` and the internal `NotificationFacts`.

Design D9 and D12 (research r54). `list_notifications` reads Android's notification listener, `KestrelNotificationListener` (declared in `:core:datatools`' manifest with `BIND_NOTIFICATION_LISTENER_SERVICE`), only after `onListenerConnected`, from `getActiveNotifications()`: at most 20 notifications, newest first, each with the app's label, the time, the title, and the text from `EXTRA_MESSAGES` (the last five messages with their senders), else `EXTRA_BIG_TEXT`, else `EXTRA_TEXT_LINES`, else `EXTRA_TEXT`, with `EXTRA_SUB_TEXT`, every value read as a nullable `CharSequence`. Notifications of agent-free apps and of Kestrel itself, and group summaries (which repeat their children), are left out. On Android 15 to 17 a notification that the system marks as sensitive arrives as "Sensitive notification content hidden"; Kestrel passes that text on with the note "(Android hides this notification's content)" and never reads it another way; on Android 13 the listener gets the full text, so the redaction of `:core:agent` is the only protection there. Without notification access the tool gives `NeedsAccess(NOTIFICATIONS)`, and the agent hands over with kind `ACCESS` (Task 13 opens `accessSettings` and ends the hand-over when `connected` turns true). `AndroidDataPort` puts Tasks 1 to 5's tools behind plan 5A's `DataPort`; Task 14 wires it into `AppGraph`. The last step checks on kestrel-api37 whether Android 17 treats notification access as a restricted setting after `scripts\install.ps1`, and records the answer for the controller; the spec and the checklist step (Task 15) say how to allow restricted settings in either case.

Counts: `:core:datatools` JVM N + 3 (`NotificationLinesTest`); `:core:datatools` device N + 1 (`DataToolsTest`); the rest unchanged.

```kotlin
package dev.kestrel.datatools.notifications

import dev.kestrel.agent.port.DataField
import dev.kestrel.agent.port.DataLine
import dev.kestrel.datatools.DataLines
import java.time.ZoneId

/**
 * What `list_notifications` reads of one notification (design D9 of sub-project 5): its app, the time it was posted, and
 * its texts as Android's extras give them. Every text is untrusted; nothing of it is logged.
 */
internal data class NotificationFacts(
    val packageName: String,
    val appLabel: String?,
    val postTime: Long,
    val title: String?,
    val messages: List<Pair<String?, String?>>,
    val bigText: String?,
    val textLines: List<String>,
    val text: String?,
    val subText: String?,
) {
    override fun toString() = "NotificationFacts(messages=${messages.size}, lines=${textLines.size})"
}

/**
 * The lines of `list_notifications` (design D9 of sub-project 5; research r54): at most [MAX], newest first, without
 * Kestrel's own and those of agent-free apps; each with its time in Kestrel's words and the app, the title, the text and
 * the sub-text as untrusted fields. Pure, for the JVM tests.
 */
object NotificationLines {
    const val MAX = 20

    /** The newest messages of a messaging notification that a line holds. */
    const val MESSAGES = 5

    /** The text that Android 15 to 17 give an untrusted listener for a notification that they mark as sensitive. */
    const val HIDDEN_TEXT = "Sensitive notification content hidden"
    const val HIDDEN_NOTE = "(Android hides this notification's content)"

    internal fun lines(all: List<NotificationFacts>, ownPackage: String, isAgentFree: (String?) -> Boolean, sdk: Int, zone: ZoneId): List<DataLine> =
        all.filter { it.packageName != ownPackage && !isAgentFree(it.packageName) }
            .sortedByDescending { it.postTime }
            .take(MAX)
            .map { line(it, sdk, zone) }

    private fun line(facts: NotificationFacts, sdk: Int, zone: ZoneId): DataLine {
        val hidden = sdk >= 35 && (facts.text == HIDDEN_TEXT || facts.messages.any { it.second == HIDDEN_TEXT })
        val fixed = "notification · ${DataLines.time(facts.postTime, zone)}" + if (hidden) " $HIDDEN_NOTE" else ""
        val texts = if (facts.messages.isNotEmpty()) {
            facts.messages.takeLast(MESSAGES).mapNotNull { (sender, text) ->
                text?.let { DataField("message", if (sender.isNullOrBlank()) it else "$sender: $it") }
            }
        } else {
            listOfNotNull(
                (facts.bigText?.takeIf { it.isNotBlank() } ?: facts.textLines.takeIf { it.isNotEmpty() }?.joinToString("\n") ?: facts.text)
                    ?.takeIf { it.isNotBlank() }?.let { DataField("text", it) },
            )
        }
        val head = listOfNotNull(
            DataField("app", facts.appLabel ?: facts.packageName),
            facts.title?.takeIf { it.isNotBlank() }?.let { DataField("title", it) },
        )
        return DataLine(fixed, head + texts + listOfNotNull(facts.subText?.takeIf { it.isNotBlank() }?.let { DataField("sub", it) }))
    }
}
```

Create `core/datatools/src/main/kotlin/dev/kestrel/datatools/notifications/KestrelNotificationListener.kt`:

```kotlin
package dev.kestrel.datatools.notifications

import android.app.Notification
import android.app.NotificationManager
import android.content.ComponentName
import android.content.Context
import android.content.Intent
import android.content.pm.PackageManager
import android.os.Parcelable
import android.provider.Settings
import android.service.notification.NotificationListenerService
import android.service.notification.StatusBarNotification
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.MutableStateFlow
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.StateFlow
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.asStateFlow

/**
 * Kestrel's notification listener, which `list_notifications` reads (design D9 of sub-project 5). Android binds it only
 * after the owner gives notification access, and Kestrel reads it only after [onListenerConnected]. It keeps nothing and
 * logs nothing: each read takes the notifications that are active at that moment.
 */
class KestrelNotificationListener : NotificationListenerService() {
    override fun onListenerConnected() {
        instance = this
        state.value = true
    }

    override fun onListenerDisconnected() = forget()

    override fun onDestroy() {
        forget()
        super.onDestroy()
    }

    private fun forget() {
        if (instance === this) {
            instance = null
            state.value = false
        }
    }

    /** The active notifications without group summaries, which repeat their children. Off the main thread. */
    internal fun facts(): List<NotificationFacts> {
        val active = try {
            activeNotifications.orEmpty()
        } catch (e: SecurityException) {
            // Android disconnected the listener between the check and the read.
            return emptyList()
        }
        return active.filter { it.notification.flags and Notification.FLAG_GROUP_SUMMARY == 0 }.map(::facts)
    }

    private fun facts(sbn: StatusBarNotification): NotificationFacts {
        val extras = sbn.notification.extras
        val messages = extras.getParcelableArray(Notification.EXTRA_MESSAGES, Parcelable::class.java)
            ?.let { Notification.MessagingStyle.Message.getMessagesFromBundleArray(it) }
            .orEmpty()
            .map { it.senderPerson?.name?.toString() to it.text?.toString() }
        return NotificationFacts(
            packageName = sbn.packageName,
            appLabel = label(sbn.packageName),
            postTime = sbn.postTime,
            title = extras.getCharSequence(Notification.EXTRA_TITLE)?.toString(),
            messages = messages,
            bigText = extras.getCharSequence(Notification.EXTRA_BIG_TEXT)?.toString(),
            textLines = extras.getCharSequenceArray(Notification.EXTRA_TEXT_LINES)?.map { it.toString() }.orEmpty(),
            text = extras.getCharSequence(Notification.EXTRA_TEXT)?.toString(),
            subText = extras.getCharSequence(Notification.EXTRA_SUB_TEXT)?.toString(),
        )
    }

    private fun label(packageName: String): String? = try {
        packageManager.getApplicationLabel(packageManager.getApplicationInfo(packageName, PackageManager.ApplicationInfoFlags.of(0))).toString()
    } catch (e: PackageManager.NameNotFoundException) {
        null
    }

    companion object {
        @Volatile
        internal var instance: KestrelNotificationListener? = null
            private set

        private val state = MutableStateFlow(false)

        /** True while Android has the listener connected. */
        val connected: StateFlow<Boolean> = state.asStateFlow()

        fun component(context: Context): ComponentName = ComponentName(context, KestrelNotificationListener::class.java)

        /** Whether the owner gave Kestrel notification access. */
        fun hasAccess(context: Context): Boolean =
            context.getSystemService(NotificationManager::class.java).isNotificationListenerAccessGranted(component(context))

        /** Android's page of notification access for Kestrel's listener, from which the owner turns it on. */
        fun accessSettings(context: Context): Intent =
            Intent(Settings.ACTION_NOTIFICATION_LISTENER_DETAIL_SETTINGS)
                .putExtra(Settings.EXTRA_NOTIFICATION_LISTENER_COMPONENT_NAME, component(context).flattenToString())
                .addFlags(Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK)
    }
}
```

```kotlin
import dev.kestrel.datatools.calls.CallLogTool
import dev.kestrel.datatools.clock.ClockIntents
import dev.kestrel.datatools.contacts.AndroidContacts
import dev.kestrel.datatools.contacts.FindContact
import dev.kestrel.datatools.contacts.contactsAccess
import dev.kestrel.datatools.location.GpsLocation
import dev.kestrel.datatools.media.MediaKeys
import dev.kestrel.datatools.media.MediaTool
import dev.kestrel.datatools.navigation.NavigationIntents
import dev.kestrel.datatools.notifications.KestrelNotificationListener
import dev.kestrel.datatools.notifications.NotificationLines
import dev.kestrel.datatools.sms.SmsTool
import kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.first
import kotlinx.coroutines.withContext
import kotlinx.coroutines.withTimeoutOrNull
import java.time.DayOfWeek
import java.time.LocalDate
import java.time.LocalDateTime
import java.time.ZoneId

/**
 * The agent's data tools on Android (design D9 and D12 of sub-project 5): plan 5A's [DataPort] over Android's providers,
 * its location, its notification listener and the apps' intents. [open] starts an activity through Kestrel's accessibility
 * service (`ScreenActions.openIntent`), which Android allows while another app is in front; [isAgentFree] is the task's
 * list of agent-free apps, which `list_notifications` leaves out. A missing permission gives
 * [DataResult.NeedsPermission] with the permissions that the tool asks for together, and the agent asks the owner (D12).
 * Nothing here logs, and nothing starts a coroutine of its own.
 */
class AndroidDataPort(
    context: Context,
    private val open: suspend (Intent) -> Boolean,
    private val isAgentFree: (String?) -> Boolean,
    private val zone: () -> ZoneId = ZoneId::systemDefault,
) : DataPort {
    private val app = context.applicationContext ?: context
    private val resolver = app.contentResolver
    private val granted: (String) -> Boolean = { app.checkSelfPermission(it) == PackageManager.PERMISSION_GRANTED }
    private val contactsAllowed = contactsAccess(app)
    private val contacts = AndroidContacts(resolver)
    private val media = MediaTool(resolver, granted)
    private val calendar = CalendarTool(resolver, granted)
    private val sms = SmsTool(resolver, granted) { if (contactsAllowed.allowed()) contacts.read() else null }
    private val calls = CallLogTool(resolver, granted)
    private val location = GpsLocation(app.getSystemService(LocationManager::class.java), granted)
    private val keys = MediaKeys(app.getSystemService(AudioManager::class.java))

    override suspend fun findContact(name: String): DataResult {
        if (!contactsAllowed.allowed()) return DataResult.NeedsPermission(listOf(Manifest.permission.READ_CONTACTS))
        val all = try {
            withContext(Dispatchers.IO) { contacts.details() }
        } catch (e: SecurityException) {
            return DataResult.NeedsPermission(listOf(Manifest.permission.READ_CONTACTS))
        }
        return FindContact.result(name, all)
    }

    override suspend fun findMedia(from: LocalDate, until: LocalDate, kinds: MediaKinds): DataResult = media.find(from, until, kinds, zone())

    override suspend fun shareMedia(packageName: String, items: List<String>): DataResult {
        val unknown = media.unknown(items)
        if (items.isEmpty() || unknown.isNotEmpty()) return DataResult.Failed("there is no item ${unknown.firstOrNull() ?: ""} in this task; use find_media first")
        if (!open(media.shareIntent(packageName, items))) return DataResult.Failed(NOT_OPENED)
        return opened("Kestrel opened the share screen with ${items.distinct().size} items; choose the chat on the screen.", packageName)
    }

    override suspend fun listEvents(from: LocalDate, to: LocalDate): DataResult = calendar.list(from, to, zone())

    override suspend fun createEvent(title: String, start: LocalDateTime, end: LocalDateTime?, location: String?): DataResult =
        start(CalendarTool.insertIntent(title, start, end, location, zone()), "Kestrel opened the calendar's new event; tap Save to keep it.")

    override suspend fun setAlarm(hour: Int, minute: Int, label: String?, days: List<DayOfWeek>): DataResult =
        start(ClockIntents.alarm(hour, minute, label, days), "Kestrel asked the clock app to set an alarm for %02d:%02d.".format(hour, minute), wait = false)

    override suspend fun setTimer(seconds: Int, label: String?): DataResult =
        start(ClockIntents.timer(seconds, label), "Kestrel asked the clock app to set a timer of $seconds s.", wait = false)

    override suspend fun listNotifications(): DataResult {
        if (!KestrelNotificationListener.hasAccess(app)) return DataResult.NeedsAccess(AccessKind.NOTIFICATIONS)
        withTimeoutOrNull(CONNECT_MILLIS) { KestrelNotificationListener.connected.first { it } }
        val listener = KestrelNotificationListener.instance ?: return DataResult.Failed("Android has not connected Kestrel's notification listener yet")
        val facts = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) { listener.facts() }
        return DataResult.Ok(NotificationLines.lines(facts, app.packageName, isAgentFree, Build.VERSION.SDK_INT, zone()))
    }

    override suspend fun listSms(from: String?, limit: Int): DataResult = sms.list(from, limit, zone())

    override suspend fun composeSms(number: String, text: String): DataResult =
        start(SmsTool.composeIntent(number, text), "Kestrel opened a new SMS with the text; it is not sent.")

    override suspend fun listCalls(limit: Int): DataResult = calls.list(limit, zone())

    override suspend fun getLocation(): DataResult = location.current()

    override suspend fun mediaControl(action: MediaAction): DataResult = keys.press(action)

    override suspend fun navigate(app: NavigationApp, to: String, mode: TravelMode?): DataResult {
        if (app == NavigationApp.WAZE && installed(NavigationIntents.WAZE)) {
            if (!open(IntentSpecs.toIntent(NavigationIntents.waze(to)))) return DataResult.Failed(NOT_OPENED)
            return opened(NavigationIntents.WAZE_RESULT, NavigationIntents.WAZE)
        }
        val spec = NavigationIntents.googleMaps(to, mode) ?: return DataResult.Failed(NavigationIntents.MAPS_NEEDS_ADDRESS)
        if (!installed(NavigationIntents.GOOGLE_MAPS)) return DataResult.Failed("neither Waze nor Google Maps is installed")
        if (!open(IntentSpecs.toIntent(spec))) return DataResult.Failed(NOT_OPENED)
        val fellBack = if (app == NavigationApp.WAZE) "Waze is not installed, so Kestrel used Google Maps. " else ""
        return opened(fellBack + NavigationIntents.MAPS_RESULT, NavigationIntents.GOOGLE_MAPS)
    }

    override fun forgetTask() = media.forget()

    /** Starts [intent] and reports [done]; with [wait], the package that opens it goes to `ScreenPort.waitForFront`. */
    private suspend fun start(intent: Intent, done: String, wait: Boolean = true): DataResult {
        val target = if (wait) withContext(Dispatchers.IO) { IntentSpecs.resolve(app.packageManager, intent) } else null
        if (!open(intent)) return DataResult.Failed(NOT_OPENED)
        return opened(done, target)
    }

    private fun opened(done: String, packageName: String?): DataResult = DataResult.Ok(listOf(DataLine(done, emptyList())), opened = packageName)

    private fun installed(packageName: String): Boolean = app.packageManager.getLaunchIntentForPackage(packageName) != null

    override fun toString(): String = "AndroidDataPort($media)"

    private companion object {
        const val NOT_OPENED = "the app did not open"

        // Android binds the listener shortly after access is given; a read waits at most this long for it.
        const val CONNECT_MILLIS = 2_000L
    }
}
```

### Task 6: Kestrel's own actions and the owner's finger: the probe, `OwnActions`, `OwnerSignal` and the watcher's start

**Files:**
- Create: `core/screen/src/main/kotlin/dev/kestrel/screen/act/OwnActions.kt`, `core/screen/src/main/kotlin/dev/kestrel/screen/act/OwnerSignal.kt`
- Modify: `core/screen/src/main/kotlin/dev/kestrel/screen/act/ScreenActions.kt`, `core/screen/src/main/kotlin/dev/kestrel/screen/overlay/TouchWatcher.kt` (replaced whole), `core/screen/src/main/kotlin/dev/kestrel/screen/ScreenSession.kt`
- Create: `testapp/src/main/kotlin/dev/kestrel/testapp/PressActivity.kt`; Modify: `testapp/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml` (below `<!-- sub-project 5B: fixtures -->`)
- Test: `core/screen/src/test/kotlin/dev/kestrel/screen/act/OwnActionsRulesTest.kt`, `core/screen/src/test/kotlin/dev/kestrel/screen/act/OwnerSignalTest.kt`, `app/src/androidTest/kotlin/dev/kestrel/app/screen/OwnActionsTest.kt`
- Modify: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-12-kestrel-design.md` (14.1's "Detection" and the bullet after it)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `GestureRunner.isRunning()`, `OverlayHost.show(...): Boolean`, `ScreenChangeTracker`, `ScreenServiceRule`, `TestFinger`.
- Produces (package `dev.kestrel.screen.act`): `@Serializable enum class TouchRule { NONE, FIELD, CREDITS }`, `@Serializable enum class TouchBranch { A, B }`, `@Serializable data class TouchSource(val rule: TouchRule, val branch: TouchBranch = TouchBranch.A)` with `TouchSource.defaultFor(sdk: Int)`, `data class Touch(val owner: Boolean, val deviceId: Int, val source: Int, val toolType: Int, val flags: Int, val sinceNodeActionMillis: Long?, val credited: Boolean)`, `class OwnActions internal constructor(clock: () -> Long, sdk: Int)` with `var source: TouchSource`, `fun clear()`, `enum class Kind { CLICK, LONG_CLICK, SCROLL, SET_TEXT, FOCUS, OTHER }` and `companion object { const val CREDIT_MILLIS = 400L; const val OWN_WINDOW_TAIL_MILLIS = 300L; const val LATE_ECHO_MILLIS = 1_000L; const val SIGNAL_DEVICE = -2; val ECHOING: Set<Kind>; fun kindOf(action: Int): Kind; fun signal(): Touch }`, the internal `node`, `begin`, `end`, `busy`, `watching`, `classify`, `gestureCancelled` and `report`; `internal object OwnerSignal { fun counts(eventType: Int, packageName: String?, ownPackage: String, focusedField: Boolean, busy: Boolean): Boolean }`. `ScreenSession`: `suspend fun startTouchWatcher(): Boolean`, and below `// sub-project 5B`: `var touchSource: TouchSource`, `val touches: SharedFlow<Touch>`, `fun forgetOwnActions()`. `:testapp`'s `PressActivity` ("Press fixture": buttons "Stubborn", which acts on a click and answers it with false, and "Deaf", which refuses the click action; the status "Pressed <n>").

Design D19; deferred items 22 to 25 (D32). Spec 14.1's rule stays: the owner's finger cancels a running task, Kestrel's own actions never do. But on kestrel-api37 (Android 17) a click through `performAction(ACTION_CLICK)` reaches the input system as a touch from the touchscreen (device 0, source 4098), which the watcher reports as the owner's (plan 3C's final fix), so without a change the agent's first click would cancel its own task. `ScreenActions` now reports every node action, gesture and settle wait to `OwnActions`, and the touch watcher classifies each touch by a rule chosen per device (`TouchSource`, which Task 18's hook `agent-touch-source` stores): rule 1, the virtual device's touches while a gesture of Kestrel's runs and 100 ms after it, as today; `FIELD`, the touches that carry `MotionEvent`'s accessibility flag, only on Android 17 and later, because on 13 to 16 a real touch during a gesture carries it too (B35), and as `CREDITS` below that; `CREDITS`, the default above Android 13, one credit per accepted click or long click while the watcher runs, which lives 400 ms after the call returned and is used by the first touch inside it; a refused click creates none; starting the watcher, showing a card (Task 7) and asking a question (`forgetOwnActions`, Task 13) clear every credit; every other touch is the owner's, and `ScreenSession.touches` gives its delay since Kestrel's last node action, so that `AgentRunner` (Task 12) logs a possible late echo. `NONE` is the default on Android 13, where no click of Kestrel's is known to echo; the A71's first sitting runs the probe and sets its rule. On Android 13 to 15, a gesture of Kestrel's that ends as cancelled was cancelled by a finger, so it counts as the owner's touch (D32 item 22). Branch B (spec 14.1's fallback, for a device whose watcher misses a real finger): `OwnerSignal` counts a click or long click of any element, or a text change of a focused field, in another app's window, outside every action of Kestrel's and its settle wait, as the owner's touch; a scroll never counts, because apps scroll by themselves. `TouchWatcher.start()` and `ScreenSession.startTouchWatcher()` now say whether the watcher's window was added (D32 item 24), and `AgentRunner` refuses a task without it. The probe (`OwnActionsTest.probeRecordsWhatKestrelsActionsLookLikeToTheWatcher`) records, for each kind of node action that Kestrel performs (through Kestrel's own service, without `OwnActions`), for a refused click, a gesture, the test's virtual touchscreen and `adb shell input tap`, whether a touch reaches the watcher, with its device, source, tool type, flags and delay; it writes one line per case to logcat with the tag `KestrelProbe` (numbers only), and on API 34 and later fails when a kind outside `OwnActions.ECHOING` or a refused click reaches the watcher, or an echo comes later than half of a credit's life. If it fails, stop and report its lines to the controller, because the credit rule would then hide or miss touches.

Counts: `:core:screen` JVM N + 13 (`OwnActionsRulesTest` 10, `OwnerSignalTest` 3); `:app` device tests, screen package, N + 3 (`OwnActionsTest`); the rest unchanged.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing JVM tests**

Create `core/screen/src/test/kotlin/dev/kestrel/screen/act/OwnActionsRulesTest.kt`:

```kotlin
package dev.kestrel.screen.act

import android.view.KeyCharacterMap
import android.view.accessibility.AccessibilityNodeInfo
import org.junit.Assert.assertEquals
import org.junit.Assert.assertFalse
import org.junit.Assert.assertTrue
import org.junit.Test

class OwnActionsRulesTest {
    private var now = 1_000L

    private fun own(sdk: Int = 37, rule: TouchRule? = null) = OwnActions({ now }, sdk).also { own ->
        rule?.let { own.source = TouchSource(it) }
        own.watching(true)
    }

    // A touch of the owner's finger on the touchscreen, or an echo of Kestrel's click, which looks the same on Android 17.
    private fun touch(own: OwnActions, flags: Int = 0) = own.classify(deviceId = 0, inputSource = 4098, toolType = 1, flags = flags, gestureRunning = false)

    @Test
    fun theDefaultRuleIsNoneOnAndroid13AndCreditsAboveIt() {
        assertEquals(TouchSource(TouchRule.NONE, TouchBranch.A), TouchSource.defaultFor(33))
        assertEquals(TouchSource(TouchRule.CREDITS, TouchBranch.A), TouchSource.defaultFor(34))
        assertEquals(TouchSource(TouchRule.CREDITS, TouchBranch.A), TouchSource.defaultFor(37))
    }

    @Test
    fun theVirtualDevicesTouchDuringKestrelsGestureIsKestrelsByEveryRule() {
        for (rule in TouchRule.entries) {
            val own = own(rule = rule)
            assertFalse(rule.name, own.classify(KeyCharacterMap.VIRTUAL_KEYBOARD, 4098, 1, 0, gestureRunning = true).owner)
            assertTrue(rule.name, own.classify(KeyCharacterMap.VIRTUAL_KEYBOARD, 4098, 1, 0, gestureRunning = false).owner)
            assertTrue(rule.name, own.classify(0, 4098, 1, 0, gestureRunning = true).owner)
        }
    }

    @Test
    fun anAcceptedClickGivesOneCreditThatItsEchoUses() {
        val own = own()
        assertTrue(own.node(OwnActions.Kind.CLICK) { true })
        now += 50

        val echo = touch(own)
        assertFalse(echo.owner)
        assertTrue(echo.credited)
        assertEquals(50L, echo.sinceNodeActionMillis)
        // One credit per click: the next touch is the owner's.
        assertTrue(touch(own).owner)
    }

    @Test
    fun anEchoThatComesWhileTheClickStillRunsUsesItsCredit() {
        val own = own()
        var echo: Touch? = null

        own.node(OwnActions.Kind.LONG_CLICK) {
            echo = touch(own)
            true
        }

        assertFalse(checkNotNull(echo).owner)
        assertTrue(touch(own).owner)
    }

    @Test
    fun aCreditEndsAfterItsTimeAndALateEchoIsTheOwnersWithItsDelay() {
        val own = own()
        own.node(OwnActions.Kind.CLICK) { true }
        now += OwnActions.CREDIT_MILLIS + 1

        val late = touch(own)
        assertTrue(late.owner)
        assertEquals(OwnActions.CREDIT_MILLIS + 1, late.sinceNodeActionMillis)
    }

    @Test
    fun aRefusedClickAndTheKindsThatDoNotEchoGiveNoCredit() {
        val own = own()

        own.node(OwnActions.Kind.CLICK) { false }
        own.node(OwnActions.Kind.SCROLL) { true }
        own.node(OwnActions.Kind.SET_TEXT) { true }
        own.node(OwnActions.Kind.FOCUS) { true }

        assertTrue(touch(own).owner)
        assertEquals(OwnActions.Kind.CLICK, OwnActions.kindOf(AccessibilityNodeInfo.ACTION_CLICK))
        assertEquals(OwnActions.Kind.FOCUS, OwnActions.kindOf(AccessibilityNodeInfo.ACTION_FOCUS))
        assertEquals(setOf(OwnActions.Kind.CLICK, OwnActions.Kind.LONG_CLICK), OwnActions.ECHOING)
    }

    @Test
    fun startingTheWatcherOrClearingForgetsTheCreditsAndNoneComeWhileItIsOff() {
        val own = own()
        own.node(OwnActions.Kind.CLICK) { true }
        own.watching(true)
        assertTrue("a start forgets the credits", touch(own).owner)

        own.node(OwnActions.Kind.CLICK) { true }
        own.clear()
        assertTrue("a card or a question forgets the credits", touch(own).owner)

        own.watching(false)
        own.node(OwnActions.Kind.CLICK) { true }
        own.watching(true)
        assertTrue("an action made before the watcher ran hides no touch", touch(own).owner)
    }

    @Test
    fun theFieldRuleUsesTheAccessibilityFlagFromAndroid17AndCreditsBelowIt() {
        val field = own(sdk = 37, rule = TouchRule.FIELD)
        assertFalse(touch(field, flags = 0x800).owner)
        assertTrue(touch(field).owner)

        val older = own(sdk = 35, rule = TouchRule.FIELD)
        assertTrue("a real touch during a gesture carries the flag on Android 13 to 16", touch(older, flags = 0x800).owner)
        older.node(OwnActions.Kind.CLICK) { true }
        assertFalse(touch(older).owner)

        val none = own(sdk = 37, rule = TouchRule.NONE)
        none.node(OwnActions.Kind.CLICK) { true }
        assertTrue(touch(none).owner)
    }

    @Test
    fun kestrelIsBusyDuringItsActionsAndShortlyAfterThem() {
        val own = own()
        assertFalse(own.busy())

        own.begin()
        assertTrue(own.busy())
        own.end()
        assertTrue(own.busy())
        now += OwnActions.OWN_WINDOW_TAIL_MILLIS
        assertFalse(own.busy())

        own.node(OwnActions.Kind.SCROLL) { true }
        assertTrue(own.busy())
    }

    @Test
    fun aCancelledGestureIsTheOwnersTouchUpToAndroid15WhileTheWatcherRuns() {
        val reported = mutableListOf<Touch>()

        own(sdk = 35).apply { report = { reported += it } }.gestureCancelled()
        assertEquals(listOf(OwnActions.signal()), reported)
        assertTrue(reported.single().owner)

        own(sdk = 36).apply { report = { reported += it } }.gestureCancelled()
        own(sdk = 33).apply { report = { reported += it }; watching(false) }.gestureCancelled()
        assertEquals(1, reported.size)
    }
}
```

```kotlin
package dev.kestrel.screen.act

import android.view.KeyCharacterMap
import android.view.accessibility.AccessibilityNodeInfo
import kotlinx.serialization.Serializable

/**
 * How the touch watcher tells an echo of Kestrel's own action from the owner's finger on a device (design D19 of
 * sub-project 5). Under every rule, a touch of the virtual input device while one of Kestrel's gestures runs, or within
 * 100 ms after it, is Kestrel's.
 */
@Serializable
enum class TouchRule {
    /** Nothing else is Kestrel's: Android 13's default, where no click of Kestrel's is known to reach the watcher. */
    NONE,

    /**
     * Also every touch that carries `MotionEvent`'s accessibility flag, from Android 17 on; on Android 13 to 16 a real
     * touch during a gesture carries it too (B35), so there this rule works as [CREDITS].
     */
    FIELD,

    /** Also one touch per accepted click or long click of Kestrel's, within [OwnActions.CREDIT_MILLIS] after the call. */
    CREDITS,
}

/**
 * Whether the touch watcher sees the owner's finger on a device ([A]), or whether Kestrel also needs spec 14.1's fallback
 * of the screen events that it did not cause ([B]). The A71's first sitting chooses it (design D19 of sub-project 5).
 */
@Serializable
enum class TouchBranch { A, B }

/** A device's rule and branch, which the debug hook `agent-touch-source` stores per device. */
@Serializable
data class TouchSource(val rule: TouchRule, val branch: TouchBranch = TouchBranch.A) {
    companion object {
        /** [TouchRule.NONE] on Android 13, and [TouchRule.CREDITS] above it until a probe there says otherwise. */
        fun defaultFor(sdk: Int): TouchSource = TouchSource(if (sdk <= 33) TouchRule.NONE else TouchRule.CREDITS)
    }
}

/**
 * One touch that the watcher saw, as the rule classified it: whether it is the [owner]'s, its input [deviceId] (or
 * [OwnActions.SIGNAL_DEVICE] for a signal without a touch), [source], [toolType] and [flags], the time since Kestrel's last
 * node action returned ([sinceNodeActionMillis], null when none ran while the watcher ran), and whether a credit took it.
 * It holds no screen content.
 */
data class Touch(
    val owner: Boolean,
    val deviceId: Int,
    val source: Int,
    val toolType: Int,
    val flags: Int,
    val sinceNodeActionMillis: Long?,
    val credited: Boolean,
)

/**
 * Kestrel's own actions while the touch watcher runs (design D19 of sub-project 5): `ScreenActions` reports each node
 * action, gesture and settle wait here, and the watcher asks [classify] about each touch. With [TouchRule.CREDITS], each
 * accepted click or long click ([ECHOING]) while the watcher runs creates one credit, which lives from the call until
 * [CREDIT_MILLIS] after it returned; the first touch inside that time uses it and is Kestrel's. A refused call creates
 * none. Starting the watcher and [clear] forget every credit, so that an action made before can never hide the owner's
 * touch. [busy] tells `OwnerSignal` that Kestrel is acting or settling. Any thread may call it.
 */
class OwnActions internal constructor(private val clock: () -> Long, private val sdk: Int) {
    enum class Kind { CLICK, LONG_CLICK, SCROLL, SET_TEXT, FOCUS, OTHER }

    @Volatile
    var source: TouchSource = TouchSource.defaultFor(sdk)

    /** Where a touch of the owner's that no input event carries goes: the watcher's report. */
    @Volatile
    internal var report: (Touch) -> Unit = {}

    private class Credit {
        var until = Long.MAX_VALUE
        var used = false
    }

    private val lock = Any()
    private val credits = mutableListOf<Credit>()
    private var acting = 0
    private var quietFrom = Long.MIN_VALUE
    private var lastNodeAction: Long? = null
    private var watching = false

    /** The watcher started (true) or stopped; either forgets every credit. */
    internal fun watching(on: Boolean) = synchronized(lock) {
        watching = on
        credits.clear()
        if (!on) lastNodeAction = null
    }

    /** Forgets every credit, as when a card shows or a question is asked (design D19 rule 3). */
    fun clear() = synchronized(lock) { credits.clear() }

    /** Runs [perform], a node action of [kind], as Kestrel's own, and returns its answer. */
    internal fun node(kind: Kind, perform: () -> Boolean): Boolean {
        val credit = synchronized(lock) {
            acting++
            if (watching && kind in ECHOING && credits()) Credit().also { credits += it } else null
        }
        var accepted = false
        try {
            accepted = perform()
            return accepted
        } finally {
            synchronized(lock) {
                val now = clock()
                acting--
                quietFrom = maxOf(quietFrom, now + OWN_WINDOW_TAIL_MILLIS)
                if (watching) lastNodeAction = now
                if (credit != null) {
                    if (!accepted && !credit.used) credits.remove(credit) else credit.until = now + CREDIT_MILLIS
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /** A gesture or a settle wait of Kestrel's begins; each [begin] needs its [end]. */
    internal fun begin() = synchronized(lock) { acting++ }

    internal fun end() = synchronized(lock) {
        acting--
        quietFrom = maxOf(quietFrom, clock() + OWN_WINDOW_TAIL_MILLIS)
    }

    /** Whether Kestrel acts now, or acted less than [OWN_WINDOW_TAIL_MILLIS] ago. */
    internal fun busy(): Boolean = synchronized(lock) { acting > 0 || clock() < quietFrom }

    /** Classifies a touch that starts outside the watcher's window. */
    internal fun classify(deviceId: Int, inputSource: Int, toolType: Int, flags: Int, gestureRunning: Boolean): Touch = synchronized(lock) {
        val now = clock()
        val since = lastNodeAction?.let { now - it }
        fun touch(owner: Boolean, credited: Boolean = false) = Touch(owner, deviceId, inputSource, toolType, flags, since, credited)
        if (gestureRunning && deviceId == KeyCharacterMap.VIRTUAL_KEYBOARD) return touch(owner = false)
        if (source.rule == TouchRule.FIELD && sdk >= FIELD_SDK && flags and ACCESSIBILITY_FLAG != 0) return touch(owner = false)
        if (credits()) {
            credits.removeAll { !it.used && it.until < now }
            val credit = credits.firstOrNull { !it.used }
            if (credit != null) {
                credit.used = true
                credits.remove(credit)
                return touch(owner = false, credited = true)
            }
        }
        touch(owner = true)
    }

    /**
     * One of Kestrel's gestures ended as cancelled: on Android 13 to 15 only a touch on the screen does that, so it counts
     * as the owner's touch on both branches (design D19 of sub-project 5; B35).
     */
    internal fun gestureCancelled() {
        val watched = synchronized(lock) { watching }
        if (watched && sdk <= LAST_CANCELLING_SDK) report(signal())
    }

    private fun credits(): Boolean = source.rule == TouchRule.CREDITS || (source.rule == TouchRule.FIELD && sdk < FIELD_SDK)

    override fun toString(): String = "OwnActions(source=$source, credits=${synchronized(lock) { credits.size }})"

    companion object {
        /** How long after Kestrel's click returned its echo may use its credit: twice the probe's bound of an echo's delay. */
        const val CREDIT_MILLIS = 400L

        /** How long after an action of Kestrel's the screen's events are still its own, for `OwnerSignal`. */
        const val OWN_WINDOW_TAIL_MILLIS = 300L

        /** An owner's touch this soon after Kestrel's last node action may be a late echo; the activity log says so. */
        const val LATE_ECHO_MILLIS = 1_000L

        /** The device of a touch that no input event carried: a signal of branch B or a cancelled gesture. */
        const val SIGNAL_DEVICE = -2

        /** The kinds whose echo reaches the watcher on Android 17 (plan 3C's evidence, which the probe checks). */
        val ECHOING: Set<Kind> = setOf(Kind.CLICK, Kind.LONG_CLICK)

        private const val FIELD_SDK = 37
        private const val LAST_CANCELLING_SDK = 35

        // MotionEvent.FLAG_IS_ACCESSIBILITY_EVENT.
        private const val ACCESSIBILITY_FLAG = 0x800

        fun kindOf(action: Int): Kind = when (action) {
            AccessibilityNodeInfo.ACTION_CLICK -> Kind.CLICK
            AccessibilityNodeInfo.ACTION_LONG_CLICK -> Kind.LONG_CLICK
            AccessibilityNodeInfo.ACTION_SET_TEXT -> Kind.SET_TEXT
            AccessibilityNodeInfo.ACTION_FOCUS -> Kind.FOCUS
            AccessibilityNodeInfo.ACTION_SCROLL_FORWARD, AccessibilityNodeInfo.ACTION_SCROLL_BACKWARD -> Kind.SCROLL
            else -> Kind.OTHER
        }

        /** The owner's touch that a signal found, without an input event. */
        fun signal(): Touch = Touch(owner = true, deviceId = SIGNAL_DEVICE, source = 0, toolType = 0, flags = 0, sinceNodeActionMillis = null, credited = false)
    }
}
```

```kotlin
package dev.kestrel.screen.act

import android.view.accessibility.AccessibilityEvent

/**
 * Branch B of design D19 of sub-project 5 (spec 14.1's fallback for a device whose touch watcher misses a real finger):
 * a click or a long click of any element, or a text change of a focused field, in another app's window, while Kestrel
 * neither acts nor settles, is the owner's touch. A scroll never counts, because apps scroll by themselves.
 */
internal object OwnerSignal {
    fun counts(eventType: Int, packageName: String?, ownPackage: String, focusedField: Boolean, busy: Boolean): Boolean {
        if (busy || packageName == null || packageName == ownPackage) return false
        return when (eventType) {
            AccessibilityEvent.TYPE_VIEW_CLICKED, AccessibilityEvent.TYPE_VIEW_LONG_CLICKED -> true
            AccessibilityEvent.TYPE_VIEW_TEXT_CHANGED -> focusedField
            else -> false
        }
    }
}
```

```kotlin
package dev.kestrel.testapp

import android.app.Activity
import android.content.Context
import android.os.Bundle
import android.view.accessibility.AccessibilityNodeInfo
import android.widget.Button
import android.widget.TextView

/**
 * Two buttons for Kestrel's own actions and its press policy (design D19 and D32 item 29 of sub-project 5): "Stubborn"
 * acts on a click but answers the click action with false, as some apps do, and "Deaf" refuses the click action and acts
 * only on a touch. The status says how often they were pressed.
 */
class PressActivity : Activity() {
    private lateinit var status: TextView
    private var presses = 0

    override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
        super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
        val page = fixturePage("Press fixture")
        status = page.addStatus()
        page.addView(StubbornButton(this).apply {
            text = "Stubborn"
            setOnClickListener { pressed() }
        })
        page.addView(DeafButton(this).apply {
            text = "Deaf"
            setOnClickListener { pressed() }
        })
    }

    private fun pressed() {
        presses++
        report("Pressed $presses")
    }

    private fun report(text: String) {
        status.text = text
    }
}

/** Performs the click, but tells accessibility services that it did not. */
class StubbornButton(context: Context) : Button(context) {
    override fun performAccessibilityAction(action: Int, arguments: Bundle?): Boolean {
        if (action != AccessibilityNodeInfo.ACTION_CLICK) return super.performAccessibilityAction(action, arguments)
        performClick()
        return false
    }
}

/** Refuses the click action, so that only a touch presses it. */
class DeafButton(context: Context) : Button(context) {
    override fun performAccessibilityAction(action: Int, arguments: Bundle?): Boolean =
        action != AccessibilityNodeInfo.ACTION_CLICK && super.performAccessibilityAction(action, arguments)
}
```

```kotlin
package dev.kestrel.app.screen

import android.os.Build
import android.os.Bundle
import android.os.SystemClock
import android.util.Log
import android.view.accessibility.AccessibilityNodeInfo
import androidx.test.ext.junit.runners.AndroidJUnit4
import dev.kestrel.app.screen.ScreenServiceRule.Companion.FIXTURES
import dev.kestrel.screen.act.ActionMethod
import dev.kestrel.screen.act.ActionResult
import dev.kestrel.screen.act.OwnActions
import dev.kestrel.screen.act.Touch
import dev.kestrel.screen.model.ScreenElement
import kotlinx.coroutines.CoroutineStart
import kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers
import kotlinx.coroutines.channels.Channel
import kotlinx.coroutines.coroutineScope
import kotlinx.coroutines.delay
import kotlinx.coroutines.launch
import kotlinx.coroutines.runBlocking
import kotlinx.coroutines.withContext
import kotlinx.coroutines.withTimeout
import org.junit.Assert.assertEquals
import org.junit.Assert.assertFalse
import org.junit.Assert.assertTrue
import org.junit.Rule
import org.junit.Test
import org.junit.runner.RunWith
import java.util.Locale

/**
 * Kestrel's own actions and the owner's finger (design D19 of sub-project 5): the probe of what Kestrel's actions look
 * like to the touch watcher on this device, and the rule that keeps a click's echo from cancelling a task while the
 * finger still does.
 */
@RunWith(AndroidJUnit4::class)
class OwnActionsTest {
    @get:Rule
    val screen = ScreenServiceRule()

    private val session get() = screen.session

    /** What reached the watcher within [PROBE_MILLIS] after one action of the probe returned, each with its delay. */
    private class Probe(val case: String, val touches: List<Pair<Touch, Long>>) {
        /** One line of numbers only, for logcat's tag KestrelProbe. */
        fun line(sdk: Int): String {
            val first = touches.firstOrNull()
            val touch = first?.first
            return "case=$case sdk=$sdk touches=${touches.size} device=${touch?.deviceId ?: "none"} source=${touch?.source ?: "none"} " +
                "tool=${touch?.toolType ?: "none"} flags=${touch?.flags?.let { "0x" + Integer.toHexString(it) } ?: "none"} delayMs=${first?.second ?: "none"}"
        }
    }

    private suspend fun probe(case: String, act: suspend () -> Unit): Probe = coroutineScope {
        val seen = Channel<Pair<Touch, Long>>(Channel.UNLIMITED)
        val collector = launch(start = CoroutineStart.UNDISPATCHED) { session.touches.collect { seen.send(it to SystemClock.uptimeMillis()) } }
        act()
        val returned = SystemClock.uptimeMillis()
        delay(PROBE_MILLIS)
        collector.cancel()
        seen.close()
        val touches = mutableListOf<Pair<Touch, Long>>()
        for ((touch, at) in seen) touches += touch to (at - returned)
        Probe(case, touches)
    }

    /** Performs [action] on the element's node through Kestrel's accessibility service, without OwnActions, and gives Android's answer. */
    private suspend fun perform(predicate: (ScreenElement) -> Boolean, action: Int, arguments: Bundle? = null): Boolean {
        val element = screen.awaitElement(predicate = predicate)
        val node = checkNotNull(session.snapshots.current().node(element.key))
        return withContext(Dispatchers.IO) { node.performAction(action, arguments) }
    }

    private fun id(name: String): (ScreenElement) -> Boolean = { it.viewId == "$FIXTURES:id/$name" }

    @Test
    fun probeRecordsWhatKestrelsActionsLookLikeToTheWatcher() = runBlocking {
        val probes = mutableListOf<Probe>()
        TestFinger(screen.automation).use { finger ->
            screen.open("ViewsActivity", "Views fixture")
            assertTrue(session.startTouchWatcher())
            screen.awaitInputWindow(WATCHER)
            probes += probe("click") { assertTrue(perform(id("send_button"), AccessibilityNodeInfo.ACTION_CLICK)) }
            probes += probe("long-click") { assertTrue(perform(id("send_button"), AccessibilityNodeInfo.ACTION_LONG_CLICK)) }
            val text = Bundle().apply { putCharSequence(AccessibilityNodeInfo.ACTION_ARGUMENT_SET_TEXT_CHARSEQUENCE, "probe") }
            probes += probe("set-text") { perform(id("message_field"), AccessibilityNodeInfo.ACTION_SET_TEXT, text) }
            probes += probe("ime-focus") { perform(id("strict_field"), AccessibilityNodeInfo.ACTION_FOCUS) }
            val target = screen.awaitElement { it.label == "Touch target" }.bounds
            probes += probe("gesture") { session.actions.tapAt(target.centerX, target.centerY) }
            probes += probe("finger") { finger.tap(target.centerX, target.centerY) }
            probes += probe("input-tap") { screen.shell("input tap ${target.centerX} ${target.centerY}") }
            screen.open("ScrollActivity", "Scroll fixture")
            probes += probe("scroll") { perform({ it.scrollable }, AccessibilityNodeInfo.ACTION_SCROLL_FORWARD) }
            screen.open("PressActivity", "Press fixture")
            probes += probe("refused-click") { assertFalse(perform({ it.label == "DEAF" }, AccessibilityNodeInfo.ACTION_CLICK)) }
        }
        val sdk = Build.VERSION.SDK_INT
        for (probe in probes) Log.i(TAG, probe.line(sdk))
        if (sdk >= 34) {
            // The credits are made for clicks and long clicks only, and live twice the longest echo's delay (D19).
            for (case in listOf("set-text", "ime-focus", "scroll", "refused-click")) {
                assertEquals("$case reached the watcher: ${probes.single { it.case == case }.line(sdk)}", 0, probes.single { it.case == case }.touches.size)
            }
            for (case in listOf("click", "long-click")) {
                for ((_, delayMillis) in probes.single { it.case == case }.touches) {
                    assertTrue(String.format(Locale.ROOT, "%s echoed after %d ms", case, delayMillis), delayMillis <= OwnActions.CREDIT_MILLIS / 2)
                }
            }
        }
    }

    @Test
    fun aFingerOneSecondAfterAnEchoedClickIsTheOwners() = runBlocking {
        TestFinger(screen.automation).use { finger ->
            screen.open("ViewsActivity", "Views fixture")
            val send = screen.awaitElement(predicate = id("send_button"))
            val target = screen.awaitElement { it.label == "Touch target" }.bounds
            assertTrue(session.startTouchWatcher())
            screen.awaitInputWindow(WATCHER)
            val owners = Channel<Unit>(Channel.UNLIMITED)
            val collector = launch(start = CoroutineStart.UNDISPATCHED) { session.ownerTouches.collect { owners.send(it) } }

            assertEquals(ActionResult.Done(ActionMethod.ACTION), session.actions.tap(send.key))
            screen.awaitElement { it.label == "Clicked Send" }
            delay(1_000)
            assertTrue("Kestrel's own click was reported as the owner's touch", owners.tryReceive().isFailure)

            finger.tap(target.centerX, target.centerY)
            withTimeout(3_000) { owners.receive() }
            collector.cancel()
        }
        Unit
    }

    @Test
    fun aFingerRightAfterTheWatcherStartsIsTheOwnersAfterAnEarlierClick() = runBlocking {
        TestFinger(screen.automation).use { finger ->
            screen.open("ViewsActivity", "Views fixture")
            val send = screen.awaitElement(predicate = id("send_button"))
            val target = screen.awaitElement { it.label == "Touch target" }.bounds
            assertTrue(session.startTouchWatcher())
            screen.awaitInputWindow(WATCHER)
            val owners = Channel<Unit>(Channel.UNLIMITED)
            val collector = launch(start = CoroutineStart.UNDISPATCHED) { session.ownerTouches.collect { owners.send(it) } }
            session.actions.tap(send.key)
            screen.awaitElement { it.label == "Clicked Send" }

            // As when a task starts the watcher again: what Kestrel did before can hide no touch of the owner's.
            session.stopTouchWatcher()
            assertTrue(session.startTouchWatcher())
            screen.awaitInputWindow(WATCHER)
            finger.tap(target.centerX, target.centerY)

            withTimeout(3_000) { owners.receive() }
            delay(500)
            assertTrue("More than the finger's touch was reported", owners.tryReceive().isFailure)
            collector.cancel()
        }
        Unit
    }

    private companion object {
        const val WATCHER = "Kestrel touch watcher"
        const val TAG = "KestrelProbe"
        const val PROBE_MILLIS = 1_000L
    }
}
```

```kotlin
package dev.kestrel.screen.overlay

import android.annotation.SuppressLint
import android.graphics.PixelFormat
import android.view.Gravity
import android.view.MotionEvent
import android.view.View
import android.view.WindowManager.LayoutParams
import dev.kestrel.screen.act.GestureRunner
import dev.kestrel.screen.act.OwnActions
import dev.kestrel.screen.act.Touch
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.MutableSharedFlow
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.SharedFlow
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.asSharedFlow

/**
 * An invisible window of one pixel that reports the owner's touches anywhere on the screen, so that a touch can
 * stop a running task (design spec, sections 9.4 and 14.1). Android tells the window about every touch that starts
 * outside it, unless the touch lands on a window above it, such as an overlay that Kestrel shows later. Use it on
 * the main thread.
 *
 * Android injects the touches of Kestrel's gestures from its virtual input device, while a finger's touches come
 * from the touchscreen, so the watcher leaves out touches from the virtual device while one of Kestrel's gestures
 * runs (spike S3). The device is the clue that works on every version: Android 13 to 15, and Android 16 before QPR2
 * depending on feature flags, mark a finger's touches as accessibility events while a gesture service is on, and from
 * Android 16 QPR2, Android no longer cancels Kestrel's gesture when a finger touches the screen (design spec, section
 * 14.1 and B35). On Android 17 a click of Kestrel's through a node action arrives as a touch from the touchscreen, so
 * [OwnActions] classifies each touch by the device's rule (design D19 of sub-project 5).
 */
internal class TouchWatcher(private val host: OverlayHost, private val gestures: GestureRunner, private val own: OwnActions) {
    private val touches = MutableSharedFlow<Unit>(extraBufferCapacity = 16)
    private val classified = MutableSharedFlow<Touch>(extraBufferCapacity = 64)

    /** Whether the watcher's window is on the screen. */
    @Volatile
    var running = false
        private set

    // On purpose: the watcher only listens for touches and offers no click action.
    @SuppressLint("ClickableViewAccessibility")
    private val view = View(host.context).apply {
        setOnTouchListener { _, event ->
            val starts = event.actionMasked == MotionEvent.ACTION_OUTSIDE || event.actionMasked == MotionEvent.ACTION_DOWN
            if (starts) report(own.classify(event.deviceId, event.source, event.getToolType(0), event.flags, gestures.isRunning()))
            false
        }
    }

    init {
        own.report = ::report
    }

    /** Emits when the owner touches the screen while the watcher runs. */
    val ownerTouches: SharedFlow<Unit> = touches.asSharedFlow()

    /** Every touch that the watcher classified, Kestrel's own too, and the owner's touches that a signal found. */
    val all: SharedFlow<Touch> = classified.asSharedFlow()

    /**
     * Starts watching and returns whether the watcher's window is on the screen. A second call only updates the window's
     * layout. Each start forgets Kestrel's earlier actions, so that none of them can hide the owner's touch.
     */
    fun start(): Boolean {
        val shown = host.show(view, params())
        running = shown
        own.watching(shown)
        return shown
    }

    fun stop() {
        host.hide(view)
        running = false
        own.watching(false)
    }

    /** Reports [touch], and the owner's touches also to [ownerTouches]. Any thread may call it. */
    fun report(touch: Touch) {
        classified.tryEmit(touch)
        if (touch.owner) touches.tryEmit(Unit)
    }

    private fun params() = LayoutParams(
        1,
        1,
        LayoutParams.TYPE_ACCESSIBILITY_OVERLAY,
        LayoutParams.FLAG_NOT_FOCUSABLE or LayoutParams.FLAG_NOT_TOUCH_MODAL or LayoutParams.FLAG_WATCH_OUTSIDE_TOUCH or
            LayoutParams.FLAG_LAYOUT_IN_SCREEN or LayoutParams.FLAG_LAYOUT_NO_LIMITS,
        PixelFormat.TRANSLUCENT,
    ).apply {
        gravity = Gravity.TOP or Gravity.START
        setTitle("Kestrel touch watcher")
    }
}
```

```kotlin
    // sub-project 5B

    /**
     * How the touch watcher tells an echo of Kestrel's own actions from the owner's finger on this device (design D19 of
     * sub-project 5): the rule, and branch B, on which a click or a text change that Kestrel did not cause also counts as
     * the owner's touch. Any thread may set it; the debug hook `agent-touch-source` stores it per device.
     */
    var touchSource: TouchSource
        get() = ownActions.source
        set(value) {
            ownActions.source = value
        }

    /** Every touch that the watcher classified, Kestrel's own and the owner's, for D19's probe and the activity log. */
    val touches: SharedFlow<Touch> get() = watcher.all

    /** Forgets Kestrel's earlier actions, so that none of them hides the owner's touch that answers a question (D19). */
    fun forgetOwnActions() = ownActions.clear()

    private val ownPackage: String = service.packageName

    /** Branch B of D19: a click or a text change in another app's window that Kestrel did not cause is the owner's touch. */
    private fun signalOwner(event: AccessibilityEvent) {
        if (ownActions.source.branch != TouchBranch.B || !watcher.running) return
        val focused = event.eventType == AccessibilityEvent.TYPE_VIEW_TEXT_CHANGED && event.source?.isFocused == true
        if (OwnerSignal.counts(event.eventType, event.packageName?.toString(), ownPackage, focused, ownActions.busy())) {
            watcher.report(OwnActions.signal())
        }
    }
```

```markdown
- **Detection.** The touch watcher (section 9.4) is an accessibility overlay of 1×1 pixel that asks Android to report touches outside it (`FLAG_WATCH_OUTSIDE_TOUCH`). Android injects Kestrel's own gestures from its virtual input device, while the owner's finger comes from the touchscreen. with
```

```markdown
- **Detection.** The touch watcher (section 9.4) is an accessibility overlay of 1×1 pixel that asks Android to report touches outside it (`FLAG_WATCH_OUTSIDE_TOUCH`); starting it reports whether its window was added, and a task does not run without it. Android injects Kestrel's own gestures from its virtual input device, while the owner's finger comes from the touchscreen. So the watcher ignores touches from the virtual device while one of Kestrel's gestures runs and for 100 ms after it. On Android 17, a click of Kestrel's through an accessibility action reaches the input system as a touch from the touchscreen (device 0), so every action of Kestrel's is reported to the watcher, which classifies each touch by a rule chosen per device: none more (Android 13's default); a field of the touch that a probe found to mark an echo (never `MotionEvent`'s accessibility flag on Android 13 to 16, where a real touch during a gesture carries it too); or credits (the default above Android 13): each accepted click or long click while the watcher runs creates one credit, which lives 400 ms after the call returned, and the first touch inside it is Kestrel's. Starting the watcher, showing a confirmation card and asking a question forget every credit, so that an earlier action never hides the owner's touch; a later echo counts as the owner's touch, and the activity log records it as a possible late echo. A device test, the probe, records for each kind of Kestrel's actions whether a touch reaches the watcher and its device, source, tool type, flags and delay; the A71 runs it in its first sitting. Every other touch is the owner's. On Android 13 to 15, the owner's touch also cancels Kestrel's running gesture, and a gesture of Kestrel's that ends as cancelled counts as the owner's touch.
```

```markdown
- If the A71 shows that the watcher does not receive a real finger's touches, Kestrel uses screen events that it did not cause (clicks, scrolls and text changes) as the signal instead.
```

with

```markdown
- If the A71 shows that the watcher does not receive a real finger's touches (its first sitting chooses this branch per device), Kestrel also counts as the owner's touch a click or a long click of any element, or a text change of a focused field, in another app's window, outside every action of Kestrel's and its settle wait. Scrolls never count, because apps scroll by themselves. The watcher still runs for the touches that it does see.
```

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: Task 6's `OwnActions` and `PressActivity`; `Uncovered`, `ScreenChangeTracker`, `SnapshotCache`.
- Produces (package `dev.kestrel.screen.act`): `enum class PressPolicy { ONCE, VERIFIED }`; the internal `object Presses { fun unchanged(before: ScreenSnapshot, after: ScreenSnapshot, windowId: Int?): Boolean }`; `ActionResult.UNCERTAIN = Failed("The press may not have worked.")` and `ActionResult.CARD_OPEN = Failed("A confirmation question is open.")`; `ScreenActions.tap(key, expected = null, policy = PressPolicy.VERIFIED)`, `longPress(key, expected = null, policy = PressPolicy.VERIFIED)`, `setText(key, text, expected = null)`, `openUri(uri, packageName = null, browsable = false)`, `openIntent(intent: Intent): ActionResult`. `ConfirmationCard`: `const val ARMING_MILLIS = 600L`, `isShowing`, `bounds`. `ScreenSession`, below Task 6's lines under `// sub-project 5B`: `val cardShowing: Boolean`.

Deferred items 12, 20, 21, 28 and 29 (D32); design D1, D11, D14. Item 29: when an app acts on a click but `performAction` answers false, `press` used to look for the element again, click again and tap it with a gesture as well, so a send, a call or a delete could happen two or three times. `PressPolicy.ONCE` (the agent uses it for every action of `typing_screen_text` and above and after every confirmation, plan 5A's `ActionMapper.press`) presses once, and gives `ActionResult.UNCERTAIN` when Android refuses the node action or does not report the end of the fallback gesture. `PressPolicy.VERIFIED` (the default, the instant commands' path made safe) presses a second time only when a fresh snapshot, taken after the screen went quiet, shows the press's window with exactly the elements that it had before the press: with a gesture when the node that refused is still the same view, with the fresh node's action when the app replaced the view; never a third time, and a window that changed gives `UNCERTAIN`. Item 28: `setText` gets `expected`, checked on the fresh snapshot before the set-text action and again right before the input method types, so that a key from an older snapshot never types into a field that became a password field or another field. Item 12: `openUri` gets `packageName` and `browsable` (`CATEGORY_BROWSABLE`), and `openIntent` starts any intent (`AppScreenPort` maps `ScreenAction.OpenUri` and `OpenIntent` onto them, Task 13). Items 20 and 21: while the confirmation card shows, every gesture and node action of `ScreenActions` gives `ActionResult.CARD_OPEN` and nothing happens, and the card's bounds count as a window above every element for the fallback gestures; a card ignores taps for its first 600 ms, and a new card appears no sooner than 600 ms after the previous one closed, so that a tap aimed at an old card's button never answers a new one; showing a card forgets Kestrel's credits (D19).

```kotlin
import dev.kestrel.screen.model.ScreenElement

    private fun snapshot(at: Long, vararg elements: ScreenElement) = ScreenSnapshot(at, emptyList(), elements.toList())
```
