Create `app/src/androidTest/kotlin/dev/kestrel/app/screen/ConfirmationCardTest.kt`:

```kotlin
package dev.kestrel.app.screen

import android.graphics.Rect
import android.os.SystemClock
import androidx.test.ext.junit.runners.AndroidJUnit4
import dev.kestrel.app.screen.ScreenServiceRule.Companion.FIXTURES
import dev.kestrel.screen.act.ActionResult
import dev.kestrel.screen.act.ScrollDirection
import kotlinx.coroutines.async
import kotlinx.coroutines.delay
import kotlinx.coroutines.runBlocking
import kotlinx.coroutines.withTimeout
import org.junit.Assert.assertEquals
import org.junit.Assert.assertFalse
import org.junit.Assert.assertTrue
import org.junit.Assume.assumeTrue
import org.junit.Rule
import org.junit.Test
import org.junit.runner.RunWith

/**
 * The confirmation card's safety (design D32 items 20 and 21 of sub-project 5): it ignores taps for its first 600 ms,
 * comes no sooner than 600 ms after the previous card closed, and while it shows Kestrel performs no gesture and no node
 * action.
 */
@RunWith(AndroidJUnit4::class)
class ConfirmationCardTest {
    @get:Rule
    val screen = ScreenServiceRule()

    private val session get() = screen.session

    private suspend fun awaitConfirm(): Rect = withTimeout(5_000) {
        var found = screen.overlayButton("Confirm")
        while (found == null) {
            delay(20)
            found = screen.overlayButton("Confirm")
        }
        found
    }

    @Test
    fun aTapInTheCardsFirst600MillisecondsDoesNothing() = runBlocking {
        screen.open("ViewsActivity", "Views fixture")
        val asked = SystemClock.uptimeMillis()
        val answer = async { session.confirm("Delete the test draft?") }
        val confirm = awaitConfirm()

        screen.shell("input tap ${confirm.centerX()} ${confirm.centerY()}")
        // The card was on the screen for less time than since the question; a slow emulator cannot check the delay.
        if (SystemClock.uptimeMillis() - asked >= ARMING_MILLIS) {
            answer.cancel()
            assumeTrue("The tap came too late to check the delay", false)
        }
        delay(300)
        assertTrue("A tap within the card's first 600 ms answered it", answer.isActive)

        delay(ARMING_MILLIS)
        screen.shell("input tap ${confirm.centerX()} ${confirm.centerY()}")
        assertTrue(withTimeout(5_000) { answer.await() })
    }

    @Test
    fun aNewCardComesNoSoonerThan600MillisecondsAfterThePreviousOneClosed() = runBlocking {
        screen.open("ViewsActivity", "Views fixture")
        val first = async { session.confirm("Send a test message?") }
        awaitConfirm()

        val replaced = SystemClock.uptimeMillis()
        val second = async { session.confirm("Delete the test draft?") }
        assertFalse(withTimeout(5_000) { first.await() })
        withTimeout(5_000) { while (!screen.overlayShows("Delete the test draft?")) delay(20) }
        val after = SystemClock.uptimeMillis() - replaced
        second.cancel()

        assertTrue("The new card came after $after ms", after >= ARMING_MILLIS)
    }

    @Test
    fun noGestureAndNoNodeActionRunWhileTheCardShows() = runBlocking {
        screen.open("ViewsActivity", "Views fixture")
        val send = screen.awaitElement { it.viewId == "$FIXTURES:id/send_button" }
        val field = screen.awaitElement { it.viewId == "$FIXTURES:id/message_field" }
        val answer = async { session.confirm("Delete the test draft?") }
        try {
            awaitConfirm()
            assertTrue(session.cardShowing)

            assertEquals(ActionResult.CARD_OPEN, session.actions.tap(send.key))
            assertEquals(ActionResult.CARD_OPEN, session.actions.longPress(send.key))
            assertEquals(ActionResult.CARD_OPEN, session.actions.tapAt(send.bounds.centerX, send.bounds.centerY))
            assertEquals(ActionResult.CARD_OPEN, session.actions.setText(field.key, "Hello"))
            assertEquals(ActionResult.CARD_OPEN, session.actions.scroll(ScrollDirection.DOWN))
        } finally {
            answer.cancel()
        }
        withTimeout(5_000) { while (session.cardShowing) delay(50) }
        assertTrue(session.snapshots.current().snapshot.elements.any { it.label == "Ready" })
    }

    private companion object {
        const val ARMING_MILLIS = 600L
    }
}
```

```kotlin
package dev.kestrel.screen.act

import dev.kestrel.screen.model.ScreenSnapshot

/** How often a tap or a long press may press (design D32 item 29 of sub-project 5). */
enum class PressPolicy {
    /**
     * One press: when Android answers the node action with false, or does not report the end of the fallback gesture,
     * Kestrel does nothing more and gives [ActionResult.UNCERTAIN], because the app may have acted all the same.
     */
    ONCE,

    /**
     * A second press only when a fresh snapshot, taken after the screen went quiet, shows the press's window exactly as
     * before the press; never a third. A window that changed gives [ActionResult.UNCERTAIN].
     */
    VERIFIED,
}

/** The plain check of [PressPolicy.VERIFIED]. */
internal object Presses {
    /** Whether the window [windowId] has the same elements in [after] as in [before]; the time and other windows do not count. */
    fun unchanged(before: ScreenSnapshot, after: ScreenSnapshot, windowId: Int?): Boolean =
        before.elements.filter { it.windowId == windowId } == after.elements.filter { it.windowId == windowId }
}
```

```kotlin
    /**
     * Opens a link or a deep link in the app that handles it, or only in [packageName] when given. With [browsable], the
     * intent carries `CATEGORY_BROWSABLE`, as a link on a web page does, so that only activities that accept links from
     * the web open it (design D32 item 12 of sub-project 5).
     */
    suspend fun openUri(uri: String, packageName: String? = null, browsable: Boolean = false): ActionResult {
        val intent = Intent(Intent.ACTION_VIEW, Uri.parse(uri)).addFlags(Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK)
        packageName?.let { intent.setPackage(it) }
        if (browsable) intent.addCategory(Intent.CATEGORY_BROWSABLE)
        return try {
            service.startActivity(intent)
            settled(ActionMethod.INTENT)
        } catch (e: ActivityNotFoundException) {
            ActionResult.Failed("No app can open the link.")
        } catch (e: FileUriExposedException) {
            // Android does not let an app hand a file:// link to another app.
            ActionResult.Failed("Android does not let Kestrel open the link.")
        } catch (e: SecurityException) {
            ActionResult.Failed("Android does not let Kestrel open the link.")
        }
    }

    /**
     * Starts [intent] from Kestrel's accessibility service, which Android allows while another app is in front, such as
     * a settings page of `open_settings` or an app's screen that a data tool opens (design D11 and D12 of sub-project 5).
     */
    suspend fun openIntent(intent: Intent): ActionResult {
        return try {
            service.startActivity(intent.addFlags(Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK))
            settled(ActionMethod.INTENT)
        } catch (e: ActivityNotFoundException) {
            ActionResult.Failed("No app can open it.")
        } catch (e: FileUriExposedException) {
            ActionResult.Failed("Android does not let Kestrel open it.")
        } catch (e: SecurityException) {
            ActionResult.Failed("Android does not let Kestrel open it.")
        }
    }
```

```kotlin
    private suspend fun press(
        key: String,
        action: Int,
        fallback: (Int, Int) -> GestureDescription,
        expected: ((ScreenElement) -> Boolean)?,
    ): ActionResult {
        val live = snapshots.current()
        refused(live.snapshot, key, expected)?.let { return it }
        val node = live.node(key) ?: return NOT_ON_SCREEN
        val target = node.touchTarget(action)
        if (target != null && !target.node.isEnabled) return DISABLED
        if (target != null && target.node.offers(action)) {
            if (target.node.perform(action)) {
                return settled(if (target.isSelf) ActionMethod.ACTION else ActionMethod.PARENT_ACTION)
            }
        } else if (node.refresh() && node.isVisibleToUser) {
            // The element is still there, but what a touch on it reaches does not offer the action.
            val bounds = node.screenBounds()
            if (!bounds.isEmpty) {
                return fallbackAt(bounds, live.snapshot.windowsAbove(live.snapshot.element(key)?.windowId), fallback)
            }
        }
        // The node has gone, is hidden or refused the action, so look for the element again (design spec, section 14.3).
        // The key may name another element in the fresh snapshot, so [expected] checks it again.
        snapshots.invalidate()
        val fresh = snapshots.current()
        val element = fresh.snapshot.element(key) ?: return GONE
        if (expected != null && !expected(element)) return ActionResult.CHANGED
        val freshTarget = fresh.node(key)?.touchTarget(action)
        if (freshTarget != null && !freshTarget.node.isEnabled) return DISABLED
        if (freshTarget != null && freshTarget.node.offers(action) && freshTarget.node.perform(action)) {
            return settled(ActionMethod.RETRY_ACTION)
        }
        return fallbackAt(element.bounds, fresh.snapshot.windowsAbove(element.windowId), fallback)
    }
```

```kotlin
        cardOpen()?.let { return it }
        val live = snapshots.current()
        refused(live.snapshot, key, expected)?.let { return it }
        val node = live.node(key) ?: return NOT_ON_SCREEN
        val windowId = live.snapshot.element(key)?.windowId
        val target = node.touchTarget(action)
        if (target != null && !target.node.isEnabled) return DISABLED
        if (target != null && target.node.offers(action)) {
            if (target.node.perform(action)) {
                return settled(if (target.isSelf) ActionMethod.ACTION else ActionMethod.PARENT_ACTION)
            }
            // Android answered no, but some apps act all the same, so a second press could send twice (D32 item 29).
            if (policy == PressPolicy.ONCE) return ActionResult.UNCERTAIN
            return pressAgain(key, action, fallback, expected, live.snapshot, windowId, target.node)
        }
        if (node.refresh() && node.isVisibleToUser) {
            // The element is still there, but what a touch on it reaches does not offer the action: a gesture presses it.
            val bounds = node.screenBounds()
            if (!bounds.isEmpty) return pressed(fallbackAt(bounds, live.snapshot.coversAbove(windowId), fallback))
        }
        // The node has gone or is hidden, so nothing was pressed yet: look for the element again (design spec, section
        // 14.3). The key may name another element in the fresh snapshot, so [expected] checks it again.
        snapshots.invalidate()
        val fresh = snapshots.current()
        val element = fresh.snapshot.element(key) ?: return GONE
        if (expected != null && !expected(element)) return ActionResult.CHANGED
        val freshTarget = fresh.node(key)?.touchTarget(action)
        if (freshTarget != null && !freshTarget.node.isEnabled) return DISABLED
        if (freshTarget != null && freshTarget.node.offers(action)) {
            if (freshTarget.node.perform(action)) return settled(ActionMethod.RETRY_ACTION)
            if (policy == PressPolicy.ONCE) return ActionResult.UNCERTAIN
            return pressAgain(key, action, fallback, expected, fresh.snapshot, element.windowId, freshTarget.node)
        }
        return pressed(fallbackAt(element.bounds, fresh.snapshot.coversAbove(element.windowId), fallback))
    }

    /**
     * The second and last press of [PressPolicy.VERIFIED] after the node [refusedNode] answered no: only when a fresh
     * snapshot, taken after the screen went quiet, shows the press's window exactly as [before] did. It taps with a gesture
     * when the node is still the view that refused, and uses the fresh node's action when the app replaced the view.
     */
    private suspend fun pressAgain(
        key: String,
        action: Int,
        fallback: (Int, Int) -> GestureDescription,
        expected: ((ScreenElement) -> Boolean)?,
        before: ScreenSnapshot,
        windowId: Int?,
        refusedNode: AccessibilityNodeInfo,
    ): ActionResult {
        tracker.awaitQuiet(ScreenChangeTracker.ACTION_QUIET_MILLIS, since = tracker.now())
        snapshots.invalidate()
        val fresh = snapshots.current()
        if (!Presses.unchanged(before, fresh.snapshot, windowId)) return ActionResult.UNCERTAIN
        val element = fresh.snapshot.element(key) ?: return ActionResult.UNCERTAIN
        if (expected != null && !expected(element)) return ActionResult.CHANGED
        val freshTarget = fresh.node(key)?.touchTarget(action)
        if (freshTarget != null && freshTarget.node.isEnabled && freshTarget.node.offers(action) && freshTarget.node != refusedNode) {
            return if (freshTarget.node.perform(action)) settled(ActionMethod.RETRY_ACTION) else ActionResult.UNCERTAIN
        }
        return pressed(fallbackAt(element.bounds, fresh.snapshot.coversAbove(element.windowId), fallback))
    }

    /** A pressing gesture whose end Android did not report may still have pressed (design D32 item 29 of sub-project 5). */
    private fun pressed(result: ActionResult): ActionResult = if (result == GESTURE_TIMED_OUT) ActionResult.UNCERTAIN else result
```

In `core/screen/src/main/kotlin/dev/kestrel/screen/overlay/ConfirmationCard.kt`, replace the whole file with

```kotlin
package dev.kestrel.screen.overlay

import android.graphics.Color
import android.graphics.PixelFormat
import android.graphics.drawable.GradientDrawable
import android.os.SystemClock
import android.util.TypedValue
import android.view.Gravity
import android.view.WindowInsets
import android.view.WindowManager.LayoutParams
import android.widget.Button
import android.widget.LinearLayout
import android.widget.TextView
import dev.kestrel.screen.R
import dev.kestrel.screen.model.IntRect
import kotlinx.coroutines.CancellableContinuation
import kotlinx.coroutines.delay
import kotlinx.coroutines.suspendCancellableCoroutine
import kotlin.coroutines.resume

/**
 * A card at the bottom of the screen with a question and Confirm and Cancel buttons (design spec, section 12.4).
 * Unlike the other overlays it takes touches, but only on itself. A card ignores taps for its first [ARMING_MILLIS], and
 * a new card appears no sooner than [ARMING_MILLIS] after the previous one closed, so that a tap aimed at an old card's
 * button never answers a new one (design D32 item 21 of sub-project 5). Use it on the main thread.
 */
internal class ConfirmationCard(private val host: OverlayHost, private val clock: () -> Long = SystemClock::uptimeMillis) {
    private var pending: Question? = null
    private var closedAt: Long? = null

    /** Whether a card is on the screen; `ScreenActions` acts on nothing while it is (design D32 item 20 of sub-project 5). */
    @Volatile
    var isShowing = false
        private set

    /** The card's bounds on the screen once Android has laid it out, or null while no card shows. */
    @Volatile
    var bounds: IntRect? = null
        private set

    /**
     * Shows [question] and returns true when the owner taps Confirm, or false for Cancel. It also returns false when a
     * newer question replaces this one or [dismiss] ends it, and its card then goes at once. Cancelling the call
     * removes the card too. When the card cannot be shown, because the session has closed, it returns false at once.
     */
    suspend fun ask(question: String): Boolean {
        dismiss()
        closedAt?.let { closed ->
            val wait = closed + ARMING_MILLIS - clock()
            if (wait > 0) delay(wait)
        }
        return suspendCancellableCoroutine { continuation ->
            val open = Question(question, continuation)
            // Cancellation can arrive on any thread, and the window must be removed on the main thread.
            continuation.invokeOnCancellation { open.card.post { open.end(false) } }
            pending = open
            if (host.show(open.card, params())) isShowing = true else open.end(false)
        }
    }

    /** Ends an open question without the owner's answer: its card goes at once, and its [ask] returns false. */
    fun dismiss() {
        pending?.end(false)
    }

    private inner class Question(question: String, private val continuation: CancellableContinuation<Boolean>) {
        private val shownAt = clock()

        val card = build(question, onConfirm = { tapped(true) }, onCancel = { tapped(false) }).apply {
            addOnLayoutChangeListener { view, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _ ->
                if (pending === this@Question) {
                    val at = IntArray(2)
                    view.getLocationOnScreen(at)
                    bounds = IntRect(at[0], at[1], at[0] + view.width, at[1] + view.height)
                }
            }
        }

        // A tap in the card's first ARMING_MILLIS may have been aimed at the card before it.
        private fun tapped(answer: Boolean) {
            if (clock() - shownAt >= ARMING_MILLIS) end(answer)
        }

        /** Removes the card and returns [answer] to the caller, unless the caller already has an answer or has cancelled. */
        fun end(answer: Boolean) {
            host.hide(card)
            // A late tap on this card, or its cancellation, may arrive after a newer question has replaced it.
            if (pending === this) {
                pending = null
                isShowing = false
                bounds = null
                closedAt = clock()
            }
            if (continuation.isActive) continuation.resume(answer)
        }
    }

    private fun build(question: String, onConfirm: () -> Unit, onCancel: () -> Unit): LinearLayout {
        val context = host.context
        val padding = dp(16f).toInt()
        return LinearLayout(context).apply {
            orientation = LinearLayout.VERTICAL
            setPadding(padding, padding, padding, padding)
            background = GradientDrawable().apply {
                setColor(Color.WHITE)
                cornerRadius = dp(16f)
            }
            elevation = dp(8f)
            addView(TextView(context).apply {
                text = question
                setTextColor(Color.BLACK)
                setTextSize(TypedValue.COMPLEX_UNIT_SP, 18f)
            })
            addView(LinearLayout(context).apply {
                gravity = Gravity.END
                addView(Button(context).apply {
                    setText(R.string.screen_cancel)
                    setOnClickListener { onCancel() }
                })
                addView(Button(context).apply {
                    setText(R.string.screen_confirm)
                    setOnClickListener { onConfirm() }
                })
            })
        }
    }

    private fun params() = LayoutParams(
        host.context.resources.displayMetrics.widthPixels - 2 * dp(16f).toInt(),
        LayoutParams.WRAP_CONTENT,
        LayoutParams.TYPE_ACCESSIBILITY_OVERLAY,
        // Touches outside the card go to the app below; Kestrel's touch watcher reports them (section 14.1).
        LayoutParams.FLAG_NOT_FOCUSABLE or LayoutParams.FLAG_NOT_TOUCH_MODAL,
        PixelFormat.TRANSLUCENT,
    ).apply {
        gravity = Gravity.BOTTOM or Gravity.CENTER_HORIZONTAL
        fitInsetsTypes = WindowInsets.Type.systemBars()
        y = dp(16f).toInt()
        setTitle("Kestrel confirmation")
    }

    private fun dp(value: Float) = TypedValue.applyDimension(TypedValue.COMPLEX_UNIT_DIP, value, host.context.resources.displayMetrics)

    companion object {
        /** How long a new card ignores taps, and how long after a card closed the next one may appear. */
        const val ARMING_MILLIS = 600L
    }
}
```

**Files:**

- Test (new): `core/screen/src/test/kotlin/dev/kestrel/screen/read/ScreenEventsTest.kt`
- Test (changed): `core/screen/src/test/kotlin/dev/kestrel/screen/act/ScrollActionsTest.kt`, `core/screen/src/test/kotlin/dev/kestrel/screen/read/FakeNodes.kt`, `core/screen/src/test/kotlin/dev/kestrel/screen/read/SnapshotBuilderTest.kt`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: Task 7's `ScreenActions` (`press`, `scroll`, `selfOrParent`, `perform` with `OwnActions.Kind`, `pressed`, `fallbackAt`, `coversAbove`), plan 5A's `ScreenElement.tooltip` and `ScreenElement.scrollAxis`, `dev.kestrel.screen.model.ScrollAxis`, `SystemUiParts` (`DEFAULT`, `isTile`, `isNotification`, `SYSTEM_UI`), `ObservationBuilder`, `ObservationInput`, `Redactor`, `Vault`, `AgentFreeApps`; `ScreenServiceRule`.
- Produces: `NodeData.tooltip` and `NodeData.scrollAxis` (with defaults of null), `ScrollActions.elementAxis(axis): dev.kestrel.screen.model.ScrollAxis?`, the internal `object FirefoxPages { val PACKAGES; const val WEB_ROOT = "android.webkit.WebView"; fun rootAction(direction, inRegion): Int? }`, `ScreenEvents.isNotification(eventType)`, the `kestrel-api37` source of `systemui-parts.json`, `:testapp`'s `NotificationActivity` extra `headsUp` (constants `EXTRA_HEADS_UP`, `HEADS_UP_TITLE`, `MARKER = "KX4711"`), the device test `dev.kestrel.app.screen.SystemUiFilterTest` (`theShadesNotificationsAreLeftOutAndTheTilesStay`, `aHeadsUpNotificationOverAnAppIsLeftOut`, `recordsTheSystemUiParts`, which logs with the tag `KestrelSystemUi` one line per SystemUI element: `part=<tile|notification|other> id=<name|none> class=<simple name>`), and Appendix B62.

Design D1, D8, D9 and D11; deferred items 14 and 30 (D32). A snapshot's element gets the node's tooltip (`getTooltipText()`, cleaned as the other texts are) and the axis of a scrollable node from `ScrollActions.axis` (its directional actions, its class and its collection's shape), where both ways and an unknown axis give null, so that the observation can say "more below" and the swipe rule of D10 knows a pager. Firefox (r57, B62): Gecko lists no scroll action on a page's inner nodes, its page root (class `android.webkit.WebView`, compared as a string, because the audit flags the class) scrolls the whole page with forward and backward, and a web node's long click does nothing although it answers true. So a long press on a Firefox page goes straight to the gesture, a page scrolls up and down with its root's action (else with the swipe that follows), and a scrollable region inside a page scrolls with the swipe. A notification's accessibility event carries the whole notification unredacted on every version (r54, B61): `ScreenSession` now returns at once for it and reads nothing but its type. `systemui-parts.json` gets kestrel-api37's tile and notification IDs, which prototype P3 of plan 4 and plan 2D recorded (`qs_tile_large`, `qs_tile_toggle_target`, `expandableNotificationRow`); `SystemUiFilterTest` checks them on the live shade, Quick Settings and a heads-up notification whose text holds a marker that no observation may hold, and its recording method gives plan 5C's sitting the A71's parts. When `recordsTheSystemUiParts` on kestrel-api37 shows a tile or a notification row under another ID, add that ID to the `kestrel-api37` source and run the test again.

Counts: `:core:screen` JVM N + 4 (`ScrollActionsTest` + 2, `SnapshotBuilderTest` + 1, `ScreenEventsTest` 1); `:app` device screen N + 3 (`SystemUiFilterTest`); the rest unchanged.

```kotlin
    /** The axis that a snapshot's element shows (design D1 and D8 of sub-project 5): none for both ways or an unknown one. */
    fun elementAxis(axis: ScrollAxis): ElementAxis? = when (axis) {
        ScrollAxis.VERTICAL -> ElementAxis.VERTICAL
        ScrollAxis.HORIZONTAL -> ElementAxis.HORIZONTAL
        ScrollAxis.BOTH, ScrollAxis.UNKNOWN -> null
    }
}

/**
 * Firefox's web pages (design D11 of sub-project 5; research r57, Appendix B62). Gecko lists no scroll action on the
 * nodes inside a page; its page root, of the class [WEB_ROOT], scrolls the whole page by 0.8 of its height with the
 * forward and backward actions, and a node's long click does nothing although it answers true.
 */
internal object FirefoxPages {
    val PACKAGES = setOf("org.mozilla.firefox", "org.mozilla.firefox_beta", "org.mozilla.fenix")

    /** The class of Gecko's page root, compared as a string: the audit flags the class itself (design D1). */
    const val WEB_ROOT = "android.webkit.WebView"

    /**
     * The page root's action that scrolls a page's node in [direction], or null when only a swipe can: sideways, and
     * inside a scrollable region of the page ([inRegion]), whose scroll the root's action would not do.
     */
    fun rootAction(direction: ScrollDirection, inRegion: Boolean): Int? = when {
        inRegion -> null
        direction == ScrollDirection.DOWN -> AccessibilityNodeInfo.ACTION_SCROLL_FORWARD
        direction == ScrollDirection.UP -> AccessibilityNodeInfo.ACTION_SCROLL_BACKWARD
        else -> null
    }
}
```

Create `app/src/androidTest/kotlin/dev/kestrel/app/screen/SystemUiFilterTest.kt`:

```kotlin
package dev.kestrel.app.screen

import android.util.Log
import androidx.test.ext.junit.runners.AndroidJUnit4
import dev.kestrel.agent.observe.ObservationBuilder
import dev.kestrel.agent.observe.ObservationInput
import dev.kestrel.agent.observe.SystemUiParts
import dev.kestrel.app.screen.ScreenServiceRule.Companion.FIXTURES
import dev.kestrel.safety.AgentFreeApps
import dev.kestrel.safety.Redactor
import dev.kestrel.safety.Vault
import dev.kestrel.screen.act.GlobalAction
import dev.kestrel.screen.model.ScreenElement
import dev.kestrel.screen.model.ScreenSnapshot
import kotlinx.coroutines.runBlocking
import org.junit.After
import org.junit.Assert.assertFalse
import org.junit.Assert.assertTrue
import org.junit.Before
import org.junit.Rule
import org.junit.Test
import org.junit.runner.RunWith

/**
 * SystemUI's parts in an observation (design D9 of sub-project 5): Quick Settings' tiles stay, and a notification, also
 * a heads-up one, is only counted, so that its text, such as a one-time code, never reaches a prompt. The heads-up
 * notification of `:testapp` (`NotificationActivity` with the extra `headsUp`) carries the text [MARKER].
 * [recordsTheSystemUiParts] writes the view IDs and classes of SystemUI's elements to logcat (tag `KestrelSystemUi`, one
 * line per element:
 * `part=<tile|notification|other> id=<name|none> class=<simple name>`), from which the `a71` source of
 * `systemui-parts.json` is filled after the owner's first sitting.
 */
@RunWith(AndroidJUnit4::class)
class SystemUiFilterTest {
    @get:Rule
    val screen = ScreenServiceRule()

    private val parts = SystemUiParts.DEFAULT

    @Before
    fun post() {
        screen.shell("pm grant $FIXTURES android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS")
        screen.shell("am start -W -n $FIXTURES/.NotificationActivity")
        screen.shell("am start -W -n $FIXTURES/.NotificationActivity --ez ${HEADS_UP} true")
    }

    @After
    fun cancel() = runBlocking<Unit> {
        screen.shell("am start -W -n $FIXTURES/.NotificationActivity --ez ${CANCEL} true")
        screen.session.actions.global(GlobalAction.DISMISS_SHADE)
    }

    @Test
    fun theShadesNotificationsAreLeftOutAndTheTilesStay() = runBlocking<Unit> {
        screen.session.actions.global(GlobalAction.NOTIFICATIONS)
        // 15 s, as in SystemCommandsTest: SystemUI's windows were slow to show while the host ran short of memory.
        screen.awaitElement(15_000) { it.packageName == SystemUiParts.SYSTEM_UI && shows(it) }
        val shade = screen.session.snapshots.current().snapshot
        assertTrue("No notification row was recognised", shade.elements.any(parts::isNotification))
        assertFalse("The observation holds the notification's text", observe(shade).contains(MARKER))
        screen.session.actions.global(GlobalAction.DISMISS_SHADE)

        screen.session.actions.global(GlobalAction.QUICK_SETTINGS)
        val tile = screen.awaitElement(15_000) { it.packageName == SystemUiParts.SYSTEM_UI && parts.isTile(it) && it.label != null }
        assertTrue("The observation left out a tile", observe(screen.session.snapshots.current().snapshot).contains(tile.label!!))
    }

    @Test
    fun aHeadsUpNotificationOverAnAppIsLeftOut() = runBlocking<Unit> {
        screen.open("CommandsActivity", "Commands fixture")
        screen.shell("am start -W -n $FIXTURES/.NotificationActivity --ez ${HEADS_UP} true")
        screen.awaitElement(15_000) { it.packageName == SystemUiParts.SYSTEM_UI && shows(it) }

        assertFalse("The observation holds the heads-up's text", observe(screen.session.snapshots.current().snapshot).contains(MARKER))
    }

    @Test
    fun recordsTheSystemUiParts() = runBlocking<Unit> {
        for (global in listOf(GlobalAction.NOTIFICATIONS, GlobalAction.QUICK_SETTINGS)) {
            screen.session.actions.global(global)
            screen.awaitElement(15_000) { it.packageName == SystemUiParts.SYSTEM_UI && it.isActionable }
            for (element in screen.session.snapshots.current().snapshot.elements.filter { it.packageName == SystemUiParts.SYSTEM_UI }) {
                val part = when {
                    parts.isTile(element) -> "tile"
                    parts.isNotification(element) -> "notification"
                    else -> "other"
                }
                val id = element.viewId?.substringAfter(":id/", missingDelimiterValue = "")?.ifEmpty { null } ?: "none"
                Log.i(TAG, "part=$part id=$id class=${element.className?.substringAfterLast('.') ?: "none"}")
            }
            screen.session.actions.global(GlobalAction.DISMISS_SHADE)
        }
    }

    private fun observe(snapshot: ScreenSnapshot): String =
        ObservationBuilder(Redactor(Vault()), AgentFreeApps(), parts).build(ObservationInput(1, snapshot, "System UI")).text

    private fun shows(element: ScreenElement): Boolean = element.text?.contains(MARKER) == true || element.label?.contains(MARKER) == true

    private companion object {
        const val TAG = "KestrelSystemUi"

        // NotificationActivity's extras and the text of its heads-up notification.
        const val HEADS_UP = "headsUp"
        const val CANCEL = "cancel"
        const val MARKER = "KX4711"
    }
}
```

**Files:**
- Modify: `app/build.gradle.kts`, `app/src/main/kotlin/dev/kestrel/app/settings/LogPages.kt`, `app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml`, `core/privacy/src/main/kotlin/dev/kestrel/privacy/db/LogEntryRow.kt`, `core/privacy/src/main/kotlin/dev/kestrel/privacy/logs/LogEvents.kt`, `core/privacy/src/main/kotlin/dev/kestrel/privacy/logs/LogStore.kt`
- Test (changed): `core/privacy/src/test/kotlin/dev/kestrel/privacy/logs/LogStoreTest.kt`
- Test (changed): `app/src/androidTest/kotlin/dev/kestrel/app/settings/LogExportFileTest.kt`, `core/privacy/src/androidTest/kotlin/dev/kestrel/privacy/KestrelDatabaseTest.kt`
- Modify: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-12-kestrel-design.md`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `LogStore`, `LogDao`, `LogEntryRow`, `ActivityEvent`, `ActivityKind`, `KestrelDatabase`; `LogPages` and its strings below `<!-- sub-project 5B -->`.
- Produces: `ActivityKind.PROMPT`, `REPLY`, `SAFETY`; `LogDao.oldestAfter(after: Long, limit: Int)`; `LogStore.export` writing pages of `LogStore.EXPORT_PAGE` (100) entries; the string `logs_newest` and the kind labels; spec 13.5's export and kinds.

Design D25; deferred items 46 and 47 (D32). Before the agent writes its prompts and replies into the activity log, the log gets the kinds `PROMPT`, `REPLY` and `SAFETY`, the log pages name them, and the export streams the entries 100 at a time, oldest first, as compact JSON, so that a week of prompts never has to fit in memory; an entry that can no longer be decrypted is left out and deleted, as a read does. The pages show the newest entries and say how many (`logs_newest`). `LogExportFileTest` exports a store of its own, in an in-memory Room database, so that it no longer depends on what the emulator's own log holds; `:app`'s device tests get `room-runtime` for it.

Counts: `:core:privacy` JVM N + 3 (`LogStoreTest`); `:core:privacy` device N + 1 (`KestrelDatabaseTest`); `:app` device settings unchanged (`LogExportFileTest` is rewritten); the rest unchanged.

with

```kotlin
    /**
     * Writes both logs to [output] as a [LogExport] in JSON, with every entry, not only the newest. The logs leave the
     * phone only this way, when the owner exports them to a file of their choice (design spec, section 13.5). It reads and
     * writes [EXPORT_PAGE] entries at a time, so that a log of tens of megabytes never has to fit into memory (design D32
     * item 47 of sub-project 5). An entry that can never be read is left out and deleted, as when the log is read. It
     * flushes [output] and leaves it open.
     */
    suspend fun export(output: OutputStream) = withContext(dispatcher) {
        purgeExpired()
        val writer = output.bufferedWriter(Charsets.UTF_8)
        writer.write("{\"exportedAt\":")
        writer.write(json.encodeToString(String.serializer(), isoTime(clock())))
        writer.write(",\"activity\":[")
        val activity = exportLog(writer, ACTIVITY, ActivityEvent.serializer())
        writer.write("],\"network\":[")
        val network = exportLog(writer, NETWORK, NetworkEvent.serializer())
        writer.write("]}")
        writer.flush()
        noteUnreadable(ACTIVITY, activity)
        noteUnreadable(NETWORK, network)
    }

    /** Writes the entries of [log], oldest first and separated by commas, page by page; returns how many were unreadable. */
    private suspend fun <T> exportLog(writer: Writer, log: String, serializer: KSerializer<T>): Int {
        val entry = LogExport.Entry.serializer(serializer)
        var afterMillis = Long.MIN_VALUE
        var afterId = Long.MIN_VALUE
        var first = true
        var unreadable = 0
        while (true) {
            val rows = dao.oldestAfter(log, afterMillis, afterId, EXPORT_PAGE)
            for (row in rows) {
                val event = decodeOrNull(log, serializer, row)
                if (event == null) {
                    dao.delete(row.id)
                    unreadable++
                    continue
                }
                if (!first) writer.write(",")
                first = false
                writer.write(json.encodeToString(entry, LogExport.Entry(isoTime(row.timestampMillis), event)))
            }
            if (rows.size < EXPORT_PAGE) return unreadable
            afterMillis = rows.last().timestampMillis
            afterId = rows.last().id
        }
    }

    private fun isoTime(millis: Long) = Instant.ofEpochMilli(millis).toString()
```

- [ ] **Step 6: Describe the export and the kinds in spec 13.5**

In `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-12-kestrel-design.md`, replace

```markdown
| Activity log | The spoken command, each redacted observation and prompt that was sent, each LLM reply, each action and safety decision, confirmations, timings, tokens and estimated cost | 7 days |
| Network log | Time, host, path, request and response size, status, and the task it belongs to. The path is the request's path with the parts that name the owner's project or account replaced, such as Vertex's project or a Bedrock model; a failed request's detail is the error's class, except for a request that the allowlist refused, whose detail names the host and the rule | 7 days |

- Both logs are encrypted and can be viewed in settings. A button in settings wipes both after a confirmation; "Kestrel, delete history" by voice, after a spoken confirmation, comes with the agent (sub-project 5).
- The logs leave the phone only when the owner exports them to a file of their choice. The export is one JSON file with both logs and all their entries, oldest first, with times in UTC.
- Screenshots, audio and credentials are never logged.
- Kestrel writes no audio, transcript, reply, boost word, app name, screen text, exception message or exit record's description to Android's log. It logs a failure only by its classes and stack frames, and the text form (`toString`) of anything that carries the owner's words gives only lengths or counts.
```

with

```markdown
| Activity log | The spoken command, each redacted observation and prompt that was sent, each LLM reply, each action and safety decision, confirmations, timings, tokens and estimated cost | 7 days |
| Network log | Time, host, path, request and response size, status, and the task it belongs to. The path is the request's path with the parts that name the owner's project or account replaced, such as Vertex's project or a Bedrock model; a failed request's detail is the error's class, except for a request that the allowlist refused, whose detail names the host and the rule | 7 days |

- Both logs are encrypted and can be viewed in settings. A button in settings wipes both after a confirmation; "Kestrel, delete history" by voice, after a spoken confirmation, comes with the agent (sub-project 5).
- The logs leave the phone only when the owner exports them to a file of their choice. The export is one JSON file with both logs and all their entries, oldest first, with times in UTC. Kestrel writes it 100 entries at a time, so that a week of prompts never has to fit in memory, and leaves out an entry that it can no longer decrypt.
- The activity log's entries have a kind: an action, a note, an error, a prompt (the new part of a model call's request), a reply (with its usage and cost) or a safety decision, and a task's entries carry the task's ID (sub-project 5's design D25). The log pages show the newest entries and say how many.
- Screenshots, audio and credentials are never logged.
- Kestrel writes no audio, transcript, reply, boost word, app name, screen text, exception message or exit record's description to Android's log. It logs a failure only by its classes and stack frames, and the text form (`toString`) of anything that carries the owner's words gives only lengths or counts.
```

### Task 10: The Orchestrator, part 1: the task's phases, its questions and its hand-overs

**Files:**
- Create: `app/src/main/kotlin/dev/kestrel/app/orchestrator/TaskAnswers.kt`
- Modify: `app/src/main/kotlin/dev/kestrel/app/listen/Listening.kt`, `app/src/main/kotlin/dev/kestrel/app/orchestrator/Orchestrator.kt`, `app/src/main/kotlin/dev/kestrel/app/orchestrator/Requests.kt`, `app/src/main/kotlin/dev/kestrel/app/orchestrator/Rules.kt`
- Test (changed): `app/src/test/kotlin/dev/kestrel/app/orchestrator/OrchestratorTest.kt`, `app/src/test/kotlin/dev/kestrel/app/orchestrator/RequestsTest.kt`, `app/src/test/kotlin/dev/kestrel/app/orchestrator/RulesTest.kt`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `Rules`, `State`, `Event`, `Effect`, `Reply`, `Feedback`, `Requests`, `Orchestrator`, `Listening`, `ListeningTexts`, `SpokenNumbers`, `Normalizer`.
- Produces: `enum class TaskPhase { RUNNING, HANDED_OVER, PAUSED }`, `enum class TaskAsk { YES_NO, CONFIRM, FREE, CONTINUE, PICK_NUMBER }`; `State.taskPhase`, `taskAsking`, `voiceAnswers`, `handOver`, `taskExists`; events `TaskSays(task, text)`, `TaskAsks(task, question, kind, voice = true)`, `TaskHandsOver(task, text)`, `TaskBusy(task)`, `OwnerTouched`, `HandOverEnded(handOver)`; effects `AnswerTask(task, answer: String?)`, `ContinueTask(task)`, `TimeHandOver`, `ExpireHandOver(task)`; `Reply.NoTaskToContinue`; `Feedback.TaskText(text, keep)`, `Feedback.FinishHandOverFirst`; `Request.Continue`; `internal object TaskAnswers { const val YES = "yes"; const val NO = "no"; fun read(kind, text, named, request): String?; fun saysYes(text, named): Boolean }`; `Orchestrator(handOverMillis = HAND_OVER_MILLIS)` (180 s); `Listening.steerTask: (Effect) -> Unit` and `ListeningTexts.NO_TASK_TO_CONTINUE`, `FINISH_HAND_OVER_FIRST`.

Design D2; deferred items 5 and 26 (D32). `Work` keeps saying what Kestrel does now, and the task's own state is `taskPhase` and `taskAsking`, so that an instant command during a hand-over leaves the hand-over open. The agent's side speaks through `TaskSays`, asks through `TaskAsks` (spoken, with the command question's answer wait of 15 s to start and 35 s once the owner speaks; `voice = false` takes only the card's answer, D32 item 17), hands over through `TaskHandsOver` and says that it acts again with `TaskBusy`. The answers are read on `Normalizer`'s words (`TaskAnswers`): a confirmation takes "confirm", "yes" or "send it"; a yes-or-no question "yes", "continue" or "go on"; both "no"; a free question the next transcript; a number question a number; "stop" and "cancel" cancel the task in every question, and only "no" and silence answer no. During a hand-over the instant commands work, the owner's touches do nothing, "Kestrel, continue" gives `ContinueTask`, "cancel" ends the task, a new task is refused with "Say 'Kestrel, continue' or 'cancel' first.", and after 3 minutes `ExpireHandOver` ends it. While a task runs, an owner's touch (`OwnerTouched`) cancels it. "Kestrel, continue" outside a hand-over says "There's no task to continue." (`Request.Continue`, which this task adds because the hand-over needs it; the design lists it under Task 11). The effects that steer a task go through `Listening.steerTask`, which Task 12 points at the agent.

Counts: `:app` JVM N + 23 (`RulesTest` + 21, `RequestsTest` + 1, `OrchestratorTest` + 1); the rest unchanged.

```kotlin
    // Design D2 of sub-project 5: the task's own state, its questions, touches and hand-overs.
    private val runningTask = listening.copy(work = Work.RUNNING_TASK, task = 1, taskPhase = TaskPhase.RUNNING)

    private fun asking(kind: TaskAsk, voice: Boolean = true): State =
        Rules.next(runningTask, Event.TaskAsks(1, "Shall I?", kind, voice)).state

    private val handOverText = "Please enter your password, then say 'Kestrel, continue'."

    // A hand-over whose sentence has been spoken.
    private fun handedOver(from: State = runningTask): State =
        Rules.next(Rules.next(from, Event.TaskHandsOver(1, handOverText)).state, Event.SpeechEnded).state

    private fun heard(state: State, text: String, named: Boolean = false) = Rules.next(state, Event.Heard(text, named))

    @Test
    fun aTaskStartsInItsRunningPhaseAndEndsWithoutOne() {
        val started = heard(listening, "Kestrel, open Viber.", named = true).state
        assertEquals(TaskPhase.RUNNING, started.taskPhase)
        assertTrue(started.taskExists)

        val ended = Rules.next(started, Event.TaskEnded(1, "Done."))
        assertEquals(null, ended.state.taskPhase)
        assertFalse(ended.state.taskExists)
    }

    @Test
    fun aTaskSaysItsTextAndShowsIt() {
        val step = Rules.next(runningTask, Event.TaskSays(1, "Android gave Kestrel only the photos that you selected."))

        assertEquals(
            listOf(
                Effect.Show(Feedback.TaskText("Android gave Kestrel only the photos that you selected.")),
                Effect.Say(Reply.Text("Android gave Kestrel only the photos that you selected.")),
            ),
            step.effects,
        )
        // An older task says nothing.
        assertEquals(Step(runningTask), Rules.next(runningTask, Event.TaskSays(0, "Late.")))
    }

    @Test
    fun aTaskQuestionIsSpokenKeptOnTheBarAndWaitsForItsAnswer() {
        val step = Rules.next(runningTask, Event.TaskAsks(1, "I'm not getting anywhere. Should I keep trying?", TaskAsk.YES_NO))

        assertEquals(
            listOf(
                Effect.Show(Feedback.TaskText("I'm not getting anywhere. Should I keep trying?", keep = true)),
                Effect.Say(Reply.Text("I'm not getting anywhere. Should I keep trying?")),
                Effect.WaitForAnswer(),
            ),
            step.effects,
        )
        assertEquals(TaskAsk.YES_NO, step.state.taskAsking)
        assertEquals(Work.RUNNING_TASK, step.state.work)
        // The wait starts again when the question has been spoken, and grows once the owner speaks.
        val spoken = Rules.next(step.state, Event.SpeechEnded)
        assertEquals(listOf(Effect.WaitForAnswer()), spoken.effects)
        assertEquals(Recognition.ALL, spoken.state.recognition)
        assertEquals(listOf(Effect.WaitForAnswer(answering = true)), Rules.next(spoken.state, Event.Speaking).effects)
        // A second question while one is open is ignored: questions come one at a time.
        assertEquals(Step(step.state), Rules.next(step.state, Event.TaskAsks(1, "Another?", TaskAsk.FREE)))
    }

    @Test
    fun aYesOrNoQuestionTakesOnlyItsAnswers() {
        val question = asking(TaskAsk.YES_NO)

        for (yes in listOf("Yes.", "Yes, please.", "Continue", "Go on.")) {
            val step = heard(question, yes)
            assertEquals(yes, Effect.AnswerTask(1, TaskAnswers.YES), step.effects.last())
            assertEquals(null, step.state.taskAsking)
        }
        assertEquals(Effect.AnswerTask(1, TaskAnswers.YES), heard(question, "Kestrel, continue.", named = true).effects.last())
        assertEquals(Effect.AnswerTask(1, TaskAnswers.NO), heard(question, "No.").effects.last())
        // Other speech is only shown, and the question goes on.
        assertEquals(Step(question, listOf(Effect.Show(Feedback.Heard("Open Viber")))), heard(question, "Open Viber"))
    }

    @Test
    fun aConfirmationGoesAheadOnConfirmYesOrSendIt() {
        val question = asking(TaskAsk.CONFIRM)

        for (yes in listOf("Confirm.", "Yes", "Send it!", "Kestrel, confirm")) {
            assertEquals(yes, Effect.AnswerTask(1, TaskAnswers.YES), heard(question, yes, named = yes.startsWith("Kestrel")).effects.last())
        }
        assertEquals(Effect.AnswerTask(1, TaskAnswers.NO), heard(question, "No").effects.last())
        assertEquals(listOf(Effect.Show(Feedback.Heard("Go on."))), heard(question, "Go on.").effects)
    }

    @Test
    fun theSilenceAfterATaskQuestionIsNoAnswer() {
        val question = asking(TaskAsk.CONFIRM)

        val ended = Rules.next(question, Event.AnswerWaitEnded(question.wait))

        assertEquals(listOf(Effect.AnswerTask(1, null)), ended.effects)
        assertEquals(null, ended.state.taskAsking)
        // The end of an older wait changes nothing.
        assertEquals(Step(question), Rules.next(question, Event.AnswerWaitEnded(question.wait - 1)))
    }

    @Test
    fun stopAndCancelCancelTheTaskInEveryKindOfQuestion() {
        for (kind in TaskAsk.entries) {
            for (text in listOf("Stop.", "Cancel", "Okay, cancel that")) {
                val step = heard(asking(kind), text)
                assertTrue("$kind $text", Effect.CancelTask in step.effects)
                assertEquals("$kind $text", null, step.state.taskPhase)
                assertEquals("$kind $text", null, step.state.taskAsking)
            }
        }
    }

    @Test
    fun aFreeQuestionTakesTheNextTranscriptAndANumberQuestionANumber() {
        assertEquals(Effect.AnswerTask(1, "The blue one."), heard(asking(TaskAsk.FREE), "The blue one.").effects.last())
        assertEquals(Effect.AnswerTask(1, "12"), heard(asking(TaskAsk.PICK_NUMBER), "12").effects.last())
        val number = asking(TaskAsk.PICK_NUMBER)
        assertEquals(Step(number, listOf(Effect.Show(Feedback.Heard("the red one")))), heard(number, "the red one"))
    }

    @Test
    fun whileOnlyTheCardMayAnswerSpokenAnswersDoNotCount() {
        val question = asking(TaskAsk.CONFIRM, voice = false)

        assertEquals(Step(question, listOf(Effect.Show(Feedback.Heard("Confirm.")))), heard(question, "Confirm."))
        assertTrue(Effect.CancelTask in heard(question, "Cancel.").effects)
        assertEquals(listOf(Effect.AnswerTask(1, null)), Rules.next(question, Event.AnswerWaitEnded(question.wait)).effects)
        // The card answered: the agent says that it acts again.
        assertEquals(null, Rules.next(question, Event.TaskBusy(1)).state.taskAsking)
    }

    @Test
    fun theOwnersTouchCancelsARunningTaskButNotAHandOver() {
        assertEquals(listOf(Effect.CancelTask), Rules.next(runningTask, Event.OwnerTouched).effects)
        assertTrue(Effect.CancelTask in Rules.next(asking(TaskAsk.CONFIRM), Event.OwnerTouched).effects)
        val handed = handedOver()
        assertEquals(Step(handed), Rules.next(handed, Event.OwnerTouched))
        assertEquals(Step(listening), Rules.next(listening, Event.OwnerTouched))
    }

    @Test
    fun aHandOverKeepsItsSentenceOnTheBarAndStartsItsThreeMinutes() {
        val step = Rules.next(runningTask, Event.TaskHandsOver(1, "This is a payment. Please finish it yourself, then say 'Kestrel, continue'."))

        assertEquals(
            listOf(
                Effect.Show(Feedback.TaskText("This is a payment. Please finish it yourself, then say 'Kestrel, continue'.", keep = true)),
                Effect.Say(Reply.Text("This is a payment. Please finish it yourself, then say 'Kestrel, continue'.")),
                Effect.TimeHandOver,
            ),
            step.effects,
        )
        assertEquals(TaskPhase.HANDED_OVER, step.state.taskPhase)
        assertEquals(Work.IDLE, step.state.work)
        assertEquals(1, step.state.handOver)
        assertTrue(step.state.taskExists)
    }

    @Test
    fun duringAHandOverTheInstantCommandsWorkAlsoInThePausedMode() {
        for (from in listOf(runningTask, runningTask.copy(mode = Mode.PAUSED))) {
            val handed = handedOver(from)
            assertEquals(Recognition.ALL, handed.recognition)
            val command = heard(handed, "Scroll down")
            assertEquals(Work.RUNNING_COMMAND, command.state.work)
            assertTrue(command.effects.last() is Effect.RunCommand)
            // The command's end leaves the hand-over open.
            val ended = Rules.next(command.state, Event.CommandEnded(command.state.command, CommandResult(Outcome.DONE)))
            assertEquals(Work.IDLE, ended.state.work)
            assertEquals(TaskPhase.HANDED_OVER, ended.state.taskPhase)
        }
    }

    @Test
    fun kestrelContinueEndsAHandOverAndCancelEndsTheTask() {
        val handed = handedOver()

        val continued = heard(handed, "Kestrel, continue.", named = true)
        assertEquals(listOf(Effect.Show(Feedback.Heard("Kestrel, continue.")), Effect.ContinueTask(1)), continued.effects)
        assertEquals(TaskPhase.RUNNING, continued.state.taskPhase)
        assertEquals(Work.RUNNING_TASK, continued.state.work)

        for (text in listOf("Cancel.", "Stop", "Kestrel, cancel")) {
            val cancelled = heard(handed, text, named = text.startsWith("Kestrel"))
            assertTrue(text, Effect.CancelTask in cancelled.effects)
            assertEquals(text, null, cancelled.state.taskPhase)
            assertTrue(text, cancelled.state.cancelled)
        }
        // "Kestrel" and then "never mind" ends only the wait for a task; "Kestrel" and then "stop" ends the task.
        val awaiting = heard(handed, "Kestrel", named = true).state
        assertFalse(Effect.CancelTask in heard(awaiting, "Never mind.").effects)
        assertTrue(Effect.CancelTask in heard(awaiting, "Stop.").effects)
        assertTrue(Effect.CancelTask in heard(awaiting, "Kestrel, cancel.", named = true).effects)
    }

    @Test
    fun kestrelContinueDuringACommandOfAHandOverLeavesTheCommandAndContinues() {
        val command = heard(handedOver(), "Scroll down").state

        val continued = heard(command, "Kestrel, continue", named = true)

        assertEquals(listOf(Effect.CancelCommand, Effect.Show(Feedback.Heard("Kestrel, continue")), Effect.ContinueTask(1)), continued.effects)
        assertEquals(Work.RUNNING_TASK, continued.state.work)
    }

    @Test
    fun aNewTaskDuringAHandOverWaitsAndStopFirstReplacesIt() {
        val handed = handedOver()

        assertEquals(
            listOf(Effect.Show(Feedback.Heard("Kestrel, open Viber.")), Effect.Show(Feedback.FinishHandOverFirst)),
            heard(handed, "Kestrel, open Viber.", named = true).effects,
        )
        val replaced = heard(handed, "Stop. Kestrel, open Viber.", named = true)
        assertEquals(listOf(Effect.Show(Feedback.Heard("Stop. Kestrel, open Viber.")), Effect.CancelTask, Effect.RunTask(2, "open Viber.")), replaced.effects)
        assertEquals(TaskPhase.RUNNING, replaced.state.taskPhase)
        // After "Kestrel" on its own, "Yes?" takes "continue" for the hand-over, and refuses a new task.
        val awaiting = heard(handed, "Kestrel", named = true).state
        assertEquals(Effect.ContinueTask(1), heard(awaiting, "Continue.").effects.last())
        assertEquals(Effect.Show(Feedback.FinishHandOverFirst), heard(awaiting, "Open Viber.").effects.last())
    }

    @Test
    fun kestrelContinueWithoutAHandOverSaysSo() {
        val step = heard(listening, "Kestrel, continue, please.", named = true)

        assertEquals(listOf(Effect.Show(Feedback.Heard("Kestrel, continue, please.")), Effect.Say(Reply.NoTaskToContinue)), step.effects)
        // While the task runs, it is ignored.
        assertEquals(Step(runningTask), heard(runningTask, "Kestrel, continue", named = true))
    }

    @Test
    fun aHandOverThatLastsThreeMinutesEndsTheTaskWithItsReport() {
        val handed = handedOver()

        assertEquals(listOf(Effect.ExpireHandOver(1)), Rules.next(handed, Event.HandOverEnded(1)).effects)
        // The timer of an older hand-over changes nothing.
        assertEquals(Step(handed), Rules.next(handed, Event.HandOverEnded(0)))
        // The task's report comes in every phase, also while a command runs.
        val report = Rules.next(handed, Event.TaskEnded(1, "I stopped because the hand-over took too long."))
        assertEquals(null, report.state.taskPhase)
        assertEquals(Effect.Say(Reply.Text("I stopped because the hand-over took too long.")), report.effects.last())
        val command = heard(handed, "Scroll down").state
        val late = Rules.next(command, Event.TaskEnded(1, "Report."))
        assertEquals(Work.RUNNING_COMMAND, late.state.work)
        assertEquals(null, late.state.taskPhase)
        assertEquals(Effect.Say(Reply.Text("Report.")), late.effects.last())
    }

    @Test
    fun aHandOverThatEndedByItselfRunsTheTaskAgain() {
        val busy = Rules.next(handedOver(), Event.TaskBusy(1))

        assertEquals(TaskPhase.RUNNING, busy.state.taskPhase)
        assertEquals(Work.RUNNING_TASK, busy.state.work)
        assertEquals(Step(runningTask), Rules.next(runningTask, Event.TaskBusy(0)))
    }

    @Test
    fun theSpottersStopCancelsATaskDuringItsHandOverSentence() {
        val speaking = Rules.next(runningTask, Event.TaskHandsOver(1, handOverText)).state

        val step = Rules.next(speaking, Event.Spotted(Keyword.STOP))

        assertEquals(listOf(Effect.StopSaying, Effect.CancelTask), step.effects)
        assertEquals(null, step.state.taskPhase)
    }

    @Test
    fun turningOffEndsATaskInEveryPhase() {
        for (state in listOf(runningTask, asking(TaskAsk.FREE), handedOver())) {
            val off = Rules.next(state, Event.TurnOff)
            assertTrue(Effect.CancelTask in off.effects)
            assertEquals(null, off.state.taskPhase)
            assertEquals(null, off.state.taskAsking)
        }
    }

    @Test
    fun theTaskEventsAndEffectsPrintNoWords() {
        val printed = listOf(
            Event.TaskSays(1, "secret"),
            Event.TaskAsks(1, "secret", TaskAsk.FREE),
            Event.TaskHandsOver(1, "secret"),
            Effect.AnswerTask(1, "secret"),
            Feedback.TaskText("secret"),
        ).joinToString()

        assertFalse(printed, printed.contains("secret"))
    }
```

```kotlin
    }

    // Design D2 of sub-project 5: while the task asks, "stop" and "cancel" cancel it in every kind of question, Kestrel's
    // requests that stop something act as while it runs, and otherwise only the answer that it asked for counts. While
    // only the card may answer (D32 item 17), no spoken answer counts.
    private fun answering(state: State, request: Request, event: Event.Heard, shown: Effect): Step {

        val stopsFirst = (request is Request.Task && request.stopFirst) || (request is Request.OpenSettings && request.stopFirst)
        if (stopsFirst || request == Request.PauseListening || request == Request.TurnOff) return whileTaskRuns(state, request, shown)
        val kind = state.taskAsking ?: return Step(state)
        if (!state.voiceAnswers) return Step(state, listOf(shown))
        val answer = TaskAnswers.read(kind, event.text, event.named, request) ?: return Step(state, listOf(shown))
        return answerTask(state, answer, shown)
    }

    // The question has its answer, or its wait ended without one (null).
    private fun answerTask(state: State, answer: String?, vararg first: Effect): Step =
        Step(state.copy(taskAsking = null, voiceAnswers = true), first.toList() + Effect.AnswerTask(state.task, answer))

    // The answer to "Yes?" is read as the words after the name, so it is never Other. While Kestrel is paused, a near miss
    // of "wake up" ends the wait and starts nothing (plan 4E). While a task waits for the owner's hand, "Yes?" takes
    // "continue" or "cancel" for it ("never mind" ends only the wait), and a new task waits until it has ended (design D2
    // of sub-project 5).
    private fun whileAwaitingTask(state: State, request: Request, text: String, shown: Effect): Step = when (request) {
        is Request.Task -> when {
            request.nearWakeUp && state.mode == Mode.PAUSED -> Step(state.copy(work = Work.IDLE), listOf(shown))
            state.taskExists -> Step(state.copy(work = Work.IDLE), listOf(shown, Effect.Show(Feedback.FinishHandOverFirst)))

        is Request.Other ->
            if (state.taskExists) {
                Step(state.copy(work = Work.IDLE), listOf(shown, Effect.Show(Feedback.FinishHandOverFirst)))

        Request.Continue ->
            if (state.taskPhase == TaskPhase.HANDED_OVER) continueTask(state, shown) else say(state.copy(work = Work.IDLE), Reply.NoTaskToContinue, shown)
        Request.Name -> askForTask(state, shown)
        Request.WakeUp -> changeMode(state.copy(work = Work.IDLE), Mode.LISTENING, shown)
        is Request.Stop -> if (state.taskExists && Normalizer.words(text).any { it in STOP_WORDS }) cancelTask(state, shown) else Step(state.copy(work = Work.IDLE), listOf(shown))

        Request.TurnOff -> turnOff(state, shown)
```

```kotlin
    private fun whileHandedOver(state: State, request: Request, text: String, shown: Effect, spokeAt: Long?): Step = when (request) {

        is Request.Task ->

            } else {
                Step(state, listOf(shown, Effect.Show(Feedback.FinishHandOverFirst)))
            }
        else -> whileIdle(state, request, text, shown, spokeAt)
    }
```

```kotlin
    }

    // The wait starts again when "Yes?" or a task's question has been spoken, so that the owner has all of it to start
    // the answer.
    private fun speechEnded(state: State): Step {
        val ended = state.copy(speeches = maxOf(0, state.speeches - 1))
        return when {
            state.speeches == 1 && state.work == Work.AWAITING_TASK -> waitForTask(ended)
            state.speeches == 1 && state.taskAsking != null -> waitForAnswer(ended)
            else -> Step(ended)
        }
    }

    // A cancelled task still reports what it had already done, unless a newer task or wait has started (sections 14.1
    // and 14.5). A task's report counts in every phase (design D2 of sub-project 5).
    private fun taskEnded(state: State, event: Event.TaskEnded): Step {
        if (event.task != state.task || !(state.taskExists || state.cancelled)) return Step(state)
        val ended = state.copy(
            work = if (state.work == Work.RUNNING_TASK) Work.IDLE else state.work,
            cancelled = false,
            taskPhase = null,
            taskAsking = null,
            voiceAnswers = true,
        )
        return if (event.reply == null) Step(ended) else say(ended, Reply.Text(event.reply))
    }

    private fun ownTask(state: State, task: Int): Boolean = task == state.task && state.taskExists

    // Design D2 of sub-project 5: the task asks one question at a time while it runs. The question stays on the bar until
    // the task's owner port releases it; the wait for the answer starts now and again when it has been spoken.
    private fun taskAsks(state: State, event: Event.TaskAsks): Step {
        if (event.task != state.task || state.work != Work.RUNNING_TASK || state.taskAsking != null) return Step(state)
        return say(
            state.copy(taskAsking = event.kind, voiceAnswers = event.voice),
            Reply.Text(event.question),
            Effect.Show(Feedback.TaskText(event.question, keep = true)),
        ).then { waitForAnswer(it) }
    }

    // Design D15 of sub-project 5: the owner does the step by hand. Kestrel stops acting, the bar keeps the sentence, the
    // instant commands work, the touch watcher cancels nothing, and 3 minutes without "Kestrel, continue" or "cancel"
    // end the task with its report (section 12.4).
    private fun handOver(state: State, event: Event.TaskHandsOver): Step {
        if (event.task != state.task || state.work != Work.RUNNING_TASK) return Step(state)
        val handed = state.copy(
            work = Work.IDLE,
            taskPhase = TaskPhase.HANDED_OVER,
            taskAsking = null,
            voiceAnswers = true,
            handOver = state.handOver + 1,
        )
        return say(handed, Reply.Text(event.text), Effect.Show(Feedback.TaskText(event.text, keep = true)))
            .then { Step(it, listOf(Effect.TimeHandOver)) }
    }

    // The task acts again: after a hand-over that ended by itself it runs, and a question that the card answered is over.
    private fun taskBusy(state: State, task: Int): Step = when {
        task != state.task -> Step(state)
        state.taskPhase == TaskPhase.HANDED_OVER -> Step(state.copy(work = Work.RUNNING_TASK, taskPhase = TaskPhase.RUNNING))
        state.taskAsking != null -> Step(state.copy(taskAsking = null, voiceAnswers = true))
        else -> Step(state)
    }

    // "Kestrel, continue" gives the step back to the task, which observes the screen again (design D15 of sub-project 5).
    private fun continueTask(state: State, vararg first: Effect): Step = Step(
        state.copy(work = Work.RUNNING_TASK, taskPhase = TaskPhase.RUNNING),
        first.toList() + Effect.ContinueTask(state.task),
    )

    // The bar shows "Yes?" at the start of the wait, also when "Yes?" cannot be spoken (section 8.9).
```

```kotlin
package dev.kestrel.app.orchestrator

import dev.kestrel.commands.SpokenNumbers
import dev.kestrel.commands.text.Normalizer

/**
 * The answers that a task's question takes (design D2 of sub-project 5), read on Normalizer's words, so that "Confirm."
 * counts like "confirm" and "Kestrel, continue" like "continue". A confirmation goes ahead on "confirm", "yes" or "send
 * it"; a yes-or-no question and "Continue the task?" take "yes", "continue" or "go on"; both take "no". The polite words
 * and the name may come with them. A free question takes any words, and a number question a number. Anything else is no
 * answer, and the question goes on.
 */
internal object TaskAnswers {
    const val YES = "yes"
    const val NO = "no"

    private val FILLERS = setOf("please", "now", "ok", "okay", "thanks", "thank", "you", "oh", "well")
    private val CONFIRM = setOf("confirm", "yes", "send it")
    private val GO_ON = setOf("yes", "continue", "go on")

    /** The answer to a question of [kind] in the transcript [text], or null when it gives none. */
    fun read(kind: TaskAsk, text: String, named: Boolean, request: Request): String? = when (kind) {
        TaskAsk.CONFIRM -> yesOrNo(text, named, CONFIRM)
        TaskAsk.YES_NO, TaskAsk.CONTINUE -> yesOrNo(text, named, GO_ON)
        TaskAsk.PICK_NUMBER -> text.trim().takeIf { SpokenNumbers.answer(it) != null }
        TaskAsk.FREE -> when (request) {
            is Request.Task -> request.text
            is Request.Other -> request.text
            else -> text.trim()
        }.takeIf { it.isNotEmpty() }
    }

    private fun yesOrNo(text: String, named: Boolean, yes: Set<String>): String? {
        val phrase = Normalizer.words(text).filter { it !in FILLERS && Requests.read(it, named) != Request.Name }.joinToString(" ")
        return when (phrase) {
            in yes -> YES
            NO -> NO
            else -> null
        }
    }
}
```

- Consumes: Task 10's phases and events; `CallApi`; `ListeningTexts`; `Listening.steerTask`.
- Produces: `enum class PauseCause { LOCK, INCOMING_CALL, OUTGOING_CALL }`; `State.pause`, `continueAsked`, `touchesArmed`, `pauseExpired`, `heldReport`, `offAfterTask`, `deleteAsking`; events `PauseExpired(pause)`, `TouchesArmed(question)`, `HistoryDeleted(deleted)`; effects `PauseTask(task, cause)`, `ResumeTask(task)`, `TimePause`, `ArmTouches`, `ExpirePause(task)`, `DeleteHistory`, `RunMemoryTask(task, request)`; `Reply.ContinueQuestion`, `DeleteHistoryQuestion`, `HistoryDeleted(deleted)`; `Feedback.ContinueQuestion`, `AnswerContinueFirst`; `Request.DeleteHistory`, `sealed interface Request.Memory { Remember(key, value), Forget(key), SaveRoutine(name) }`; `Orchestrator(pauseMillis = PAUSE_MILLIS, armMillis = ARM_MILLIS)` (30 minutes, 1 s); `Listening.runMemory: (task: Int, request: Request.Memory) -> Unit`; `internal class CallBackstop(calls: CallApi, clock: () -> Long) { enum class Verdict { PAUSE, STOP }; fun acted(); fun forget(); fun onPause(cause): Verdict; WINDOW_MILLIS = 5_000 }`.

Design D2 and D13; deferred items 3 and 41 (D32). A call or the lock pauses a running task instead of cancelling it (spec 8.7 and 14.4 change): `PauseTask` withdraws an open question and closes the agent's gate, the 30-minute timer runs, and when the call ends with the screen unlocked, or the owner unlocks, Kestrel asks "Continue the task?". Its answer counts like a yes-or-no answer, and a touch counts as "no" only 1 s after the question began (`ArmTouches`), because the unlock's own touches come just before. A pause that ran out cancels the task, and its report is held until the screen is on and no call runs; with "Stay off" on wake-up, Kestrel applies it only after the question or that report. A hand-over is not paused. "Kestrel, delete history" asks "Delete the activity log and the network log? Say yes or no." and only "yes" gives `DeleteHistory`; it is ignored while a task exists. "Kestrel, remember that <key> is <value>", "Kestrel, forget <key>" and "Kestrel, save that as <name>" are read on the phone and run as Kestrel's own memory task (`RunMemoryTask`), which Task 12 runs; "Kestrel, remember to buy milk" stays a task. `CallBackstop` (D13; review B3-I1): a call that became active without ringing within 5 s after the agent's last action stops the task at once and, with the permission for calls, Kestrel ends that call; a call that rang only pauses the task, and a call that the owner places during a hand-over reaches no backstop.

Counts: `:app` JVM N + 22 (`RulesTest` + 15, `RequestsTest` + 1, `OrchestratorTest` + 1, `CallBackstopTest` 5); the rest unchanged.

```kotlin
package dev.kestrel.app.agent

import dev.kestrel.app.listen.CallApi
import dev.kestrel.app.orchestrator.CallState
import dev.kestrel.app.orchestrator.Effect
import dev.kestrel.app.orchestrator.Event
import dev.kestrel.app.orchestrator.Mode
import dev.kestrel.app.orchestrator.PauseCause
import dev.kestrel.app.orchestrator.Rules
import dev.kestrel.app.orchestrator.State
import dev.kestrel.app.orchestrator.TaskPhase
import dev.kestrel.app.orchestrator.Work
import org.junit.Assert.assertEquals
import org.junit.Assert.assertFalse
import org.junit.Test

class CallBackstopTest {
    private var now = 0L
    private val calls = FakeCalls()
    private val backstop = CallBackstop(calls) { now }
    private val running = State(mode = Mode.LISTENING, work = Work.RUNNING_TASK, task = 1, taskPhase = TaskPhase.RUNNING)

    private fun pauseOf(state: State, call: CallState): PauseCause? =
        Rules.next(state, Event.CallState(call)).effects.filterIsInstance<Effect.PauseTask>().singleOrNull()?.cause

    @Test
    fun anIncomingCallOneSecondAfterAnActionOnlyPausesTheTask() {
        backstop.acted()
        now = 1_000

        val cause = pauseOf(running, CallState.RINGING)

        assertEquals(PauseCause.INCOMING_CALL, cause)
        assertEquals(CallBackstop.Verdict.PAUSE, backstop.onPause(cause!!))
        assertEquals(0, calls.ended)
    }

    @Test
    fun anOutgoingCallOneSecondAfterAnActionStopsTheTaskAndEndsTheCall() {
        backstop.acted()
        now = 1_000

        val cause = pauseOf(running, CallState.ACTIVE)

        assertEquals(PauseCause.OUTGOING_CALL, cause)
        assertEquals(CallBackstop.Verdict.STOP, backstop.onPause(cause!!))
        assertEquals(1, calls.ended)
    }

    @Test
    fun anOutgoingCallLongAfterTheLastActionOrWithoutThePermissionDoesNotEndTheCall() {
        backstop.acted()
        now = 6_000
        assertEquals(CallBackstop.Verdict.PAUSE, backstop.onPause(PauseCause.OUTGOING_CALL))

        calls.allowed = false
        now = 7_000
        backstop.acted()
        assertEquals(CallBackstop.Verdict.STOP, backstop.onPause(PauseCause.OUTGOING_CALL))
        assertEquals(0, calls.ended)
    }

    @Test
    fun aCallThatTheOwnerPlacesDuringAHandOverIsLeftAlone() {
        backstop.acted()
        val handedOver = Rules.next(running, Event.TaskHandsOver(1, "Tap Call yourself if you want this call.")).state
        now = 1_000

        val step = Rules.next(handedOver, Event.CallState(CallState.ACTIVE))

        assertFalse(step.effects.any { it is Effect.PauseTask || it == Effect.CancelTask })
        assertEquals(TaskPhase.HANDED_OVER, step.state.taskPhase)
        assertEquals(0, calls.ended)
    }

    @Test
    fun anActionOfAnEarlierTaskNeverCounts() {
        backstop.acted()
        backstop.forget()
        now = 1_000

        assertEquals(CallBackstop.Verdict.PAUSE, backstop.onPause(PauseCause.OUTGOING_CALL))
    }

    private class FakeCalls : CallApi {
        var allowed = true
        var ended = 0

        override fun allowed(): Boolean = allowed

        override fun answer() = Unit

        override fun end(): Boolean {
            ended++
            return true
        }

        override fun active(): Boolean = false

        override fun showInCallScreen() = Unit
    }
}
```
